| dvpn program | `J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs` | upgradeable program, last deploy slot 517924537 |
| token mint | `Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa` (**Token-2022**, 6 decimals: 1 tDVPN = 1 000 000 base units) | `Config.mint`, `Config.decimals` |
| token program | `TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb` | pinned by the program (`address = token_2022::ID`) |
| Config PDA | `Cu5vofxVQgZXRVwfBqApw84ZWy1hjhDmHkznyDr6TRiQ` (seeds `["config"]`) | decoded live |
| vault | `EQJyAyWLGZSye3BMfDQVdhrfp1QKEByNX9q2J9TzFmfy` = the Token-2022 ATA of the Config PDA | `Config.vault` |
| `fee_bps` | 200 (2 % of every redemption goes to fees) | `Config` |
| `channel_close_grace_seconds` | **7200** (2 h) | `Config` |
| `node_listing_ttl_seconds` | 86400 (a node must re-list every 24 h to stay live) | `Config` |
| `paused_mask` | 0 (nothing paused) | `Config` |

**The IDL file carries a placeholder address** (`SentineLDVPN1111111111111111111111111111111`).
The same goes for the generated Go client's `dvpn.ProgramID`. The real id is chosen when you build.
Set it yourself: in TS, override `idl.address`; in Go, call `dvpn.SetProgramID(...)`.

**Is devnet running this source?** Yes, as far as anything outside the binary can show. Every
account type's on-chain size matches the 26de5240 layout: Channel 299 B, User 117 B, Config 277 B,
Node 337 B, Grant 201 B, Lease 331 B, Subscription 198 B, Plan 155 B, Provider 313 B, both Unbonding
153 B. The program also returns error **6049 `MissingRentRecipient`**, which only exists in the
newest error table. An `open_channel` encoded from this IDL was accepted, and a real one was sent.

## 2. The pieces

```
your code ──(Solana tx)──▶ dvpn program   escrow, vouchers, settlement, refunds
    │
    └──(gRPC, local socket)──▶ sentinel-dvpnd ──(HTTPS node API)──▶ node   the tunnel itself
```

The chain never sees traffic. It holds your escrow and lets the node redeem the **vouchers** you
sign as you use bandwidth. You can do all the chain work yourself. For the tunnel, either let the
daemon run the session (section 6), or implement the node API
([`sentinel-go-sdk/nodeapi/openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/sentinel-official/sentinel-solana/blob/26de52407c5b722cfecad1772dcbeefd984ef6d0/sentinel-go-sdk/nodeapi/openapi.yaml)).

## 3. Accounts and PDA seeds (client side)

All PDAs belong to the dvpn program. Seeds are the raw UTF-8 string, then the 32 raw bytes of each key.

| account | seeds | size | holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `"config"` | 277 | mint, vault, fees, grace windows, pause mask |
| `User` | `"user"`, owner | 117 | `owner`, `balance` (refunds land here), `open_channels`, `rent_recipient` |
| `Node` | `"node"`, node.owner, node.node_id (32 B) | 337 | `status` (1 = listed), `listed_at`, `channel_price_per_gb`, `channel_price_per_hour`, `uri`, `country`, `opened_at` |
| `Channel` | `"channel"`, owner, channel_id (32 B, you choose it) | 299 | `owner`, `node`, `opener`, `mode` (0 voucher / 1 stream), `voucher_signer`, `escrow`, `redeemed`, `opened_at`, `close_started_at`, `status` (0 open / 1 closing), `rent_recipient`, `node_opened_at` |
| `Grant` | `"grant"`, granter (owner), grantee, target | 201 | `permissions` bitmask, `expires_at` (0 = never), `allowance` (u64::MAX = unlimited), `rent_recipient` |
| vault | ATA of `Config` (`[config, token_program, mint]` under the ATA program) | — | all escrowed tokens |

A node is **usable** only when `status == 1` **and** `now < listed_at + node_listing_ttl_seconds`.
Otherwise `open_channel` fails with 6015 or 6016. On 2026-11-20, 36 of 79 Node accounts were live.

**Optional accounts:** Anchor encodes "None" for an optional account (the `grant` everywhere, and
`node` in `close_channel`) by passing **the program id itself** in that slot. The generated Go
builders do this for you when `Grant` is `nil`.

## 4. The client flow, instruction by instruction

Every instruction is **owner-or-grantee**. If no grant is passed, `signer` must equal `owner`
(otherwise 6000). With a grant, the signer must be the grantee, the grant must hold the permission
bit (6046), it must not be expired (6045), and its `target` must be `111…1` (any) or the
node/channel the call touches (6047). Accounts are listed in IDL order. **w** = writable, **s** = signer.

### Step 0: prerequisites (not dvpn instructions)

- A Solana wallet with SOL for fees and rent. Each tx costs a 5 000-lamport fee. A first channel
  open also pays the User and Channel rent (section 8).
- A **Token-2022** associated token account for the mint holding tDVPN (`owner_token`). Plain SPL
  Token accounts are rejected (Anchor `token::mint` / `token::authority` constraints).

### Step 1: User account (no instruction of its own)

There is **no `open_user`**. `open_channel` creates `User` (`init_if_needed`) the first time an
owner opens a channel. It stores `user_rent_recipient` then. `withdraw_user_balance` closes it once
`open_channels == 0`.

### Step 2 (optional): delegate with a grant: `open_grant` / `update_grant` / `close_grant`

Use this when a different key (an agent's hot key, or the daemon's operator key) should spend for the owner.

`open_grant(grantee: pubkey, target: pubkey, permissions: u64, expires_at: i64, allowance: u64, grant_rent_recipient: pubkey)`

| # | account | flags | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `granter` | s | the owner |
| 2 | `rent_payer` | w s | pays the Grant rent |
| 3 | `grant` | w | PDA `["grant", granter, grantee, target]` |
| 4 | `system_program` | | |

Errors: **6003** `ParamOutOfRange` (grantee is `111…1` or the granter itself, unknown permission
bits, or `expires_at` not 0 and not in the future), **6049/6050** (rent recipient, section 8).

Client permission bits (IDL `constants`):

| bit | value |
|---|---|
| `PERM_OPEN_CHANNEL` | 16777216 (`0x1000000`) |
| `PERM_FUND_CHANNELS` | 33554432 (`0x2000000`) |
| `PERM_START_CLOSE_CHANNEL` | 67108864 (`0x4000000`) |
| `PERM_CLOSE_CHANNEL` | 134217728 (`0x8000000`) |
| `PERM_WITHDRAW_USER_BALANCE` | 268435456 (`0x10000000`) |
| `PERM_OPEN_SUBSCRIPTION` | 536870912 (`0x20000000`) |

The Go SDK's `program.PermsClient` = open | fund | start-close | close channel + open
subscription. It leaves out withdraw, so a delegate cannot pull your refunds out to your wallet.
`allowance` is charged by the escrow amount on every `open_channel` / `fund_channels`; going past
it gives **6024** `AmountExceedsAllowance`.

- `update_grant(permissions: Option<u64>, expires_at: Option<i64>, allowance: Option<u64>)`:
  accounts `signer` (s, must be the granter, else 6000), `grant` (w). Errors 6000, 6003.
- `close_grant()`: accounts `signer` (s), `grant` (w), `rent_recipient` (w, must equal
  `grant.rent_recipient`). The granter or grantee may close it, or anyone once it has expired (else
  6000). The rent goes to the stored rent recipient.

### Step 3: open a channel: `open_channel`

`open_channel(channel_id: [u8;32], escrow: u64, terms: PositionTerms, channel_rent_recipient: pubkey, user_rent_recipient: pubkey)`

`PositionTerms` is an enum:
- `Voucher { voucher_signer: pubkey }` (mode 0). Pay per use: the node redeems vouchers signed by
  `voucher_signer`. The key must be a valid prime-order ed25519 point (6048); any normal wallet key is.
- `Stream { expected_rate_per_hour: u64 }` (mode 1). Pay per time. The value must equal the node's
  current `channel_price_per_hour` (6017), so a price change between read and send is caught.

| # | account | flags | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `signer` | w s | owner, or a grantee holding `PERM_OPEN_CHANNEL` |
| 2 | `config` | | `["config"]` |
| 3 | `owner` | | the wallet the channel belongs to |
| 4 | `grant` | w, optional | `["grant", owner, signer, target]`; program id = None |
| 5 | `user` | w | `["user", owner]`, created if missing |
| 6 | `node` | | `["node", node.owner, node.node_id]` |
| 7 | `channel` | w | `["channel", owner, channel_id]`, created |
| 8 | `vault` | w | `Config.vault` |
| 9 | `mint` | | `Config.mint` |
| 10 | `owner_token` | w | owner's Token-2022 account for the mint |
| 11 | `token_program` | | Token-2022 |
| 12 | `rent_payer` | w s | pays User + Channel rent |
| 13 | `system_program` | | |

Money: the escrow is taken **from `User.balance` first** (old refunds), then the rest from
`owner_token`. Errors: **6001** (channel opens paused), **6015** `NodeNotListed`, **6016**
`NodeNotLive`, **6017** `NodePriceChanged` (stream), **6000/6045/6046/6047** (grant gate),
**6024** (allowance), **6048** `InvalidVoucherSigner`, **6049/6050** (rent recipient), **6043**
(overflow). Opening with a `channel_id` already used for this owner fails in the System program
("already in use").

The program does **not** check the escrow against the node's price. A tiny escrow opens fine, but
the node or daemon may refuse to serve it (section 6).

### Step 4 (optional): top up: `fund_channels`

`fund_channels(amounts: Vec<u64>)`. Accounts: `signer` (w s), `config`, `owner`, `user` (w),
`grant` (w, optional, needs `PERM_FUND_CHANNELS`), `vault` (w), `mint`, `owner_token` (w),
`token_program`. **Remaining accounts:** the channels to fund, writable, **sorted ascending by
pubkey bytes with no duplicates** (6041 `BatchNotSorted`). There must be exactly one amount per
channel and at least one (6040 `BatchLengthMismatch`). Each channel must be `owner`'s (Anchor 2001)
and open (6032 `ChannelNotOpen`). Like open, this draws from `User.balance` first, then the wallet.

### Step 5: start a session (through the daemon)

See section 6. Your channel must be voucher-signable by the daemon. Either let the daemon open the
channel itself (`NewChannel`), or open it with `voucher_signer` = the daemon's operator key and pass
its address.

### Step 6: vouchers (what the node redeems)

A voucher is `{ cumulative_amount: u64, signature: [u8;64] }`. It is an **ed25519 signature by
`channel.voucher_signer`** over an 80-byte message:

```
bytes  0..32  domain   = sha256("sentinel-dvpn/channel-voucher/v1")
              = 0a34aa1e233037f6558a364baf39c430236bdfc99943bdeec1bae0ee7222b354
bytes 32..64  channel PDA (32 bytes)
bytes 64..72  channel.opened_at  (i64, little-endian)
bytes 72..80  cumulative_amount  (u64, little-endian)
```

`cumulative_amount` is the **running total** owed for the whole channel, not a delta. The node calls
`redeem_channel_vouchers(vouchers)` (accounts `signer`, `config`, `node` (w); remaining accounts =
the channels, sorted). It is paid `cumulative − redeemed` minus `fee_bps`. Rules a client can rely on:

- A voucher above `channel.escrow` is rejected (**6034** `VoucherExceedsEscrow`). The node can never
  take more than you escrowed.
- A voucher at or below `channel.redeemed` is skipped. Replaying an old voucher pays nothing. If
  nothing new is redeemable the call fails with 6036.
- `opened_at` is in the message, so a voucher cannot be replayed on a later channel at the same PDA.
  `channel.node_opened_at` must match `node.opened_at`, so a node that was closed and reopened cannot
  redeem old channels (6042).
- A bad signature gives 6039. Only sign what you have actually used. With the daemon, it signs for you.

### Step 7: get your money back: `start_close_channel` → wait → `close_channel` → `withdraw_user_balance`

**`start_close_channel()`** (voucher mode only). Accounts: `signer` (s, owner or grantee with `PERM_START_CLOSE_CHANNEL`), `config`, `channel` (w),
`grant` (optional). Sets `status = 1` (closing) and `close_started_at = now`. Errors: **6037**
`ModeNotVoucher` (it is a stream channel; close it directly), **6032** `ChannelNotOpen`, and the
grant gate. During the grace the node can still redeem vouchers you already signed. That is the
point of the wait.

**Wait `Config.channel_close_grace_seconds`, 7200 s (2 h) on devnet.** The deadline is
`close_started_at + 7200`, inclusive.

**`close_channel()`.** Accounts: `signer` (s), `config`, `channel` (w; closed), `user` (w,
`["user", channel.owner]`), `grant` (optional), `node` (w, optional: **required for stream**,
None for voucher), `rent_recipient` (w, must equal `channel.rent_recipient`, Anchor 2012
otherwise).
- Voucher mode: must be closing (**6033** `ChannelNotClosing`) and past the grace (**6035**
  `GraceNotElapsed`). There is **no signer check** in voucher mode: once the grace is over, **anyone**
  can pay the fee to close it. The refund still goes only to the owner's `User.balance`.
- Stream mode: owner or grantee with `PERM_CLOSE_CHANNEL`. It settles what accrued so far to the
  node and closes at once, with no grace. If the node account is gone or was reopened, the accrued
  part is forfeited (not paid to anyone) and the rest is refunded.
- Effect: `User.balance += escrow − redeemed`, `User.open_channels −= 1`, Channel rent goes to
  `channel.rent_recipient`.

**`withdraw_user_balance()`** has no args and withdraws the **whole** balance. Accounts: `signer`
(s, owner or grantee with `PERM_WITHDRAW_USER_BALANCE`), `config`, `owner`, `grant` (optional),
`user` (w), `rent_recipient` (w, must equal `user.rent_recipient`), `owner_token` (w), `vault` (w),
`mint`, `token_program`. It sends `User.balance` from the vault to `owner_token`. If
`open_channels == 0` it also **closes the User account** and sends its rent to
`user.rent_recipient`. It fails with **6023** `BalanceZero` only when the balance is 0 *and*
channels are still open. With 0 balance and no open channels it just closes the account.

`close_channel` + `withdraw_user_balance` fit in one transaction. `close-channel.ts finish` does that.

## 5. Reading state (what to poll)

- `Config`: fetch once and cache `vault`, `mint`, `decimals` and the grace windows.
- Live nodes: `getProgramAccounts(program, memcmp offset 0 = Node discriminator)`, then keep those
  with `status == 1 && now < listed_at + ttl`. Discriminators are in the IDL (`accounts[].discriminator`).
  The Go client has `dvpn.NodeFilter()` and `program.Live()`.
- Your channels: memcmp on the Channel discriminator, plus `owner` at byte offset 40 (8-byte
  discriminator + 32-byte `channel_id`).
- Your refunds: `User.balance` at PDA `["user", owner]`.

## 6. Running the session with `sentinel-dvpnd` (`ClientService` gRPC)

The daemon listens on a **local** endpoint, not TCP
([`daemon/instance/instance.go`](https://github.com/sentinel-official/sentinel-solana/blob/26de52407c5b722cfecad1772dcbeefd984ef6d0/sentinel-go-sdk/daemon/instance/instance.go)):
Linux `/var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/<tag>/daemon.sock`, macOS
`/Library/Application Support/sentinel-dvpn/<tag>/daemon.sock`, Windows
`\\.\pipe\ProtectedPrefix\Administrators\sentinel-dvpn\<tag>` (`<tag>` is the instance name, e.g.
`client`). `DaemonService.GetVersion` returns the `network`, `program_id` and `mint` it was built
for. Check them against section 1 before you trust it.

`service ClientService` (package `sentinel.daemon.v1`):

| rpc | request → response |
|---|---|
| `StartSession` | `{ node, credential, terms }` → `{ session }` |
| `StopSession` | `{ id }` → `{ session, kill_switch_released, dns_revert_failed }` |
| `GetSession` / `WatchSession` (server stream) | `{ id }` → `{ session }` |
| `ListSessions` / `ListChannels` / `ListTickets` | `{}` → lists |

`Credential` is a `oneof`:
- `channel: "<channel address>"`: use a channel you opened yourself.
- `new_channel: { mode, escrow }`: the daemon opens one. **`escrow = 0` means the daemon's
  `escrow_base_units` default, 1 000 000 000 base units = 1 000 tDVPN.** Always set it.
- `ticket_request` / `ticket_hash`: the subscription path (not covered here).

`Terms { basis, price, prepay }` mirror the node's listed price.

What the daemon enforces (`sentinel-dvpnd/internal/client/`):
- The daemon signs vouchers with its **operator key** (`client.key`). For an existing voucher
  channel, that key must equal `channel.voucher_signer`, or the session fails with *"the operator
  key is not the voucher signer of this channel"*. Open your channel with
  `voucher_signer = <daemon operator pubkey>`.
- `client.owner` is the wallet that owns the channels. If the operator key is not the owner, the
  daemon looks up a **Grant** from owner to operator covering the call. Create it in step 2 with
  `program.PermsClient` bits.
- For `new_channel` in voucher mode it refuses an escrow under half the node's minimum prepay block
  (*"channel escrow below node minimum: fund or close the channel"*). Check this before you spend.

## 7. Two-hour close, as a timeline

```
t0           start_close_channel   status=closing; node may still redeem signed vouchers
t0 … t0+7199 close_channel         → 6035 GraceNotElapsed (simulated live, see §10)
t0+7200 …    close_channel         anyone may send it; refund → User.balance; Channel rent → channel.rent_recipient
any time     withdraw_user_balance  User.balance → owner_token; closes User when open_channels == 0
```

Stream channels skip the wait: `close_channel` directly (`start_close_channel` → 6037).

## 8. Rent rules

1. **Who gets rent back.** Every account the client creates stores a `rent_recipient`: the Channel
   (`channel_rent_recipient`), the User (`user_rent_recipient`) and the Grant
   (`grant_rent_recipient`). When that account closes, its lamports go **to that stored address**,
   checked by `address = …rent_recipient`, so pass exactly that account.
2. **What you may pass.** At open time each rent recipient must be **the signer or the
   `rent_payer`** (6050 `InvalidRentRecipient`) and must not be `111…1` (6049
   `MissingRentRecipient`). So the rent can only go back to whoever paid it or whoever signed. A
   relayer that pays rent can name itself.
3. **How much.** The rent is the rent-exempt minimum for the account size. Measured on devnet on
   2026-11-20 (`getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption`): User 117 B = **1 244 600** lamports, Channel
   299 B = **2 169 160**, Grant 201 B = 1 671 320. The open in §10 moved exactly 1 244 600 + 2 169 160
   + 5 000 fee lamports out of the wallet.
4. **The 0-or-rent-exempt rule (Solana runtime, not dvpn).** After any transaction, a plain wallet
   account must hold either **0 lamports or at least the rent-exempt minimum for 0 bytes**. Otherwise
   the transaction fails (`InsufficientFundsForRent`). So never drain a fee payer to a few lamports,
   and do not send dust to a fresh address. **Query the minimum, do not hard-code it:** on devnet on
   2026-11-20 `getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption(0)` returned **650 240**, not the 890 880 often quoted
   (890 880 is the classic `3480 lamports/byte-year × 2 years × 128 bytes` figure).

## 9. Program errors

A Solana transaction is atomic, so **a failed transaction moves no tokens and creates or closes no
account**. You still pay the 5 000-lamport fee if you *sent* it; a simulation costs nothing. That is
why every row's "money moved?" is "No". Read the number from the log line `Error Number: N`, from
`custom program error: 0x…`, or from `{"Custom": N}`. On devnet on 2026-11-20 these were produced
live: 6033, 6035 and 6049 (§10).

**Decode it in code:** [`ts/errors.ts`](build-your-own-client/ts/errors.ts) turns a failed
simulation or send into exactly one row of this table, `{ code, name, meaning, moneyMoved, fix }`.
`open-channel.ts` and `close-channel.ts` print it on every failure.
[`ts/explain-failure.ts`](build-your-own-client/ts/explain-failure.ts) shows it with no key at all:
it simulates `close_channel` on a live voucher channel still in its grace, unsigned (§10).

**What the table covers:**
- Every IDL error, 6000–6050.
- Every Anchor framework code the client flow can hit. These numbers are from anchor-lang **1.2.2**,
  the version in `sentinel-programs/Cargo.lock`, checked against its `lang/error/src/lib.rs`. They
  are the same 16 codes the Devnet dVPN app decodes.

`meaning` is the IDL `msg`, followed by where the program raises it (source at 26de5240). A row a
channel-only client never hits says "governance only" or names the node or provider instruction.

The table is generated from `errors.ts` and the IDL. Regenerate it with `npx tsx gen-error-table.ts`;
`npx tsx gen-error-table.ts --check BUILD-YOUR-OWN-CLIENT.md` fails when it drifts.

| 6038 | `ModeNotStream` | position mode is not stream: redeem_*_streams on a voucher position | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | use the voucher redeem instead |

| 6041 | `BatchNotSorted` | batch not sorted: batch instructions: accounts not strictly ascending by pubkey bytes | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | sort by pubkey bytes and remove duplicates |
| 6042 | `NodeReopened` | position belongs to an earlier incarnation of this node: redeem / stream settle: the node was closed and reopened after the channel opened | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | close the channel (refund) and open a new one |
| 6043 | `ArithmeticOverflow` | arithmetic overflow: any: a u64 sum or product overflowed | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | use sane amounts (a client bug) |
| 6044 | `VaultFrozen` | vault is frozen: governance: the vault is frozen | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | wait; payments are frozen network-wide |
| 6045 | `GrantExpired` | grant has expired: any delegated instruction: now >= grant.expires_at (not 0) | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | the owner extends it with update_grant |
| 6046 | `PermissionNotGranted` | grant does not include the permission for this action: any delegated instruction: the grant lacks this action’s permission bit | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | the owner adds the bit with update_grant |
| 6047 | `GrantTargetMismatch` | grant target does not cover this account: any delegated instruction: grant.target is not 111…1, the node or the channel | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | use a grant whose target covers the account |
| 6048 | `InvalidVoucherSigner` | voucher signer is not a valid key: open_channel / open_lease (voucher): voucher_signer is not a prime-order ed25519 point | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | use a real ed25519 public key |
| 6049 | `MissingRentRecipient` | rent recipient is missing: open_channel / open_grant (and other opens): a rent recipient argument is 111…1 | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | pass the signer or the rent payer |
| 6050 | `InvalidRentRecipient` | rent recipient is neither the signer nor the rent payer: the same opens: the rent recipient is neither the signer nor the rent payer | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | pass the signer or the rent payer |
| 100 | `InstructionMissing` | no 8-byte instruction discriminator in the data | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | encode the instruction with the IDL |
| 101 | `InstructionFallbackNotFound` | unknown instruction discriminator | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | encode with the IDL of the deployed program |
| 102 | `InstructionDidNotDeserialize` | the args do not match this program version | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | re-encode with the IDL of the deployed program |
| 2000 | `ConstraintMut` | an account that must be writable was passed read-only | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | mark it writable (IDL "writable") |
| 2001 | `ConstraintHasOne` | an account does not belong to the owner it must (e.g. a funded channel of another wallet) | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | pass the owner’s own accounts |
| 2002 | `ConstraintSigner` | an account that must sign did not | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | add its signature (IDL "signer") |
| 2003 | `ConstraintRaw` | a custom account constraint failed | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | check the accounts against the IDL |
| 2006 | `ConstraintSeeds` | a PDA does not match its seeds (also: a grant passed while the owner signs) | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | derive the PDA again; pass no grant when the owner signs |
| 2012 | `ConstraintAddress` | an account is not the one stored on chain (vault, mint, token program, rent recipient) | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | pass Config.vault, Config.mint, Token-2022 and the stored rent_recipient |
| 2014 | `ConstraintTokenMint` | owner_token is for another mint | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | use the owner’s Token-2022 account for Config.mint |
| 2015 | `ConstraintTokenOwner` | owner_token belongs to another wallet | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | use the owner’s Token-2022 account for Config.mint |
| 2019 | `ConstraintSpace` | an account was created with the wrong size | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | a client or program bug: report it |
| 2020 | `ConstraintAccountIsNone` | a required optional account was None (e.g. node on a stream close) | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | pass the account (node on a stream close_channel) |
| 3005 | `AccountDidNotSerialize` | the program could not write an account | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | a program bug: report it |
| 3007 | `AccountOwnedByWrongProgram` | an account is owned by another program (e.g. a plain SPL Token account) | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | pass the dvpn / Token-2022 account the IDL names |
| 3012 | `AccountNotInitialized` | an account the instruction reads does not exist yet (e.g. User before the first channel) | No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing. | open a channel first (it creates the User account) |

## 10. Examples (run on 2026-11-20)

All runs: Azure VM, Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.23.5, Go 1.27.3 (via `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`), public devnet
RPC, a fresh wallet `<your-wallet-address>` funded with 0.05 SOL and 1 tDVPN.

What each run proves, and where:

| Example | Run | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| `ts/read.ts` | live read, no key | the output below (Config, 79 nodes, 36 live) |
| `ts/open-channel.ts` | real `open_channel` + `start_close`, plus three simulated failures (6049, 6033, 6035) | the output below and the explorer links ([open](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/3D3s6MWY6LLxVgT2eNimyLcS8XfYo8kzWa423gK9UiM386NYm7Cc2znKXQSBM5Nrcb3ngfDK8pEuBisvRy3EAV3d?cluster=devnet), [start_close](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/2pdoKkBLEwvc6G2tq9uc12GeKNbCpQ6wEkG4npZox4Z2AfBr4C6zvkrcyiwcf114EUkVKC5jjMc4PMJmUT7VrHtC?cluster=devnet)) |
| `ts/close-channel.ts` | real `close_channel` + `withdraw_user_balance` at 10:52Z, after the grace | [hPKsn1mw…](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/hPKsn1mwMb77EVkGn9mfC8eiVCiK8JS2xapBirAW7N3HDueSQ9ET8SQmT4bnuA1eLHsS4EGvT17PRNUkBsrdSMC?cluster=devnet): the full 0.5 tDVPN escrow back |
| `ts/explain-failure.ts` | live unsigned simulation, no key, second VM | the 6035 output below |
| `go/main.go` | live read + simulated `open_channel` (no transaction sent) | the Go output below (`units=29683`) |

**Checked on every push** (CI, no wallet, no transaction): `go vet` and `go build` of `go/` against the
public repo at `26de5240`, and `ts/gen-error-table.ts --check`, which fails when the §9 error table
drifts from `errors.ts` and the public IDL. The live runs above are not repeated in CI: they need a funded wallet.

### TypeScript (`@solana/web3.js` 1.98.4 + `@coral-xyz/anchor` 0.31.1 coders + the IDL)

Files: [`build-your-own-client/ts/`](build-your-own-client/ts/) (`common.ts`, `errors.ts`, `read.ts`,
`open-channel.ts`, `close-channel.ts`, `explain-failure.ts`, `gen-error-table.ts`, `package.json`). Put `dvpn.json` from the
public repo next to them. All files typecheck with `tsc --strict` (TypeScript 5.9.3).

```bash
npm install
npx tsx read.ts <ownerPubkey>                                   # read
npx tsx explain-failure.ts                                      # decode a failing close_channel; no key, nothing signed
npx tsx open-channel.ts wallet.json <node> 500000 --bad-rent     # prove 6049, sends nothing
npx tsx open-channel.ts wallet.json <node> 500000                # open (sends)
npx tsx close-channel.ts wallet.json <channel> start             # start_close (sends)
npx tsx close-channel.ts wallet.json <channel> finish            # after 2 h: close + withdraw
```

The core of the open, with accounts in IDL order and the optional grant as the program id:

```ts
const data = ixCoder.encode('open_channel', {
  channel_id: [...channelId], escrow: new BN(500000),
  terms: { Voucher: { voucher_signer: owner } },
  channel_rent_recipient: owner, user_rent_recipient: owner,
});
const keys = [signer(owner, w), config, owner, PROGRAM_ID /* grant=None */, userPda(owner) /* w */,
  node, channelPda(owner, channelId) /* w */, config.vault /* w */, MINT, ata(owner) /* w */,
  TOKEN_2022, rentPayer(owner, w s), SystemProgram.programId];
```

Output (trimmed):

```

  mint Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa (matches)
  decimals 6 fee_bps 200 paused_mask 0
```

`explain-failure.ts` (run later the same day on a second Ubuntu VM, no wallet, unsigned simulation):

```
channel <a-closing-channel> (closing, inside its grace) status 1
{
  "code": 6035,
  "name": "GraceNotElapsed",
  "meaning": "grace window not elapsed: close_channel (voucher): less than Config.channel_close_grace_seconds (7200 s) since close_started_at",
  "moneyMoved": "No. A sent transaction still pays its 5000-lamport fee; a simulation pays nothing.",
  "fix": "wait until close_started_at + channel_close_grace_seconds"
}
```

What the open transaction moved: wallet −3 418 760 lamports (User rent 1 244 600 + Channel rent
2 169 160 + fee 5 000); wallet ATA 1 000 000 → 500 000 base units; vault +500 000.
Explorer: [open](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/3D3s6MWY6LLxVgT2eNimyLcS8XfYo8kzWa423gK9UiM386NYm7Cc2znKXQSBM5Nrcb3ngfDK8pEuBisvRy3EAV3d?cluster=devnet),
[start_close](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/2pdoKkBLEwvc6G2tq9uc12GeKNbCpQ6wEkG4npZox4Z2AfBr4C6zvkrcyiwcf114EUkVKC5jjMc4PMJmUT7VrHtC?cluster=devnet).
`finish` ran at 10:52Z, after the grace: one transaction with `close_channel` + `withdraw_user_balance`,
[hPKsn1mw…](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/hPKsn1mwMb77EVkGn9mfC8eiVCiK8JS2xapBirAW7N3HDueSQ9ET8SQmT4bnuA1eLHsS4EGvT17PRNUkBsrdSMC?cluster=devnet).
No vouchers had been redeemed, so the whole 0.5 tDVPN escrow came back to the wallet's token account.
The Channel and User accounts closed (`open_channels` was 0), and their rent went to the wallet,
the stored `rent_recipient`. Afterwards the channel and User addresses read "no account" on the public RPC.

### Go (public SDK `sentinel-go-sdk/program` + generated `clients/go/dvpn`)

Files: [`build-your-own-client/go/`](build-your-own-client/go/) (`main.go`, `go.mod`; `go mod tidy` writes `go.sum`).
`go.mod` points both modules at a clone of the public repo in `../ss`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sentinel-official/sentinel-solana ../ss && git -C ../ss checkout 26de5240
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go mod tidy                                    # fetches deps, writes go.sum
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go run .                                       # read only
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go run . wallet.json <node> 500000             # read + build + SIMULATE open_channel
```

```go
dvpn.SetProgramID(programID)                       // the generated client ships a placeholder id
client := program.NewClient(rpc.New(rpc.DevNet_RPC), programID, mint, rpc.CommitmentConfirmed)
client.CheckMint(ctx)                              // Config.mint must equal the mint you expect
cfg, _ := client.Config(ctx)
nodes, _ := client.FindNodeAccounts(ctx, dvpn.NodeFilter())
// live = Status == dvpn.ListingStatusListed && program.Live(node, cfg, now)
ix, _ := dvpn.BuildOpenChannelInstruction(programID, dvpn.OpenChannelParams{
  ChannelID: id, Escrow: 500000, Terms: &dvpn.PositionTermsVoucher{VoucherSigner: owner},
  ChannelRentRecipient: owner, UserRentRecipient: owner, Signer: owner, Owner: owner,
  Grant: nil, Node: node, Vault: cfg.Vault, Mint: mint, OwnerToken: ata, RentPayer: owner,
})
```

Output:

```
config: mint Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa decimals 6 fee_bps 200 close_grace 7200s listing_ttl 86400s paused_mask 0
  Kg96W7ScKBycWHjDyoTPxeQZTv7ry15P7Ug663rC7yf BR https://163.176.182.147:41000 per_gb=50000000 per_hour=97500000
nodes: 79 accounts, 36 listed and live
open_channel 7WkQr8zsMkHEZsGhL3N37xMxQBtmnh1S3iJUrh6Km31T simulate: err=<nil> units=29683
```

The Go open was **simulated only** (allowed: one real channel open per run, done in TS). The
simulation ran the real program against live accounts and succeeded.

## 11. What was checked, and where sources disagreed

- **Program version.** Older notes said devnet ran an earlier build: errors only up to 6048, an
  `OperatorMandate` account instead of `Grant`, a 3-argument `open_channel`. The live chain
  disagrees. It returned 6049, it accepted the 5-argument 26de5240 `open_channel`, and every account
  size matches 26de5240. **This doc follows the live chain = 26de5240.**
- **Close wait.** "2 h" is not a program constant. It is `Config.channel_close_grace_seconds`, read
  live as 7200. Read it from Config; governance can change it with `set_params`.
- **"Rent goes back to the rent payer."** Not exactly. It goes to the stored `rent_recipient`,
  which at open time must be **the signer or the rent payer**. In the common case (one wallet signs
  and pays) that is the same key.
- **"0 or ≥ 890 880 lamports."** The rule is real (Solana runtime), but the number is not fixed. On
  devnet on 2026-11-20 the 0-byte minimum was **650 240** lamports. Query
  `getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption(0)`.
- **Daemon escrow default** is 1 000 tDVPN (`escrow_base_units = 1000000000`) when
  `NewChannel.escrow` is 0 (`sentinel-dvpnd/internal/config/client.go`).
- **Not run here:** the daemon (`StartSession`), node redemption, `fund_channels`, grants, stream
  mode. Their accounts, args and errors above come from
  the IDL and program source at 26de5240 only.

# file: direct/install.sh

#!/bin/sh
# ─── direct/install.sh: install Sentinel's own client tools for Solana devnet (Linux, no app) ───
#
#   sudo sh direct/install.sh       # from your normal user; creates your owner key if you have none
#
# What it does, in order (each command is printed before it runs; safe to run again):
#   1. checks it runs as root and finds the user who called sudo
#   2. apt-get installs wireguard-tools, jq, curl
#   3. puts sentinel-dvpnd + sentinel-dvpn in /usr/local/bin: from the release direct-v1, checked
#      against SHA256SUMS; or BUILD=1 builds them from the public source with direct/build.sh
#   4. sentinel-dvpnd init --instance c1 (client role, public devnet RPC). This creates the DEVICE
#      key: a second key that signs and pays fees for the daemon. Your owner key never enters the daemon
#   5. sets kill_switch = 'off' (see "Remote box" in docs/DIRECT.md: the upstream default 'on'
#      drops all outbound traffic except the tunnel, which cuts SSH). KILL_SWITCH=on keeps it on
#   6. registers and starts the systemd service sentinel-dvpnd@c1 (FOREGROUND=1: skip, run it yourself)
#   7. adds the calling user to the sentinel-dvpn group, so the CLI can reach the daemon socket
#
# Env: OWNER=<base58> (default: the calling user's "owner" key), BUILD=1, KILL_SWITCH=on, FOREGROUND=1
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
. "$HERE/lib.sh"
STEP=install
parse_args "$@"

RELEASE_URL=${RELEASE_URL:-https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet/releases/download/direct-v1}

[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail "$E_USAGE" needs-root "run as root" "sudo sh direct/install.sh"
CALLER=${SUDO_USER:-}

# ─── 1. packages ───
if ! command -v wg >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  step "$E_NETWORK" download-failed "sleep 60 && sudo sh direct/install.sh" none apt-get update -qq
  step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo apt-get install -y wireguard-tools jq curl && sudo sh direct/install.sh" none env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq wireguard-tools jq curl
fi

# ─── 2. binaries ───
case $(uname -m) in
  x86_64) ARCH=amd64 ;;
  aarch64|arm64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
  *) fail "$E_OTHER" unsupported "unsupported CPU $(uname -m)" "grep -n Needs docs/DIRECT.md" ;;
esac
if [ "${BUILD:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  [ -n "$CALLER" ] || fail "$E_USAGE" usage "BUILD=1 needs sudo from a normal user" "sudo BUILD=1 sh direct/install.sh"
  brc=0; run sudo -u "$CALLER" env PATH="$PATH" ARCHES="$ARCH" sh "$HERE/build.sh" >&2 || brc=$?
  case $brc in
    0) ;;
    5) fail "$E_SAFETY" checksum-mismatch "your build's SHA-256 differs from direct/SHA256SUMS with Go 1.27.3; not installed" "sh direct/build.sh" none ;;
    *) fail "$E_OTHER" build-failed "direct/build.sh failed (exit $brc): git, make and Go 1.27.3 are needed" "sh direct/build.sh" none ;;
  esac
  for tool in sentinel-dvpnd sentinel-dvpn; do
    step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo sh direct/install.sh" none install -m 0755 "./dist-build/$tool-linux-$ARCH" "/usr/local/bin/$tool"
  done
else
  TMP=$(mktemp -d)
  step "$E_NETWORK" download-failed "sleep 60 && sudo sh direct/install.sh" none curl -fsSL -o "$TMP/SHA256SUMS" "$RELEASE_URL/SHA256SUMS"
  for tool in sentinel-dvpnd sentinel-dvpn; do
    step "$E_NETWORK" download-failed "sleep 60 && sudo sh direct/install.sh" none curl -fsSL -o "$TMP/$tool-linux-$ARCH" "$RELEASE_URL/$tool-linux-$ARCH"
  done
  (cd "$TMP" && run sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS) || fail "$E_SAFETY" checksum-mismatch "SHA-256 mismatch on the downloaded binaries; not installed" "sudo BUILD=1 sh direct/install.sh"
  for tool in sentinel-dvpnd sentinel-dvpn; do
    step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo sh direct/install.sh" none install -m 0755 "$TMP/$tool-linux-$ARCH" "/usr/local/bin/$tool"
  done
  rm -rf "$TMP"
fi
step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo BUILD=1 sh direct/install.sh" none sentinel-dvpn version

# ─── 3. owner address ───
OWNER=${OWNER:-}
if [ -z "$OWNER" ] && [ -n "$CALLER" ]; then
  OWNER=$(sudo -u "$CALLER" sentinel-dvpn key show owner 2>/dev/null | jq -r .public_key) || OWNER=
  if [ -z "$OWNER" ]; then
    # first run: create the owner (wallet) key for the calling user, a plain file under ~/.sentinel-dvpn/keys
    OWNER=$(run sudo -u "$CALLER" sentinel-dvpn key new owner --unencrypted | jq -r ".public_key // empty") || OWNER=""   # empty -> no-wallet below
    echo "created owner key ~$CALLER/.sentinel-dvpn/keys/owner.json: never print it, never commit it; back it up:" >&2
    echo "  cp ~/.sentinel-dvpn/keys/owner.json /some/safe/place/owner.json && chmod 600 /some/safe/place/owner.json" >&2
  fi
fi
[ -n "$OWNER" ] || fail "$E_OPERATOR" no-wallet "no owner key: run 'sudo sh direct/install.sh' from your normal user (not a root shell), or pass OWNER=<address>" "sudo sh direct/install.sh"

# ─── 4. daemon instance ───
CFG=/var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/$INSTANCE/config.toml
if [ ! -f "$CFG" ]; then
  step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo sentinel-dvpnd init --instance $INSTANCE --owner $OWNER --plain-key && sudo sh direct/install.sh" none sentinel-dvpnd init --instance "$INSTANCE" --owner "$OWNER" --plain-key
else
  echo "instance $INSTANCE already exists ($CFG); keeping it" >&2
fi

# ─── 5. kill switch ───
if [ "${KILL_SWITCH:-off}" = on ]; then
  step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo sh direct/install.sh" none sed -i "s/^kill_switch = .*/kill_switch = 'on'/" "$CFG"
else
  step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo sh direct/install.sh" none sed -i "s/^kill_switch = .*/kill_switch = 'off'/" "$CFG"
fi
grep '^kill_switch' "$CFG" >&2

# ─── 6. service ───
if [ "${FOREGROUND:-0}" != 1 ]; then
  if [ ! -f "/etc/systemd/system/sentinel-dvpnd@.service" ] && ! systemctl cat "sentinel-dvpnd@$INSTANCE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo sentinel-dvpnd doctor --instance $INSTANCE" none sentinel-dvpnd service install --instance "$INSTANCE"
  fi
  # Not started here: the daemon refuses to start until the grant exists ("preflight failed: grant").
  # connect.sh opens the grant, then starts it. Restart only if it already runs (config change).
  if systemctl is-active --quiet "sentinel-dvpnd@$INSTANCE.service"; then
    step "$E_OTHER" daemon-unavailable "sudo journalctl -u sentinel-dvpnd@$INSTANCE -n 20" none sentinel-dvpnd service restart --instance "$INSTANCE"
  else
    run systemctl stop "sentinel-dvpnd@$INSTANCE.socket" "sentinel-dvpnd@$INSTANCE.service" 2>/dev/null || true
    run systemctl reset-failed "sentinel-dvpnd@$INSTANCE.service" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ─── 7. socket access ───
[ -z "$CALLER" ] || step "$E_OTHER" install-failed "sudo usermod -aG sentinel-dvpn $CALLER" none usermod -aG sentinel-dvpn "$CALLER"

DEVICE=$(device_address)
if [ "${FOREGROUND:-0}" = 1 ]; then NEXT="sh direct/fund-request.sh; after connect.sh opened the grant, run: sudo sentinel-dvpnd run --instance $INSTANCE (in another shell)"; else NEXT="sh direct/fund-request.sh (the daemon starts in connect.sh, once the grant exists; no new login needed: the scripts use sudo for the daemon socket until a NEW ssh session, or newgrp sentinel-dvpn, gives you the group)"; fi
summary true install "$NEXT" "\"owner\":\"$OWNER\",\"device\":\"$DEVICE\",\"instance\":\"$INSTANCE\""

# file: GLOSSARY.md

# Glossary

One plain line per term the page ([`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)), [`docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md`](docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md),
[`mcp/README.md`](mcp/README.md) and the JSON answers use, with the command that shows or changes it.
A line is `**term** (`other names`) — meaning. Shows: … Changes: …`. Every command starts with
`devnet-dvpn` (except the Path B section at the end: `sentinel-dvpn`). Failure `code` values are not listed here: each one is defined, with its message and its next
command, in the failure-code tables of [`docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md`](docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md).

## Money and accounts

- **tDVPN** (`tdvpn`, `deposit.tdvpn`) — the devnet token you pay nodes with. It has no value. Shows: `agent status --json` (`tdvpn`). Changes: a person asks the faucet (page, section 3), or `wallet send --to <ADDRESS> --tdvpn 100 --yes`. `deposit.tdvpn` = the most tDVPN one deposit can hold.
- **SOL** (`sol`) — devnet SOL: pays transaction fees only. It has no value. Shows: `agent status --json` (`sol`). Changes: a person asks the Solana faucet.
- **devnet** — the Solana test network. Nothing on it is worth money. Shows: `version --json` (must say network devnet).
- **wallet** (`address`, `owner`) — your account: an address that holds tDVPN and SOL. Shows: `wallet show --json`, `agent status --json` (`address`). Changes: `wallet create --keyfile <path> --yes`, `wallet import <file>`.
- **key file** (`DVPN_KEYFILE`) — the file with your wallet's secret key; whoever has it owns the wallet. The environment variable `DVPN_KEYFILE` names it. Shows: `wallet show`. Changes: `wallet create`, `wallet import <file>`. Never print it or commit it.
- **base units** (`baseUnits`, `ownerLamports`, `ownerTdvpn`, `priceUnit`, `deviceLamports`, `solLamports`, `tdvpnBase`, `heldBase`, `spentBase`, `refundableBase`, `deposit.baseUnits`, `deposit.tdvpnBase`) — the same amount as a whole number: 1 tDVPN = 1000000, 1 SOL = 1000000000. Shows: any `--json` answer that carries the field. From v0.3.0-rc6 every amount has a twin in base units: `sol` → `solLamports`, `tdvpn` → `tdvpnBase`, `held` → `heldBase`, `spent` → `spentBase`, `refundable` → `refundableBase`, `deposit.tdvpn` → `deposit.tdvpnBase` (`deposit.baseUnits` is the older name). `deviceLamports` = the SOL this computer's device key holds.
- **userBalance** — tDVPN held for your wallet inside the program, in base units; `settle withdraw` moves it to the wallet. It is the number `agent status` calls `held`. Shows: `wallet show --json`. Changes: `settle withdraw --yes`.

## Deposits and refunds

- **deposit** (`channel`, `userOpenChannels`) — tDVPN you lock for one node. The part you do not use comes back. Shows: `settle list`. Changes: `agent up --yes` opens one, `agent down --yes` closes it. `userOpenChannels` = how many deposits are open (`wallet show --json`).
- **per GB / per hour** (`per_gb`, `per_hour`, `perGb`, `perHour`, `basis`) — how a deposit is billed: by data or by time. Shows: `cost <node> --basis per_gb --units 1`. Changes: `agent up --basis per_gb|per_hour --units <N>`.
- **price** (`priceUnit`, `cost`) — tDVPN per GB or per hour a node asks. Shows: `nodes list --json`, `cost <node>`. Changes: `agent up --max-price N` caps it. `cost <node>` = the command that shows the exact deposit before you pay.
- **open / in-use / closing / ready** (`pending`) — the state of a deposit: open = unused, in-use = the live session's, closing = refund started and waiting, ready = refund can be taken. Shows: `settle list`, `agent down --json` (`pending`).
- **deposits** — in `agent status --json`: the wallet's open or closing deposits (`channel`, `node`, `status`, `refundable`, `readyAt`); present only when it has any. Shows: `agent status --json` (`deposits`).
- **readyAt** — the time (Unix seconds) a closing deposit becomes ready. Shows: `settle list`, `agent down --json`.
- **refundable** — in `settle list` and `agent down --json`: the tDVPN still to come back from deposits that are closing; a lower bound. Not the `held` of `agent status` (in v0.3.0-rc4, `agent status` called that balance `refundable`: [`docs/OLDER-RELEASES.md`](docs/OLDER-RELEASES.md)). Shows: `settle list`, `agent down --json`.
- **settle** — the two steps that return a deposit's unused part: `settle run --yes` starts closing, and again after the wait finishes it. Shows: `settle list`. Changes: `settle run --yes`.
- **withdraw** — moves the tDVPN held for your wallet (`userBalance`) into the wallet. Changes: `settle withdraw --yes`. Shows: `agent status --json` (`refundable`).
- **spent** — tDVPN the live session has used so far. Shows: `agent status --json` (`spent`).
- **plan** (`plan session`, `subscription`) — a prepaid subscription: one price up front, no refund, only the plan's own nodes. Shows: `plans list`. Changes: `plans subscribe <plan> --yes`, then `agent up --plan <subscription>`.
- **voucher** (`stream`) — how a node bills: voucher = per hour, stream = per GB. A node supports one; the codes `mode_not_voucher` and `mode_not_stream` mean the other. Changes: `agent up --basis per_hour|per_gb`.

## This computer

- **device** (`device key`) — what signs for you on this computer: a key kept here that spends from your wallet only up to the spending limit. Shows: `device show --json`. Changes: `daemon init`, `device setup --yes`, `device switch --yes`, `device discard-setup --yes`.
- **spending limit** (`allowance`, `grant.allowance`, `token approval`, `spending approval`, `delegated`, `limitRaised`, `limitNote`) — the most tDVPN the device may spend from your wallet; a cap, not a charge. It is a token approval, and repeated setups can leave it larger than you set. Shows: `device show --json` (`grant.allowance`, base units). Changes: `device setup --allowance N --yes`. `delegated` = the approval left, in base units (`wallet show --json`). `limitRaised` (`from`, `to`) and `limitNote` (the command that lowers it again) = `agent up` raised the limit for this deposit; from v0.3.0-rc6 only with `--raise-limit`.
- **device SOL** — a little SOL (about 0.05) that `device setup` sends the device to pay its own fees. Shows: `device show --json`. Changes: `device setup --yes`.
- **service** (`dvpnd`, `no-service`) — the VPN program that runs in the background on this computer and builds the tunnel. Shows: `daemon doctor --json`. Changes: `daemon install --yes`, `daemon uninstall`.
- **drivers** (`repair-drivers`) — the protocol tools the service needs on this computer. Shows: `daemon drivers`. Changes: `daemon repair-drivers --yes`.
- **relogin** — the service does not accept this account yet in a normal shell: start a new sign-in or SSH session. Shows: `daemon install --json` (`"relogin": true`).
- **RPC** (`rpc-ws`) — the Solana connection the service uses. Shows: `daemon settings --json`. Changes: `daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes`. `rpc-ws` = the failure code (exit 6) when the RPC's websocket address (set with `daemon set --rpc-ws <wss url> --yes`) does not answer; nothing changed, retry in a minute.
- **kill switch** (`persist`, `on`, `off`, `blocked`, `blockedBefore`, `kill-switch`) — blocks the internet whenever the tunnel is not up. `persist` and `on` are the same setting in these apps. `blocked` = no session and the internet is blocked. Shows: `daemon settings --json`, `quality ip`, `agent status --json` (`blocked`). Changes: `daemon set --kill-switch on|off --yes`, `daemon restore-network`. `kill-switch` = the failure code (exit 5) when the kill switch refuses a step; run the `action`.
- **split tunnelling** — sends some addresses or apps around the tunnel. Shows: `split status`. Changes: `daemon set --split-mode exclude --split-routes <list> --yes`.
- **whole device** (`wholeDevice`) — the whole computer goes through the node, not only apps that use the proxy. Shows: `agent status --json` (`wholeDevice`), `daemon settings --json`. Changes: `daemon set --whole-device false --yes`.

## Nodes and the connection

- **node** (`server`) — a computer that sells VPN traffic; you pay it a deposit. The page says node; `server` means the same. Shows: `nodes list --online --json`. Changes: `agent up --node N`.
- **protocol** (`wireguard`, `amneziawg`, `openvpn`, `hysteria2`, `v2ray`, `xray`) — how the tunnel is built; a node serves one. WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenVPN and Hysteria2 carry the whole computer. V2Ray and Xray carry the whole computer on a new Windows or macOS install and only proxy users on Linux. Shows: `daemon drivers`, `nodes list --protocol <name>`. Changes: `agent up --protocol <name>`.
- **country** — the two-letter country the node reports. Changes: `agent up --country DE`.
- **tunnel** — the encrypted link between this computer and the node. Shows: `quality ip --json`.
- **connected** (`disconnected`, `session`) — a session with a node is live; `session` is its id. Shows: `agent status --json`. Changes: `agent up --yes`, `agent down --yes`.
- **exitIp / directIp** (`direct`, `direct.ip`, `viaSocks.ip`) — the address the internet sees. `directIp` is this computer's own address; `exitIp` is the node's. If they are equal you are not tunnelled. Shows: `quality ip --json`, `agent up --json` (`exitIp`, `directIp`).
- **socks** (`viaSocks`) — the local proxy address (`socks5h://host:port`) for apps; the only traffic that uses a V2Ray or Xray tunnel on Linux. Shows: `agent status --json` (`socks`), `quality ip --json` (`viaSocks`).
- **reused** — `agent up` kept the live session because it already matches what you asked; nothing was paid. Shows: `agent up --json` (`reused`).
- **switchFrom** — the node a switch would leave. Shows: `agent up` without `--yes` (`switchFrom`).
- **note** — one sentence on what the live session means (whole computer through the node, or only the proxy) and the command to stop it. Shows: `agent up --json` (`note`).
- **server stopped** (`server-stopped`, `serverStopped`, `alsoNext`, `message`) — the node stopped serving: your traffic is not going through it, the deposit is safe. `agent status` answers `connected: false` with this code; `serverStopped` names the node, the session and the reason. Changes: `next` = `agent up --yes` (another node), `alsoNext` = `agent down --yes` (closes the deposit, refunds the unused part). Shows: `agent status --json`. `message` = the sentence that comes with this code: what happened, and that your deposit is safe.
- **node refused** (`node-refused`) — a node refused after you paid it. The deposit is open: `agent down --yes` closes it; `agent up` is not offered, because it would open a second deposit. Shows: a failed `agent up --json`.
- **replaced** (`replacedNote`) — the live session was not tunnelled (its exit address is this computer's own), so `agent up` did not reuse it and switched to another node; `replaced` names the old node. Shows: `agent up --json`.
- **notClosed / warning** — in `agent down --json`: deposits that another device of this wallet opened (a replaced computer) and that this computer cannot close. `notClosed` = `[{channel, device}]`, `warning` = the sentence that says so. Changes: `device revoke --device <device> --yes`, then `settle run --device <device> --yes`.
- **skipped** (`skippedNote`) — a node `agent up` leaves out for 10 minutes because it stopped serving or refused after a deposit. Shows: `agent up` (with or without `--yes`).

## Answers and flags

- **devnet-dvpn** (`DVPN_CLI_NAME`, `<cli>`) — the command-line program of the Sentinel dVPN apps; every command here starts with it. When an app's shortcut renames it, `DVPN_CLI_NAME` holds the new name and `<cli>` stands for it. Shows: `version --json`.
- **programId / mint** (`J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs`, `Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa`) — the Solana program this build pays and the tDVPN token it uses. On devnet: `programId` = `J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs`, `mint` = `Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa`; any other value is the wrong build: pay nothing. Shows: `version --json` (v0.3.0-rc6 and newer).
- **sentinel-dvpn / sentinel-dvpnd** — Sentinel's own public command-line tool and VPN daemon, used on Path B instead of `devnet-dvpn`. Shows: [`docs/DIRECT.md`](docs/DIRECT.md).
- **signatures** — the transactions a command signed; an empty list means none. Shows: `agent down --json` (`signatures`).
- **agent** (`connect`, `disconnect`, `status`) — `agent up`, `agent down` and `agent status` do the whole flow with one command each; `connect`, `disconnect` and `status` are the single steps. Shows: `agent status --json`.
- **ok** — `true` when the command worked, `false` when it failed. Shows: every `--json` answer.
- **code** — a short name for what failed; the list is in the failure-code tables of `docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md`. Shows: any failed `--json` answer.
- **error** — the sentence saying what failed. Shows: any failed `--json` answer.
- **action** — the command that fixes the failure, or null. Run it as printed. Shows: any failed `--json` answer.
- **next** — the command to run next, or the funding step. Run it as printed. Shows: any successful `agent` answer.
- **defaults** (`priceCap`, `priceCapBase`, `spendingLimit`, `spendingLimitRecommended`, `defaults.priceCap`, `defaults.spendingLimitRecommended`, `defaults.source`, `source`, `fixed`, `market`, `reason`, `p50`, `p75`, `outliers`) — in `agent up --json` (v0.3.0-rc7): what the price cap and the spending limit are and where they came from: `source` `market` (sized from the matching online nodes, `market.p50` / `p75` per unit) or `fixed` (too few priced nodes; `reason` says why). Shows: `agent up --json`. Changes: `--max-price`, `devnet-dvpn settings set allowanceTdvpn=<n>`.
- **nextAfter** — in `settle run --json` (v0.3.0-rc7): Unix seconds when the last closing deposit is ready for the next `settle run --yes`. Shows: `settle run --json`.
- **docUrl** — on every failure line (v0.3.0-rc7): a link to the code's row in `docs/CODES.md` (`…/docs/CODES.md#code-<code>`). Shows: any `--json` failure.
- **needsConfirm** (`what`) — exit `2`: nothing was signed; `what` is the sentence of what it would do. Changes: run it again with `--yes`.
- **dry run** — a command without `--yes`: it prints what it would do and changes nothing (exit `2`). Shows: any command that spends money or changes the system.
- **`--yes`** — the flag that lets a command spend money or change the system. Without it nothing happens.
- **`--json`** — the flag that makes a command print one line of JSON.
- **ready** — in `wallet show --json`: `true` when this wallet is set up to connect. Shows: `wallet show --json`.
- **version, tag, file, path** — the installer's answer: the app version it installed, the release tag, the file it used and the program's path. Shows: the last line of `install.sh` or `install.ps1`.
- **DVPN_VERSION** — the release tag the installer takes, e.g. `v0.3.0-rc6`; without it the installer takes the newest. Changes: `DVPN_VERSION=v0.3.0-rc6 sh` (PowerShell: `$env:DVPN_VERSION = 'v0.3.0-rc6'`).
- **SHA256SUMS** — the list of checksums in a release; the installer compares the file to it. Shows: the release page.

## Next release (v0.3.0-rc4 does not have these yet)

Terms from the release after v0.3.0-rc4. Until it is published, the answers of the published apps do not carry them.

- **money** — next release: every failed answer says whether money moved, in one sentence: "Nothing was paid." / "A deposit may be open: `agent down --yes` closes it." / "It is not known whether a deposit was opened: `agent status` lists it." Shows: any failed `--json` answer (`money`).
- **held** — in `agent status --json`: the tDVPN held for your wallet inside the program (the same number as `userBalance`), which `settle withdraw` moves to the wallet. Shows: `agent status --json` (`held`). Changes: `settle withdraw --yes`.
- **nodeStopped** — next release: the new name of `serverStopped` (see **server stopped**). Shows: `agent status --json`.

## Path B (Sentinel's own tools, or your own code)

Terms for [`docs/DIRECT.md`](docs/DIRECT.md) (Sentinel's `sentinel-dvpn` CLI and `sentinel-dvpnd` daemon) and
[`docs/BUILD-YOUR-OWN-CLIENT.md`](docs/BUILD-YOUR-OWN-CLIENT.md) (your own code against the program). Commands here start
with `sentinel-dvpn`, not `devnet-dvpn`. A field written `Account.field` is the program's IDL field
(`sentinel-programs/idl/dvpn.json` in the public repo).

- **grant** — an on-chain permission from your wallet (granter) to another key (grantee) for a set of actions, at PDA `["grant", owner, grantee, target]`. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn grant search --granter <owner> --grantee <device>`; IDL `Grant.permissions`, `Grant.expires_at`. Changes: `grant open-grant`, `grant update-grant`, `grant close-grant`.
- **allowance** (the cap) — the most tDVPN, in base units, the grantee may lock into channels for you; each new escrow is charged against it and it is not given back on close. Error 6024 when exceeded. Shows: `grant search` (`Grant.allowance`; 18446744073709551615 = unlimited). Changes: `grant open-grant --allowance N`, `grant update-grant`.
- **delegate** (`approve-delegate`) — the Token-2022 approval that lets the program move tDVPN from your token account when the grantee opens or funds a channel; set it to the allowance. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn wallet balance`. Changes: `wallet approve-delegate --amount-base-units N`, `wallet revoke-delegate`.
- **operator key** (`device key`, `client.key`) — the daemon's own key: it signs the daemon's transactions and every voucher, and pays channel and user-account rent. Shows: `sentinel-dvpnd init` output (`public_key`), `/var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/<instance>/keys/`. Changes: `sentinel-dvpnd init --instance <name>`.
- **escrow** — the tDVPN locked in one channel for one node; the unspent part comes back after close + withdraw. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn channel show <channel>` (`Channel.escrow`, `Channel.redeemed`). Changes: `client start --new-channel --escrow-base-units N`, IDL `open_channel(escrow)`, `fund_channels(amounts)`.
- **escrow_base_units** — the daemon's default escrow when a new channel gives none: 1000000000 = 1000 tDVPN. Always pass `--escrow-base-units`. Shows: `/var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/<instance>/config.toml` (`escrow_base_units`).
- **signed voucher** (`Voucher`) — not the billing mode **voucher** above: a signed running total (`cumulative_amount` + 64-byte ed25519 signature) of what you owe on a channel; the node redeems it on chain and can never take more than the escrow (6034). Shows: `sentinel-dvpn client status <session id>` (`spent`); IDL type `Voucher`, `Channel.redeemed`. Changes: the daemon signs them as you use the session.
- **voucher_signer** — the key whose signatures a voucher channel accepts, fixed when the channel opens; with the daemon it must be the operator key. Shows: `channel show <channel>` (`Channel.voucher_signer`). Changes: IDL `open_channel(terms = Voucher { voucher_signer })`.
- **start_close** — starts a voucher channel's refund: status goes from open (0) to closing (1) and the grace clock starts. Shows: `channel search --owner <owner>` (`Channel.status`, `Channel.close_started_at`). Changes: `sentinel-dvpn channel start-close-channel --channel <channel>`.
- **channel_close_grace** (`channel_close_grace_seconds`) — the wait between start-close and close, 7200 s (2 h) on devnet, so the node can redeem signed vouchers; closing early gives 6035. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn program params` (`Config.channel_close_grace_seconds`).
- **close** (`close-channel`) — after the grace, moves the unspent escrow to your user account and returns the channel rent; anyone may send it for a voucher channel. Changes: `sentinel-dvpn channel close-channel --channel <channel>`.
- **withdraw-user-balance** — the Path B command for **withdraw** above: moves your whole user balance from the program to your token account, and closes the user account when no channels are open. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn user search --owner <owner>` (`User.balance`). Changes: `sentinel-dvpn user withdraw-user-balance`.
- **rent_recipient** — the address that gets an account's SOL rent back when it closes; it must be the signer or the rent payer when the account opens (6049, 6050). Shows: `channel show <channel>` (`Channel.rent_recipient`), `User.rent_recipient`, `Grant.rent_recipient`. Changes: IDL `open_channel(channel_rent_recipient, user_rent_recipient)`, `open_grant(grant_rent_recipient)`.
- **user account** (`User`) — the program's record for your wallet at PDA `["user", owner]`: refunds land in `balance`, `open_channels` counts channels. The first channel open creates it; `withdraw-user-balance` closes it. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn user search --owner <owner>`.
- **Config PDA** — the program's one settings account at PDA `["config"]` (devnet `Cu5vofxVQgZXRVwfBqApw84ZWy1hjhDmHkznyDr6TRiQ`): mint, vault, fees, grace windows, pause mask. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn program params`, `program status`.
- **node API address** (`uri`) — the HTTPS address where a node serves its session API, stored on chain with the node. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn node search --live`, `node inspect <node>` (`Node.uri`).
- **kill_switch setting** (`config.toml`) — the config key behind **kill switch** above: the daemon's firewall that blocks all traffic except the tunnel when no session is up; `on` locks you out of an SSH box. Shows: `/var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/<instance>/config.toml` (`kill_switch`), `StopSession` reply `kill_switch_released`. Changes: edit `kill_switch = 'on'|'off'|'persist'`, then restart the daemon.
- **paused_mask** — the program's switches for new opens; bit 32 (`PAUSE_CHANNEL_OPENS`) set means `open_channel` fails with 6001. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn program status` (`paused_features`), `Config.paused_mask` (0 on devnet).
- **fee_bps** — the network's cut of every redeemed voucher, in basis points: 200 = 2 %. It comes out of the node's pay, not your escrow. Shows: `sentinel-dvpn program params` (`Config.fee_bps`).
- **instance** (`c1`, `INSTANCE`) — the daemon's name on this computer, `c1` unless `INSTANCE` says otherwise; its files are in `/var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/<instance>/`. Shows: `sudo sentinel-dvpnd doctor --instance c1`. Changes: `INSTANCE=<name> sh direct/install.sh`.
- **tunnel adapter** (`dvpn-c1`) — the WireGuard interface the daemon makes for instance `c1` during a session (on Windows, the adapter's name). Shows: `ip link`, `wg show` (Linux).
- **script settings** (`UNITS`, `MAX_PRICE`, `ESCROW`, `ALLOWANCE`, `WANT_DVPN`, `MIN_DVPN`, `MIN_OWNER_SOL`, `MIN_DEVICE_SOL`, `RPC_URL`) — environment variables the `direct/*.sh` scripts read; each rule and default is in DIRECT.md's "Market defaults" table (step 5). `UNITS` = GB per deposit (1); `RPC_URL` = the Solana RPC (default `api.devnet.solana.com`). Changes: set one before the script, e.g. `MAX_PRICE=60 sh direct/connect.sh`.
- **moneyNote** — the sentence beside `money` on every `direct/*.sh` failure line: what moved and how to see or undo it. Shows: the last line of a script.
- **script answers** (`funded`, `signature`, `closeAfter`) — fields on a script's last JSON line: `funded` (fund-request: both wallets hold enough), `signature` (fund-device: the transfer), `closeAfter` (refund: when to run it again, Unix seconds). Shows: the step table in DIRECT.md.
- **selftest hold** (`hold`) — the seconds `selftest.sh` keeps the session up while it checks the exit IP; a drop inside it is `session-dropped`. Changes: `HOLD=<s> sh direct/selftest.sh`.
- **direct-v1** (`direct-build`) — the release of prebuilt `sentinel-dvpn` / `sentinel-dvpnd` binaries the scripts install, checked against `direct/SHA256SUMS`; `direct-build` is the workflow that rebuilds them for the attestation. Shows: `sudo sh direct/install.sh`.
- **sentinel-dvpn subcommands** (`init`, `doctor`, `approve`, `open-grant`, `update-grant`, `fund-channels`, `start-close-channel`) — Sentinel's own CLI and daemon commands the scripts run (`sentinel-dvpnd init` / `doctor`; `sentinel-dvpn wallet approve-delegate`, `grant open-grant` / `update-grant`, `channel fund-channels` / `start-close-channel`). Shows: `sentinel-dvpn --help`.
- **program, proto and RPC names** (`signer`, `vault`, `balance`, `decimals`, `mode`, `permissions`, `target`, `granter`, `opener`, `redeemed`, `constants`, `errors`, `meaning`, `msg`, `Custom`, `Credential`, `oneof`, `nil`, `client`, `client.owner`, `network`, `finish`, `dvpn`, `idl.address`, `channel.escrow`, `channel.redeemed`, `sendTransaction`, `getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption`, `api.devnet.solana.com`) — names quoted from the program's IDL (`sentinel-programs/idl/dvpn.json`), the daemon's `daemon.proto`, Go, the example programs and the Solana RPC, as BUILD-YOUR-OWN-CLIENT.md uses them; they mean what those sources say. `snake_case` and `CamelCase` program names (`open_channel`, `GraceNotElapsed`) are read the same way without a line here.

# file: docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md

# Agent commands: the output contract

What `agent status`, `agent up` and `agent down` print with `--json`, field by field, and every
failure `code` they can return. A test fails if a failure code the CLI can return is missing here.

`<cli>` below is `devnet-dvpn`, or the value of `DVPN_CLI_NAME` when a wrapper sets it.

## The four kinds of answer

Every run prints exactly one JSON line on stdout. A warning (another VPN is on) goes to stderr.

| Exit | Line | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `{"ok":true, …, "next": "…"}` | Done. `next` is the command (or the funding) to do next. |
| 1 | `{"ok":false,"error":"…","code":"…"\|null,"action":"…"\|null,"money":"…"}` | Failed. `action` is the command that fixes it, or null. `money` says whether money moved (see "Did money move?" below). |
| 2 | `{"needsConfirm":true,"what":"…", …}` | Would spend: nothing was signed. Re-run with `--yes`. |
| 3 | (no JSON; one line on stderr) | Wrong usage: bad flag value, unknown flag or unknown subcommand. Nothing ran. |
| 4 | `{"ok":false, …}` as for 1 | Needs you or your operator: `not-funded`, `spending-limit`, `price-cap`, `no-wallet`. Nothing was paid; do `action` (fund, raise the limit, load the wallet). |
| 5 | `{"ok":false, …}` as for 1 | Refused for safety: `kill-switch`, `kill-switch-held`, `kill-switch-failed`. Read `action` (often `<cli> daemon restore-network`). |
| 6 | `{"ok":false, …}` as for 1 | Network or RPC and no deposit can be open (`rpc-busy`, `rpc-unavailable`, `rpc-ws`): nothing changed. Retry in a minute, or set your own RPC endpoint. A network code after which a deposit may be open (`rpc-timeout`, `rpc-network`, `rpc-quota`, `timeout`) exits 1: read `money`. Exit 5 (`kill-switch-failed`) can also follow a paid deposit: read `money`. |

Exit codes 4–6 are from release 0.3.0-rc.6; older releases exit 1 for these.

Amounts are decimal strings in tDVPN or SOL (e.g. `"0.002"`). Each one has a sibling with the same amount in base units, as a string: `sol` → `solLamports`, `tdvpn` → `tdvpnBase`, `held` → `heldBase`, `spent` → `spentBase`, `refundable` → `refundableBase`, `deposit.tdvpn` → `deposit.tdvpnBase` (also `deposit.baseUnits`, the older name), `limitRaised.from/to` → `fromBase/toBase`. 1 tDVPN = 1000000 base units; 1 SOL = 1000000000 lamports. Times (`readyAt`) are Unix seconds.

**Default price cap (S7, rc.6):** without `--max-price` (and without `--plan`), `agent up` never pays a deposit above the Settings spending limit / 10 (5 tDVPN with the default 50): it answers `price-cap`, nothing paid. `--max-price N` is your own cap and replaces it.

**Spending limit (S7, rc.6):** `agent up --yes` never raises this computer's spending limit on its own. When the deposit is above it, the answer is `code: "spending-limit"` (exit 4, nothing paid), and `action` is the same line with `--raise-limit --yes`. Run that line to raise it (the answer then carries `limitRaised` / `limitNote`), or set your own limit with `<cli> device setup --allowance <N> --yes`.

**No catch-all (S5, rc.6):** a connect failure with no known cause never says "Something went wrong". It says whether a deposit was paid (`node-refused`, deposit safe and refunded after the wait) or not (`unknown`, "Nothing was paid", look at `<cli> logs --lines 80`).

**`version --json` (rc.6):** `{ app, network, programId, mint, platform, node, lan }`. Check `programId` = `J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs` and `mint` = `Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa` before you pay.

## agent status

Reads only. It never signs, never connects, never asks for `--yes`.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `true` | |
| `address` | string \| null | The wallet address; null = no wallet on this computer. |
| `sol` | string \| null | SOL in the wallet; null when there is no wallet or it could not be read. |
| `tdvpn` | string \| null | tDVPN in the wallet. |
| `held` | string \| null | The wallet's balance held in the program (`userBalance`), which `settle withdraw` moves to the wallet. Not the `refundable` of `agent down` (that sums the deposits still open). On devnet a closed deposit's refund went straight to the wallet's tDVPN, so this stayed `"0"` (Linux run 2026-11-15). Was `refundable` before this change. |
| `device` | string \| null | This computer's device key; null = not set up yet. |
| `service` | boolean | The VPN service answers. |
| `connected` | boolean | A session is live. |
| `blocked` | `true` | Only when no session is live and the internet does not answer (the kill switch still holds the block, or the network is down). |
| `session` | string | Only when connected: the session id. |
| `node` | string | Only when connected: the server's address. |
| `protocol` | string | Only when connected: the protocol in use. |
| `spent` | string | Only when connected: tDVPN used so far. |
| `exitIp` | string \| null | Only when connected: the address the internet sees; null if the check did not finish within 8 s. |
| `socks` | string \| null | Only when connected: `socks5h://host:port` for apps to use; null on Android or when the protocol gives none. |
| `wholeDevice` | boolean | Only when connected: true when the whole computer goes through the node (WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenVPN, Hysteria2 always; V2Ray and Xray when the service runs them whole-device, the default on a fresh Windows or macOS install; on Linux they cover only apps that use `socks`; Android always). |
| `code` | `"server-stopped"` | Only when a node stopped serving (see "The node stopped serving"). `connected` is false then. |
| `message` | string | With `code`: what happened, and that your deposit is safe. |
| `nodeStopped` | object | With `code`: `{ node, session, reason }`. |
| `alsoNext` | string | With `code`: `<cli> agent down --yes`, the other way out (`next` is `<cli> agent up --yes`). With `service: false` and a deposit to close (E-75): the deposit's own step (`<cli> agent down --yes after <ISO time>`), while `next` is the service fix (`<cli> daemon install --yes …`). |
| `deposits` | object[] | Only when the wallet has deposits on chain: `{ channel, node, status, refundable, readyAt }` for each open or closing one. |
| `next` | string | See below. |

`next`, in this order: `blocked` → `<cli> agent up --yes to reconnect through a node (protection stays), or <cli> daemon restore-network to go direct (protection off until the next connect)` (with no wallet: `<cli> daemon restore-network (the internet is blocked), then` the no-wallet step);
no wallet → `<cli> wallet create --keyfile <path> --yes, then fund the address it prints`;
connected → `<cli> agent down --yes`; a deposit still open and no session → `<cli> agent down --yes` (a closing one: `… after <ISO readyAt>`), never `agent up`, which would open a second deposit; balances unreadable → `<cli> agent status (the balances could not be read; try again in a moment)`;
SOL under 0.02 (wallet not ready) or no tDVPN → `send at least … to <address>, then <cli> agent up --yes`;
device set up but service not answering → the `daemon-missing` action below; otherwise `<cli> agent up --yes`.

## agent up

`agent up [--protocol P] [--country CC] [--node N] [--basis per_gb|per_hour] [--units N] [--plan S] [--max-price N] --yes`

Flags: `--protocol` = `any` or one of `wireguard`, `amneziawg`, `openvpn`, `v2ray`, `xray`, `hysteria2`; `--country` = two letters;
`--basis` defaults to the saved setting (not always per_gb); `--units` 1–1000 GB or hours, default from settings;
`--max-price` = tDVPN per unit of the basis; `--plan` = a subscription address you hold (no deposit, the plan's live nodes only);
`--node` = one exact node (it must still be online and match the other filters).
Without `--node` it picks the lowest latency among the matching nodes that answer. With no `--max-price`, only
among the cheapest of them (a deposit at most 2 times the cheapest one's), so a fast node at 50 tDVPN/GB is
never taken while one at 0.002 answers; `--max-price` sets your own cap instead. A flag given with no value
(`--plan` alone, `--plan=`) is a usage error: nothing runs.

**On its own (no `--yes` needed):** reads the live session, the node list (probing them), wallet and
subscriptions; creates the device key if this computer has none (`daemon init`: local, no transaction).
**Never without `--yes`:** the deposit, the spending limit, the connect, a switch. Without `--yes` it
answers exit 2:

| Field (exit 2) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `needsConfirm` | `true` | |
| `what` | string | The sentence it would do, e.g. `Connect to <node> (DE, wireguard): deposit up to 0.002 tDVPN (1 GB), unused part refunded. Nothing is signed until you pass --yes.` A switch starts `Switch from <node>.` |
| `node` | string | The node it picked. |
| `deposit` | object | As below. |
| `switchFrom` | string \| null | The live node it would leave; null = not connected. |

A live session is reused when `--node` is the live node, or, with no `--node`, `--protocol` (if given) is the
live protocol and `--country` (if given) is the live node's country. Nothing else is compared: `--basis`,
`--units`, `--max-price` and `--plan` are ignored while a session is live. A reused session is answered at once, exit 0, `reused: true`, nothing paid, no `--yes` needed. One that does not match is
switched: the switch leaves it and connects to the new node; with the kill switch on, the
block stays up between the two. The live node is never picked for the switch.

| Field (exit 0) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok`, `connected` | `true` | |
| `session` | string | Session id. |
| `node` | string | The node's address. |
| `protocol` | string | The protocol really used (on a node that offers several, the service picks). |
| `country` | string \| null | Two-letter country of the node. |
| `exitIp` | string \| null | Address the internet sees; null if the check did not finish within 8 s. |
| `directIp` | string \| null | This computer's own address, never the node's. With only `socks` routed it is measured outside the tunnel; in whole-device mode a direct check exits by the node too, so it is the address read before the connect, or null if none was read. |
| `socks` | string \| null | `socks5h://host:port`; null on Android or when the protocol gives none. |
| `wholeDevice` | boolean | True when the whole computer goes through the node (WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenVPN, Hysteria2 always; V2Ray and Xray when the service runs them whole-device, the default on a fresh Windows or macOS install; on Linux they cover only apps that use `socks`; Android always). |
| `channel` | string \| null | The account of the deposit. |
| `deposit` | object \| null | `{basis, units, tdvpn, tdvpnBase, baseUnits}` for a per-node deposit (`tdvpn` = most it can hold; the unused part is refunded); `{plan, tdvpn: "0"}` with `--plan`; null when `reused`. |
| `reused` | `true` | Only when an existing session was kept. |
| `blockedBefore` | `true` | Only when the internet was blocked before this connect (no session, kill switch holding the block); the new session lifts it while it is up. A block connect cannot lift is refused with code `kill-switch-held`. |
| `limitRaised` / `limitNote` | object / string | Only when this connect raised the computer's spending limit, because the deposit was above it (E-73): `limitRaised` = `{ from, to, fromBase, toBase }` in tDVPN and base units, and `limitNote` = `This computer's spending limit was <from> tDVPN, below this deposit, so it was raised to <to> tDVPN (the Settings limit). To lower it: <cli> device setup --allowance <N> --yes`. Without `--yes`, the preview sentence says so first: `This computer's spending limit (<x> tDVPN) is below this deposit. It is raised only with --raise-limit: then --yes raises it to <y> tDVPN.` From rc.6 the raise needs `--raise-limit` (see "Spending limit" above). |
| `next` | string | Always `<cli> agent down --yes` (one plain command a runner can run; E-38). |
| `note` | string | What the session means. Whole device: `the whole computer goes through the node; when done: <cli> agent down --yes`, with ` (<socks> works too)` after "node" when there is a `socks`. Only `socks`: `send traffic through <socks> (e.g. curl --proxy <socks> https://api.ipify.org); only apps that use it go through the node; when done: <cli> agent down --yes`. |
| `replaced` / `replacedNote` | object / string | Only when the live session was not tunnelled (its exit address is this computer's own, E-35): `replaced` = `{ node, code: "server-stopped" }`, `replacedNote` = `The node stopped serving; your traffic is NOT going through it. Switched to <node>; <old node> is skipped next time.` |

## agent down

`agent down --yes`. **On its own:** reads the live session and the open deposits. **Never without
`--yes`:** the disconnect or any transaction. Without `--yes`, exit 2:

| Field (exit 2) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `needsConfirm` | `true` | |
