| `what` | string | e.g. `Disconnect from <node>, then close 1 per-hour deposit(s) (they bill until closed) and start closing 0 per-GB deposit(s); refunds go to your wallet.` |
| `session` | string \| null | The live session. |
| `perHour`, `perGb` | number | Deposits it would close / start closing: the open and ready ones, plus the live session's own deposit (it reads `in-use` until the disconnect). |

**Kill switch.** In these apps the kill switch `on` and `persist` are the same setting. After
`disconnect` / `agent down`, check `<cli> quality ip`. If it shows no address, the kill switch
is still blocking — this happens when the session had already dropped before you disconnected.
`<cli> daemon restore-network` lifts the block for now; it can come back at the next dropped
session or service restart. `<cli> daemon set --kill-switch off --yes` stops it coming back.

With `--yes` it runs `disconnect` (which also puts back a system proxy left with no session), then one `settle run`: a per-hour deposit is closed at once (it bills until closed); a per-GB one
starts its 2-hour close. Exit 0:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `true` | |
| `disconnected` | object \| null | `disconnect`'s own answer (e.g. `{ok, session, killSwitchReleased}`); null if it printed none. |
| `spent` | string \| null | tDVPN the session used; null = there was no session. |
| `refundable` | string | The sum of `refundable` over `pending`: tDVPN still to come back from the deposits left. Not the `held` balance of `agent status`. A lower bound: on the Linux run of 2026-11-15 a deposit listed 0.001883 and 0.001999 came back. |
| `readyAt` | number \| null | Latest time a closing deposit can be finished. |
| `signatures` | string[] | Transactions this run signed. |
| `pending` | object[] | Deposits left: `{channel, node, mode, status ('open'\|'closing'\|'ready'\|'in-use'), readyAt, refundable, …}`. |
| `notClosed` / `warning` | object[] / string | Only when a deposit another device of this wallet opened is still open (a replaced device, E-72): `notClosed` = `[{channel, device}]`, `warning` = `<n> deposit(s) opened by another device of this wallet (<device>) are still open: this computer cannot close them, so nothing was refunded for them.` `next` is then `<cli> device revoke --device <device> --yes (if it is not revoked yet), then <cli> settle run --device <device> --yes`. |
| `next` | string | A deposit of another device still open: see `notClosed`. With `readyAt`: `<cli> settle run --yes after <ISO time> (a closing deposit waits 2 h), then <cli> settle withdraw --yes`; deposits left: `<cli> settle list`; none: `<cli> agent up --yes to connect again`. |

## Failure codes (exit 1, or 4/5/6 by class: see the table above)

`action` is copied verbatim into the JSON line. Do what it says; when it is null, read `error`.

### Raised by agent-cmd itself

| Code | From | `action` | What the agent does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no-wallet` | up | `<cli> wallet create --keyfile <path> --yes, then fund the address it prints`; when this computer has a device record: `<cli> wallet import <the key file of <owner>, the wallet that set up this computer's device>, then <cli> agent up --yes` | Create a wallet in a 0600 key file, ask its owner to fund it. With a device record, import that wallet instead: a new one would not hold its funds. Nothing was paid. |
| `no-wallet` | down | `<cli> disconnect to leave the VPN now; <cli> wallet import <file> (the wallet that paid), then <cli> agent down --yes to close the deposits` | This computer's CLI has no wallet, so it cannot read or close deposits. Nothing ran. `disconnect` needs no wallet: run it to leave the VPN at once, then import the wallet that paid and run `agent down --yes`. |
| `keyfile-missing` | up, down, status | `restore <path> from your backup, then run the command again` | The key file that --keyfile or DVPN_KEYFILE names is gone. This is not "no wallet": a new wallet would not hold the funds, which stay with the lost key. Nothing ran. |
| `keyfile-mode` | up | `chmod 600 <path>, then <cli> agent up --yes` | (rc.7) The key file can be read by other users (POSIX mode with group/other bits). Refused before anything is signed; exit 4. Nothing ran. |
| `wallet-switch-needed` | up | `load the key file of the wallet named in "error", or <cli> device switch --yes (sets this computer up for the loaded wallet; the other wallet's deposits stay refundable)` | This computer is set up for another wallet, so the loaded key cannot pay here. Nothing was paid. |
| `no-device` | up | `<cli> daemon doctor` (device key could not be made) | Run it; report what it says. Nothing was paid. |
| `no-subscription` | up `--plan` | `<cli> plans list, then <cli> plans subscribe <plan> --yes` | Subscribe, or drop `--plan`. Nothing was paid. |
| `no-nodes` | up | `<cli> nodes list --online --json, then widen --protocol / --country / --max-price` | Widen the filters (check `--basis`). No transaction ran. |
| `not-funded` | up | `send at least <n> SOL and/or <n> tDVPN to <address>, then <cli> agent up --yes` | Ask the owner to fund the address. Nothing was paid. |
| `price-cap` | up (rc.6) | `<cli> agent up --node <node> --basis <basis> --units <n> --max-price <its price> --yes (you accept this price), or fewer --units, or another node` | No `--max-price` was given and the deposit is above the default cap (the Settings spending limit / 10: 5 tDVPN by default). Nothing was paid. Accept the price with `--max-price`, or ask for less. |
| `spending-limit` | up (rc.6) | `<cli> agent up --node <node> --basis <basis> --units <n> --raise-limit --yes` | The deposit is above this computer's spending limit and `--raise-limit` was not given (S7). Nothing was paid. Run `action` to raise the limit for this connect, or set your own with `<cli> device setup --allowance <N> --yes`. |
| `connect-failed` | up | `<cli> agent status` | The connect failed with no code: read `error`. It is not known whether a deposit was opened: `<cli> agent status` lists it. |
| `settle-failed` | down | `<cli> settle list` | The disconnect is done; the deposits are listed there. No new money was spent; the unused part of a deposit is still held: `<cli> settle run --yes` returns it. |
| `busy` | down | `<cli> settle run --yes` | The disconnect is done, but another refund run in the same process held the lock, so nothing was closed: run it (a per-hour deposit bills until closed). Nothing was paid. |
| disconnect's code (e.g. `daemon-unavailable`, `service-down`, `rpc-unavailable`), else `stop-failed` | down | `<cli> daemon doctor, then <cli> agent down --yes again` | The disconnect failed, so no deposit was closed (the message starts `Could not disconnect, so no deposit was closed`, then the service's plain sentence; this line is never rewritten by the rule below). A live session's deposit cannot be closed while the session is up, so a per-hour one keeps billing: fix the service, then run `agent down --yes` again. A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |

### From connect() (agent up), `action` = `nextFor(code)`

| Code | `action` |
|---|---|
| `daemon-missing` | Linux/macOS: `<cli> daemon install --yes (administrator/root once: passwordless sudo, or a person types the password), then <cli> agent up --yes`. Windows: `<cli> daemon install --yes from an elevated shell or an administrator SSH login (a normal shell shows a UAC prompt an agent cannot answer), then <cli> agent up --yes`. Nothing was paid. |
| `daemon-relogin` | Linux/macOS: as `daemon-missing`. Windows: `<cli> daemon install --yes once from an elevated shell or an administrator SSH login (the VPN service does not accept this account yet; …), then <cli> agent up --yes`. Nothing was paid. |
| `protocol-missing` | `<cli> daemon drivers (it lists the protocols ready on this computer), then <cli> agent up --protocol <a ready one> --yes; or <cli> daemon repair-drivers --yes`. The deposit is refunded by `agent down --yes`. A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `device-permission` | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` (as `no-device` from connect) Nothing was paid. |
| `daemon-unavailable` | `<cli> daemon doctor` Nothing was paid. |
| `daemon-restarting` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a few seconds (the VPN service is restarting); if it keeps failing, <cli> daemon doctor` Nothing was paid. |
| `preflight` for a service, settings or driver problem | `<cli> daemon doctor`, `<cli> daemon settings` or `<cli> daemon repair-drivers --yes`, each followed by `, then <cli> agent up --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `test-running` | `<cli> test stop, then <cli> agent up --yes` (a node test holds the VPN service) Nothing was paid. |
| `rpc-busy` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute (the network was busy)` It is not known whether a deposit was opened: `<cli> agent status` lists it. |
| `spending-limit`, and `preflight` saying "This device's spending limit is lower than this deposit" | `<cli> device setup --allowance <N> --yes (N = grant.allowance from "devnet-dvpn device show --json" divided by 1000000, plus the deposit, in tDVPN), then <cli> agent up --yes`. The limit only grows when N is above the current allowance. Nothing was paid. |
| `price-changed`, `deposit-unusable`, `deposits-unread` | `<cli> agent up --yes again (nothing was paid; it reads the price fresh)`. Nothing was paid in each case. `price-changed`: the node's price rose above the deposit `agent up` showed. `deposit-unusable`: your open deposit with this node started closing, so it cannot be used, and a new one is never paid without being shown. `deposits-unread`: your open deposits could not be read, so no second deposit was opened beside one you may have. `--max-price` still caps the next try. |
| `not-confirmed` | `<cli> agent up --yes (add --yes: nothing is paid without it)` Nothing was paid. |
| `busy` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a few seconds (another connect was running)` Nothing was paid. |
| `keyfile-missing` | `restore the key file named in "error" from your backup (it is the only key to this wallet), then <cli> agent up --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `keyfile-mode` | `chmod 600 <the key file named in "error">, then <cli> agent up --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `plan-limit` | `<cli> agent up --plan <subscription> --node <a node you already use> --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `network-mismatch` | `<cli> daemon install --yes (administrator once: it installs the service for this network), then <cli> agent up --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `session-active` | `<cli> agent down --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `node-gone`, `node-stale`, `node-offline`, `node-identity`, `node-ledger`, `peer_limit_reached`, `terms_rejected`; `preflight` that asks for another node | `<cli> nodes list --online --json, then <cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `protocol-blocked`, `tunnel-failed`, `tunnel-dead`, `tunnel-mtu`, `port-in-use` | `<cli> daemon drivers (it lists the protocols ready on this computer), then <cli> agent up --protocol <another ready one> --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `driver-missing` | `<cli> daemon repair-drivers --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `basis-unavailable` | `<cli> agent up --basis <the other one: per_gb or per_hour> --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `not-enough-tdvpn` | `send tDVPN to the wallet address (<cli> agent status shows it), then <cli> agent up --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `device-sol`, `ticket-other-owner`, `approval-revoked` | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `unauthorized` | `<cli> device show --json: if the grant is there and not revoked, set this computer's clock to the right time (a wrong clock makes the node refuse), then <cli> agent up --yes; otherwise <cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` (E-22: clock skew answered this after a deposit opened) A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `clock-skew` | `set this computer's clock to the right time (it is off by about N minutes), then <cli> agent up --yes`: refused before any deposit (nothing was paid); N is read from `error` ("about N min ahead of / behind the network's time") |
| `kill-switch-held` | `<cli> daemon restore-network, then <cli> agent up --yes` Nothing was paid. |
| `switch-reconnecting` | `<cli> agent status until "connected" is true, or <cli> agent down --yes first` Nothing was paid. |
| `switch-offline`, `timeout`, `ticket_request_stale`, `ticket_invalid`, `channel_node_reopened` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a moment` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `cancelled` | `<cli> agent up --yes again (it was stopped before it finished)` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `waiting-for-network` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute (this computer has no network yet)` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `service-stopped-connecting` | `<cli> quality ip; if it shows no address, <cli> daemon restore-network; then <cli> agent up --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `node-price`, `credit_exhausted`, `lease_insufficient`, `voucher_exceeds_escrow`, `voucher_signature_invalid` | `<cli> agent down --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes (a new deposit)` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `node-error`, `rate_limited` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `provider_unreachable` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute (the plan provider did not answer)` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `kill-switch-failed` | `<cli> agent up --yes again, or <cli> daemon set --kill-switch off --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `tunnel-closing` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a few seconds` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `dns-apply` | `<cli> daemon set --dns-mode none --yes (the VPN's DNS off), then <cli> agent up --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `deposit-pending` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a few minutes (it never pays twice)` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `rpc-network`, `rpc-quota` | `<cli> daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes (the VPN service's Solana connection), then <cli> agent up --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `rpc-timeout` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute; if it keeps failing, <cli> daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes (the VPN service's Solana connection), then <cli> agent up --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `chain-encoding`, `mode_not_voucher` | `<cli> agent up --basis per_hour --yes` (pay per hour instead) A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `mode_not_stream` | `<cli> agent up --basis per_gb --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `subscription_invalid` | `<cli> plans subscriptions, then <cli> agent up --plan <an active one> --yes, or <cli> agent up --yes without --plan` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `cannot cover the prepay` | `<cli> agent up --units <more> --yes (a deposit large enough for the node's minimum)` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `preflight` (any other action) | `read "error": it names what to change (nothing was paid), then <cli> agent up --yes` |
| `stop-failed` | `<cli> daemon doctor, then <cli> agent up --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `dns-revert-failed`, `tunnel-left` | `<cli> daemon restore-network` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `unknown`, `unsupported` | `<cli> agent status`: nothing more specific is known; read `error` (`connect-failed` is the row above) It is not known whether a deposit was opened: `<cli> agent status` lists it. |

Elevation: on Windows `agent up` can itself need one elevated step (the service pipe granting this
account); a non-elevated agent then gets `daemon-relogin`. On Linux/macOS the service install needs root once.

Every code connect() can answer (`CONNECT_CODES`) has a command above; a code before paying means nothing
was paid. Only `unknown`, `connect-failed` and `unsupported` answer `agent status`.
**An open deposit comes first (E-22):** when the start failed after the check before paying and a deposit is open
with that server, `action` is `a deposit of X tDVPN is open with this node (<channel>): <cli> agent up --yes
picks another node (this node is skipped), or <cli> agent down --yes closes it and refunds the unused part at once (per hour: it bills until closed)` (per GB:
`2 h after it starts the close`; a closing deposit: `after <ISO readyAt>`), whatever the code. A failure that follows the deposit with code `unknown` or `connect-failed` answers `node-refused` (E-37; the node refused after it was paid, and is skipped next time). `agent status` then lists every open or closing deposit in `deposits` (`channel`, `node`, `status`, `refundable`, `readyAt`), with `next` = `<cli> agent down --yes` (closing: `<cli> agent down --yes after <ISO readyAt>`), never `agent up`, which would open a second deposit.

**The node stopped serving (E-35 / E-36):** when the exit address of the live session is this computer's own, or the daemon ended the session with "the connection to this server stopped working" (the service's own words) in the last 30 min, `agent status` answers `connected: false`, `code: "server-stopped"`, `message` = `The node stopped serving; your traffic is NOT going through it. Your deposit is safe: <cli> agent down --yes closes it and the unused <X> tDVPN is refunded (<when>).`, `nodeStopped` = `{ node, session, reason }`, `next` = `<cli> agent up --yes` (the dead node is skipped for 10 min), `alsoNext` = `<cli> agent down --yes`. When the kill switch also holds the block (`blocked: true`, E-82), `next` = `<cli> daemon restore-network` (rc.6, E-86: one runnable command; rc.5 printed it with the rest in brackets) and `alsoNext` = `then <cli> agent up --yes to reconnect, or <cli> agent down --yes to close the deposit`. `agent up` never reuses such a session (see `replaced`).

**Reconnecting with the internet held (rc.7, E-87):** while the service reconnects a live session under the kill switch, no traffic flows. `agent status` answers `connected: false`, `reconnecting: true`, `blocked: true`, with `session`, `node` and `protocol` of that session, `next` = `<cli> daemon restore-network` (one runnable command; rc.6 printed it as `connected: true` with the rest in brackets) and `alsoNext` = `then <cli> agent up --yes to reconnect, or <cli> agent down --yes to close the deposit`. Plain `status --json` gives the same `next` and `alsoNext`. Wait for `connected: true` instead if the node comes back on its own.

A test fails when a new code has no command here, or a next step names an app screen or button. The CLI rewrites
app-screen words in `error` (text and JSON) to the command to run, and
says "node" where the service says "server".

A failed connect after a deposit was paid leaves that deposit open: `agent down --yes` closes it (closing an open
deposit is unit-tested; that connect() leaves it open after such a failure is not tested here).

### Did money move? (`money`)

Every failure line of `agent`, `connect`, `switch` and `test` carries `money`, one sentence, and the text error prints it as `Money: …`. Three answers:

| Class | `money` | Codes |
|---|---|---|
| none | `Nothing was paid.` | `price-cap` (rc.6), `session-active`, `node-gone`, `node-stale`, `node-offline`, `protocol-blocked`, `driver-missing`, `basis-unavailable`, `not-enough-tdvpn`, `spending-limit`, `device-sol`, `preflight`, `not-confirmed`, `no-wallet`, `keyfile-missing`, `keyfile-mode` (rc.7), `wallet-switch-needed`, `clock-skew`, `no-device`, `device-permission`, `plan-limit`, `busy`, `test-running`, `unsupported`, `daemon-missing`, `daemon-relogin`, `daemon-restarting`, `daemon-unavailable`, `network-mismatch`, `kill-switch-held`, `switch-reconnecting`, `price-changed`, `deposit-unusable`, `deposits-unread`, `no-nodes`, `not-funded`, `no-subscription`, `service-down`, `service-not-ready`, rc.7 R2: `device-home-gone`, `no-plan`, `driver-repair-failed`, `no-device-key`, `migrate-failed`, `device-not-ready`, `install-failed`, `daemon-settings-empty`, `daemon-settings-unreadable`, `dns-no-answer`, `uninstall-failed`, `checks-off`, `test-plan-failed`, `no-test-run`, `keystore-unavailable`, `keyfile-read-only` (wallet, device and settle failures read "Nothing was sent or signed.") |
| open | `A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it.` | `cancelled`, `switch-offline`, `waiting-for-network`, `ticket-other-owner`, `approval-revoked`, `service-stopped-connecting`, `node-identity`, `node-ledger`, `node-price`, `node-error`, `kill-switch-failed`, `tunnel-failed`, `tunnel-dead`, `tunnel-mtu`, `tunnel-closing`, `port-in-use`, `dns-apply`, `protocol-missing`, `deposit-pending`, `rpc-network`, `rpc-timeout`, `rpc-quota`, `timeout`, `chain-encoding`, `credit_exhausted`, `peer_limit_reached`, `lease_insufficient`, `subscription_invalid`, `ticket_request_stale`, `provider_unreachable`, `ticket_invalid`, `unauthorized`, `cannot cover the prepay`, `voucher_exceeds_escrow`, `channel_node_reopened`, `terms_rejected`, `rate_limited`, `voucher_signature_invalid`, `mode_not_voucher`, `mode_not_stream`, `stop-failed`, `dns-revert-failed`, `tunnel-left`, `node-refused`, `server-stopped` |
| unclear | `It is not known whether a deposit was opened: `<cli> agent status` lists it.` | `unknown`, `connect-failed`, `rpc-busy`, `rpc-unavailable`, `rpc-ws` (rc.7) |
| refund | `No new money was spent; the unused part of a deposit is still held: `<cli> settle run --yes` returns it.` | `settle-failed`, `daemon-gone` (rc.6: the service stopped mid-refund) |

A row above that lists several codes says the worst case; the `money` of the answer is exact. The text of `money` uses the command name `devnet-dvpn` (or `DVPN_CLI_NAME`).

### Replaced on the way out (any of the three)

`index.ts` rewrites an error whose raw text is a VPN-service or RPC failure. Then `code` and `action`
come from the shared copy, not the table above:

| Code | `action` |
|---|---|
| `service-down` | the service start hint, or null Nothing was paid. |
| `service-not-ready` | null: try again in a moment Nothing was paid. |
| `approval-revoked` | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` A deposit may be open: `<cli> agent down --yes` closes it. |
| `not-enough-tdvpn` | `send tDVPN to the wallet address (<cli> agent status shows it), then <cli> agent up --yes` (here the sentence is in `error` and `action` is null) Nothing was paid. |
| `session-active` | `<cli> disconnect`, then `<cli> agent up --yes` (when the service itself reports the live session; the row above is the answer to a connect `agent up` started) Nothing was paid. |
| `rpc-unavailable`, `rpc-ws` | `<cli> daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes (the VPN service's Solana connection), then <cli> agent up --yes` (rc.7; was the RPC hint) It is not known whether a deposit was opened: `<cli> agent status` lists it. |

### Usage (exit 3) and confirm (exit 2)

Exit 3, nothing ran: `--basis must be per_gb or per_hour`, `--units must be a whole number from 1 to 1000`,
`--protocol must be any, …`, `--country must be a two-letter country code, e.g. DE`, `--max-price: …`,
an unknown flag, `unknown: agent <x> (up | down | status)`. Exit 2: `up` or `down` without `--yes` (above).

# file: docs/CODES.md

# Failure codes: what each one means, whether money moved, what to run

Every `code` an agent can get from `devnet-dvpn agent status | up | down`, and from the follow-up
commands those answers tell it to run (`settle`, `device`, `wallet`). One row per code, four answers each:

- **Meaning**: what happened, in plain words.
- **Money moved?**: the `money` field of the `{ok:false}` line, by class. `none` = nothing was paid.
  `open` = a deposit may be open. `unclear` = the code does not say. `refund` = no new spend, but a refund
  is still held. Only `agent`, `connect`, `switch` and `test` failures carry `money`. On other commands
  this column says `no field` and then gives the true state.
- **Next**: the `action` the line carries (`<cli>` = `devnet-dvpn`, or `DVPN_CLI_NAME`). Run it as printed.
- **alsoNext**: the other way out. Only `agent status` prints an `alsoNext` field. On a failure line this
  column is this page's fallback for when **Next** does not work.

Source of truth: the `devnet-dvpn` app at 0.3.0-rc.7 (`8f458d71`), traced from `src/cli/agent-cmd.ts`.
`tools/check-glossary.mjs --src <devnet-dvpn checkout>` fails when a code those paths can return has no
row here, or when a row's money class differs from `src/cli/money-note.ts`.

**An open deposit wins over the code (E-22).** After a failed `agent up` past the check before paying,
if a deposit is open with that node, `action` is always
`a deposit of X tDVPN is open with this node (<channel>): <cli> agent up --yes picks another node (this node is skipped), or <cli> agent down --yes closes it and refunds the unused part …`,
whatever the code. The rows below give `action` for when no deposit is open.

## agent up: refused by agent-cmd itself

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-no-wallet"></a>`no-wallet` | No wallet in this CLI: no key file named, none in the vault. | `none` | `<cli> wallet create --keyfile <path> --yes, then fund the address it prints`. When this computer has a device record: `<cli> wallet import <the key file of <owner>, the wallet that set up this computer's device>, then <cli> agent up --yes (a new wallet would not hold its funds)` | `<cli> agent status` (shows `address: null`) |
| <a id="code-keyfile-missing"></a>`keyfile-missing` | The key file that `--keyfile` or `DVPN_KEYFILE` names is gone. Not "no wallet": the funds stay with the lost key. | `none` | `restore the key file named in "error" from your backup (it is the only key to this wallet), then <cli> agent up --yes` | none: never `wallet create` (a new wallet holds none of the funds) |
| <a id="code-keyfile-mode"></a>`keyfile-mode` | rc.7. The key file can be read by other users (its mode is in `error`). Refused before anything is read or paid. Exit 4: a person fixes it. | `none` | `chmod 600 <the key file>, then <cli> agent up --yes` | none |
| <a id="code-no-device"></a>`no-device` | `daemon init` could not create this computer's device key. | `none` | `<cli> daemon doctor` | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` |
| <a id="code-no-subscription"></a>`no-subscription` | `--plan` names a subscription this wallet does not hold, or one that is not active. | `none` | `<cli> plans list, then <cli> plans subscribe <plan> --yes` | `<cli> agent up --yes` without `--plan` (pays a deposit) |
| <a id="code-no-nodes"></a>`no-nodes` | No online node matches `--protocol` / `--country` / `--max-price` / `--node` (or the plan's live roster). Under `--max-price` (rc7) the message names the cheapest matching price above it. | `none` | Under `--max-price` with a match above it (rc7): `<cli> agent up [--protocol <p>] [--country <c>] --basis <b> --units <n> --max-price <the cheapest price> --yes` (runnable as printed). Otherwise: `<cli> nodes list --online --json, then widen --protocol / --country / --max-price` | `<cli> agent up --basis <the other one> --yes` |
| <a id="code-not-funded"></a>`not-funded` | The wallet holds less than 0.06 SOL (rc7; 0.02 before) before its first connect, or less tDVPN than the deposit shown. rc7 names the exact shortfall and, when larger, a recommended amount that also covers a reconnect. | `none` | `send at least <n> SOL and/or <n> tDVPN (<m> recommended: it also covers a reconnect) to <address>, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent up --units <fewer> --yes` (a smaller deposit) |
| <a id="code-price-cap"></a>`price-cap` | rc.6 and later. With no `--max-price` and no `--plan`, the deposit (price × units) is above the default cap, `defaults.priceCap` in the preview. rc7: the larger of the spending limit / 10 and the p75 price of the matching online nodes × `--units`, never above the limit; with fewer than 3 priced nodes, the limit / 10 (rc.6: always the limit / 10). The message names the node's price and the `--max-price` that accepts it. This applies to the quick pick and to `--node`. Refused before paying. | `none` | `<cli> agent up --node <node> --basis <b> --units <n> --max-price <its price> --yes (you accept this price), or fewer --units, or another node` | `<cli> agent up --units <fewer> --yes` |
| <a id="code-node-refused"></a>`node-refused` | The connect failed with no specific code after the deposit opened (E-37). The node refused after it was paid. It is skipped next time. | `open` | the open-deposit sentence above | `<cli> agent down --yes` (closes it, refunds the unused part) |
| <a id="code-connect-failed"></a>`connect-failed` | `connect()` failed and gave no code, with no deposit open. | `unclear` | `<cli> agent status` (read `error`) | `<cli> agent down --yes` (closes any deposit that is open) |

## agent up: from connect()

`action` = `nextFor(code)`. Each code here is in `CONNECT_CODES` (`src/core/session/state.ts`).
`tests/unit/connect-codes.test.ts` fails when the connect path answers a code outside that list.
A spending-limit shortfall, whatever its code, answers the `spending-limit` command.

### Refused before anything starts

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-not-confirmed"></a>`not-confirmed` | The connect was asked without `--yes`. `agent up` itself always passes the confirm, so this comes only from a direct `connect`. | `none` | `<cli> agent up --yes (add --yes: nothing is paid without it)` | none |
| <a id="code-wallet-switch-needed"></a>`wallet-switch-needed` | This computer is set up for another wallet, so the loaded key cannot pay here. Comes from `connect()` only, so `agent up` only. | `none` | `load the key file of the wallet named in "error", or <cli> device switch --yes (sets this computer up for the loaded wallet; the other wallet's deposits stay refundable)` | `<cli> agent status` (names the loaded address) |
| <a id="code-clock-skew"></a>`clock-skew` | This computer's clock is off by N minutes. Refused before any deposit. | `none` | `set this computer's clock to the right time (it is off by about N minutes), then <cli> agent up --yes` | none |
| <a id="code-device-permission"></a>`device-permission` | This computer has no spending permission, or the permission or wallet switch could not be set up. | `none` | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| <a id="code-plan-limit"></a>`plan-limit` | The plan does not allow a new node here. | `none` | `<cli> agent up --plan <subscription> --node <a node you already use> --yes` | `<cli> agent up --yes` without `--plan` (pays a deposit) |
| <a id="code-busy"></a>`busy` | Another connect was already running. | `none` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a few seconds (another connect was running)` | `<cli> agent status` |
| <a id="code-test-running"></a>`test-running` | A node test holds the VPN service. | `none` | `<cli> test stop, then <cli> agent up --yes` | none |
| <a id="code-unsupported"></a>`unsupported` | This system cannot do what was asked. | `none` | `<cli> agent status` (read `error`) | none |
| <a id="code-daemon-missing"></a>`daemon-missing` | The VPN service is not installed. | `none` | Linux/macOS: `<cli> daemon install --yes (administrator/root once: passwordless sudo, or a person types the password), then <cli> agent up --yes`. Windows: `<cli> daemon install --yes from an elevated shell or an administrator SSH login (a normal shell shows a UAC prompt an agent cannot answer), then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| <a id="code-daemon-relogin"></a>`daemon-relogin` | The service does not accept this account yet (Windows: the service pipe has not been granted to this account). | `none` | as `daemon-missing` (Windows: `… once from an elevated shell …`) | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| <a id="code-daemon-restarting"></a>`daemon-restarting` | The VPN service is restarting. | `none` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a few seconds (the VPN service is restarting); if it keeps failing, <cli> daemon doctor` | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| <a id="code-daemon-unavailable"></a>`daemon-unavailable` | The VPN service does not answer. | `none` | `<cli> daemon doctor` | `<cli> daemon install --yes` (administrator once) |
| <a id="code-network-mismatch"></a>`network-mismatch` | The installed service is for another network. | `none` | `<cli> daemon install --yes (administrator once: it installs the service for this network), then <cli> agent up --yes` | none |

### The check before paying (nothing has been paid for any of these)

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-session-active"></a>`session-active` | A VPN session is already running (from the command line or another window). | `none` | `<cli> agent down --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent status` |
| <a id="code-node-gone"></a><a id="code-node-stale"></a><a id="code-node-offline"></a>`node-gone`, `node-stale`, `node-offline` | The node is no longer listed, has not checked in recently, or did not answer its probe. | `none` | `<cli> nodes list --online --json, then <cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` | `<cli> agent up --yes` (the quick pick skips it for 10 min) |
| <a id="code-protocol-blocked"></a>`protocol-blocked` | The kill switch blocks this protocol here. | `none` | `<cli> daemon drivers (it lists the protocols ready on this computer), then <cli> agent up --protocol <another ready one> --yes` | `<cli> daemon restore-network` |
| <a id="code-driver-missing"></a>`driver-missing` | A network adapter or protocol program is missing from this computer. | `none` | `<cli> daemon repair-drivers --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent up --protocol <another ready one> --yes` |
| <a id="code-basis-unavailable"></a>`basis-unavailable` | The node does not sell per GB, or does not sell per hour. | `none` | `<cli> agent up --basis <the other one: per_gb or per_hour> --yes` | `<cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` |
| <a id="code-not-enough-tdvpn"></a>`not-enough-tdvpn` | The wallet holds too little tDVPN for this deposit. | `none` | `send tDVPN to the wallet address (<cli> agent status shows it), then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent up --units <fewer> --yes` |
| <a id="code-spending-limit"></a>`spending-limit` | The spending approval or device limit is below this deposit. On `agent up --yes` without `--raise-limit` (rc.6 and later) nothing is paid; the message names the limit, the deposit and the raised limit. | `none` | `<cli> agent up --node <node> [--protocol <p>] --basis <b> --units <n> [--max-price <m>] --raise-limit --yes`: your own line, pinned to the node `agent up` picked, every flag you gave kept (E-88). From `connect()` (no `--raise-limit` path): `<cli> device setup --allowance <N> --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent up --units <fewer> --yes` |
| <a id="code-device-sol"></a>`device-sol` | The device or wallet is out of SOL for network fees. | `none` | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` | send SOL to the wallet address, then `<cli> agent up --yes` |
| <a id="code-preflight"></a>`preflight` | A blocker with no code of its own. When it carries an app button ("Open diagnostics", "Open settings", "Repair drivers"), `action` is that button's command followed by `, then <cli> agent up --yes`. "Pick another server" gives the `node-gone` command. | `none` | `read "error": it names what to change (nothing was paid), then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent status` |
| <a id="code-kill-switch-held"></a>`kill-switch-held` | The kill switch still blocks the internet and lets through only the last node. | `none` | `<cli> daemon restore-network, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-switch-reconnecting"></a>`switch-reconnecting` | A node switch was asked while the session is reconnecting. | `none` | `<cli> agent status until "connected" is true, or <cli> agent down --yes first` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-price-changed"></a>`price-changed` | The node's price rose above the deposit `agent up` showed. | `none` | `<cli> agent up --yes again (nothing was paid; it reads the price fresh)` | `<cli> agent up --max-price <cap> --yes` |
| <a id="code-deposit-unusable"></a>`deposit-unusable` | Your open deposit with this node has started closing, so it cannot be used, and a new deposit is never paid without being shown. | `none` | as `price-changed` | `<cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` |
| <a id="code-deposits-unread"></a>`deposits-unread` | Your open deposits could not be read, so no second deposit was opened beside one you may already have. | `none` | as `price-changed` | `<cli> agent status` (lists `deposits`) |

### After the start was asked of the service (a deposit may be open)

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-switch-offline"></a>`switch-offline` | A switch failed with the old session gone. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a moment` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-cancelled"></a>`cancelled` | The connect was stopped before it finished. The unused part of a sent deposit is refunded. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again (it was stopped before it finished)` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-waiting-for-network"></a>`waiting-for-network` | The service has no network yet. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute (this computer has no network yet)` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-ticket-other-owner"></a>`ticket-other-owner` | The plan access belongs to another wallet than this computer's. | `open` | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-approval-revoked"></a>`approval-revoked` | This wallet's spending approval for this computer was revoked. | `open` | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-service-stopped-connecting"></a>`service-stopped-connecting` | The service stopped while connecting. With the kill switch on, the internet stays blocked. | `open` | `<cli> quality ip; if it shows no address, <cli> daemon restore-network; then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-node-identity"></a><a id="code-node-ledger"></a>`node-identity`, `node-ledger` | The node failed its identity check, or billed more than this device measured. | `open` | `<cli> nodes list --online --json, then <cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-node-price"></a>`node-price` | The node's price does not match the deposit. | `open` | `<cli> agent down --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes (a new deposit)` | `<cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` |
| <a id="code-node-error"></a>`node-error` | The node had a problem starting the session. The deposit is kept for the next try. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-kill-switch-failed"></a>`kill-switch-failed` | The service could not turn on the kill switch, so it stopped. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again, or <cli> daemon set --kill-switch off --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-tunnel-failed"></a><a id="code-tunnel-dead"></a><a id="code-tunnel-mtu"></a><a id="code-port-in-use"></a>`tunnel-failed`, `tunnel-dead`, `tunnel-mtu`, `port-in-use` | The tunnel did not come up, carries no traffic, hits packet-size drops, or its port is taken. | `open` | `<cli> daemon drivers (it lists the protocols ready on this computer), then <cli> agent up --protocol <another ready one> --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-tunnel-closing"></a>`tunnel-closing` | The previous node's tunnel is still closing. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a few seconds` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-dns-apply"></a>`dns-apply` | The VPN's DNS could not be applied. | `open` | `<cli> daemon set --dns-mode none --yes (the VPN's DNS off), then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-protocol-missing"></a>`protocol-missing` | The node's protocol program is not on this computer. The deposit is kept. | `open` | `<cli> daemon drivers (it lists the protocols ready on this computer), then <cli> agent up --protocol <a ready one> --yes; or <cli> daemon repair-drivers --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` (refunds it) |
| <a id="code-deposit-pending"></a>`deposit-pending` | The deposit is still being confirmed. It is never paid twice. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a few minutes (it never pays twice)` | `<cli> agent status` |
| <a id="code-rpc-network"></a><a id="code-rpc-quota"></a>`rpc-network`, `rpc-quota` | The network intercepts Solana RPC (login page, proxy, filter), or the service's RPC quota ran out. | `open` | `<cli> daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes (the VPN service's Solana connection), then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-rpc-timeout"></a>`rpc-timeout` | The service's RPC endpoint did not answer in time. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute; if it keeps failing, <cli> daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes (the VPN service's Solana connection), then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-rpc-busy"></a>`rpc-busy` | The RPC endpoint is rate-limiting. | `unclear` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute (the network was busy)` | `<cli> agent status` (lists any deposit) |
| <a id="code-rpc-ws"></a>`rpc-ws` | rc.7. The service could not keep its Solana websocket (the RPC pair's ws side). Exit 6. | `unclear` | `<cli> daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes (the VPN service's Solana connection), then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent status` (lists any deposit) |
| <a id="code-timeout"></a>`timeout` | The node did not answer in time. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a moment` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-chain-encoding"></a>`chain-encoding` | The network program rejected the payment transaction. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --basis per_hour --yes (pay per hour instead)` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |

### A node's own refusal (it comes after the deposit)

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-peer_limit_reached"></a><a id="code-terms_rejected"></a>`peer_limit_reached`, `terms_rejected` | The node is full, or refused the terms. | `open` | `<cli> nodes list --online --json, then <cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-credit_exhausted"></a><a id="code-lease_insufficient"></a><a id="code-voucher_exceeds_escrow"></a><a id="code-voucher_signature_invalid"></a>`credit_exhausted`, `lease_insufficient`, `voucher_exceeds_escrow`, `voucher_signature_invalid` | The deposit ran out or no longer covers the session. | `open` | `<cli> agent down --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes (a new deposit)` | `<cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` |
| <a id="code-subscription_invalid"></a>`subscription_invalid` | The plan subscription is not valid at this node. | `open` | `<cli> plans subscriptions, then <cli> agent up --plan <an active one> --yes, or <cli> agent up --yes without --plan` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-ticket_request_stale"></a><a id="code-ticket_invalid"></a><a id="code-channel_node_reopened"></a>`ticket_request_stale`, `ticket_invalid`, `channel_node_reopened` | A ticket or channel race. Usually passes on a retry. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a moment` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-provider_unreachable"></a>`provider_unreachable` | The plan provider did not answer. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute (the plan provider did not answer)` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-rate_limited"></a>`rate_limited` | The node is rate-limiting. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --yes again in a minute` | `<cli> agent up --node <another node> --yes` |
| <a id="code-unauthorized"></a>`unauthorized` | The node refused the device. A wrong clock causes this too (E-22). | `open` | `<cli> device show --json: if the grant is there and not revoked, set this computer's clock to the right time (a wrong clock makes the node refuse), then <cli> agent up --yes; otherwise <cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-cannot cover the prepay"></a>`cannot cover the prepay` | The deposit is below the node's minimum. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --units <more> --yes (a deposit large enough for the node's minimum)` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-mode_not_voucher"></a>`mode_not_voucher` | The node does not take per-GB vouchers. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --basis per_hour --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-mode_not_stream"></a>`mode_not_stream` | The node does not take per-hour streams. | `open` | `<cli> agent up --basis per_gb --yes` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |

### Leaving, and the catch-all

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-stop-failed"></a>`stop-failed` | Stopping the previous session failed during a switch. The internet may not work. | `open` | `<cli> daemon doctor, then <cli> agent up --yes` | `<cli> daemon restore-network` |
| <a id="code-dns-revert-failed"></a><a id="code-tunnel-left"></a>`dns-revert-failed`, `tunnel-left` | DNS or a tunnel was left behind. | `open` | `<cli> daemon restore-network` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| <a id="code-unknown"></a>`unknown` | Nothing more specific is known. | `unclear` | `<cli> agent status` (read `error`) | `<cli> agent down --yes` (closes any open deposit) |

## agent down

`agent down` runs `disconnect` and then one `settle run`. If the disconnect fails, nothing is settled.

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `no-wallet` | This CLI has no wallet, so it cannot read or close deposits. Nothing ran. | `none` | `<cli> disconnect to leave the VPN now; <cli> wallet import <file> (the wallet that paid), then <cli> agent down --yes to close the deposits` | `<cli> disconnect` (needs no wallet) |
| `keyfile-missing` | The named key file is gone. Nothing ran. | `none` | `<cli> disconnect to leave the VPN now; restore the key file named in "error" from your backup (it is the only key to this wallet), then <cli> agent down --yes` | `<cli> disconnect` |
| `stop-failed` | The disconnect failed with no plainer code. No deposit was closed, and a per-hour deposit keeps billing while the session is up. | `open` | `<cli> daemon doctor, then <cli> agent down --yes again` | `<cli> daemon restore-network` |
| `dns-revert-failed` | The session **did** stop, but DNS could not be restored. On rc5 the message still begins "Could not disconnect, so no deposit was closed". The first half is wrong; the second is right, because the settle step did not run. rc.6: "The session stopped, but this computer's DNS could not be put back. No deposit was closed yet." | `open` | rc5: `<cli> daemon doctor, then <cli> agent down --yes again` (the second `agent down` finds no session and closes the deposits). rc.6: `<cli> daemon restore-network, then <cli> agent down --yes again (it closes the deposits)` | `<cli> daemon restore-network` (the fix for the DNS) |
| <a id="code-service-down"></a><a id="code-service-not-ready"></a><a id="code-rpc-unavailable"></a>`service-down`, `service-not-ready`, `rpc-unavailable` | The disconnect failed in the VPN service, or on every RPC endpoint (plain copy; see "Any of the three" below). No deposit was closed. | `none` / `none` / `unclear` | `<cli> daemon doctor, then <cli> agent down --yes again` | `<cli> daemon restore-network` |
| `approval-revoked`, `not-enough-tdvpn`, `session-active` | Plain copy of a service error. With the disconnect these mean a service fault. No deposit was closed. | `open` / `none` / `none` | `<cli> daemon doctor, then <cli> agent down --yes again` | `<cli> disconnect` |
| `busy` | Disconnected, but another refund run in this process held the lock, so nothing was closed. A per-hour deposit bills until closed. | `none` | `<cli> settle run --yes` | `<cli> settle list` |
| <a id="code-settle-failed"></a>`settle-failed` | Disconnected. Some deposits could not be refunded yet; the others are done. | `refund` | `<cli> settle list` | `<cli> settle run --yes` |
| <a id="code-daemon-gone"></a>`daemon-gone` | Disconnected, but the VPN service stopped during the refund. Nothing was lost, and the settle runs again later. | `unclear` on rc5 (unclassified; the true state is refund) · rc.6: `refund` | `<cli> settle list` | `<cli> settle run --yes` |

A successful `agent down` whose deposits another device of this wallet opened (E-72) is `ok: true` with `notClosed` and
`warning`. Its `next` is `<cli> device revoke --device <D> --yes (if it is not revoked yet), then <cli> settle run --device <D> --yes`.

## agent status

`agent status` reads only and never fails with a code of its own. Its one code is a field on an `ok: true` answer:

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-server-stopped"></a>`server-stopped` | The node stopped serving. The exit address is this computer's own, or the daemon ended the session in the last 30 min. `connected: false`. The deposit is safe. | `open` (no `money` field: `ok` is true) | `<cli> agent up --yes` (the dead node is skipped for 10 min). With `blocked`: `<cli> daemon restore-network (lifts the block; then <cli> agent up --yes to reconnect, or <cli> agent down --yes)` | `<cli> agent down --yes` (an `alsoNext` field) |

## Any of the three: replaced on the way out

`index.ts` (`plainError`) replaces a raw service or RPC failure with the shared copy. This happens for any
throw that `agent-cmd` did not turn into its own code: for example, the wallet or node read before `agent up`,
or the deposit read in `agent down`.

| Code | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `service-down` | The VPN service is off. | `none` | the service start hint, or null | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| `service-not-ready` | The service is starting or stopping. | `none` | null: run the same command again in a moment | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| `rpc-unavailable` | Every RPC endpoint failed (rate limit, not a Solana RPC endpoint, or a timeout). | `unclear` | the RPC hint (check the network, or set another RPC) | `<cli> daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes` |
| `approval-revoked` | The spending approval for this computer was revoked. | `open` | `devnet-dvpn device setup --yes` | `<cli> agent status` |
| `not-enough-tdvpn` | The wallet lacks tDVPN for the deposit. | `none` | null: fund the wallet or use fewer `--units` | `<cli> agent status` (shows the address) |
| `session-active` | A session is already active. | `none` | `devnet-dvpn disconnect` | `<cli> agent down --yes` |
| (`code: null`) | A throw with no code (e.g. the key store locked over SSH, E-66). | `unclear` | null: read `error` | `<cli> agent status` |

Exit 2 (`needsConfirm: true`) and exit 3 (usage) carry no `code`. See `docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md`.

## Follow-up commands the answers name

These are not `agent` commands, so they carry **no `money` field**. The column gives the true state.

| Code | From | Meaning | Money moved? | Next (`action`) | alsoNext |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `no-wallet` | `settle list / run / withdraw`, `device switch` | No wallet in this CLI. | `no field`: nothing ran | none (the message says `wallet create` or `wallet import <file>`) | import the wallet that paid, then run it again |
| `keyfile-missing` | same | The named key file is gone. | `no field`: nothing ran | none: restore the file from your backup | none |
| `busy` | `settle run` | Another refund run in this process. | `no field`: nothing closed | none: run `<cli> settle run --yes` again | `<cli> settle list` |
| `settle-failed` | `settle run` | Some deposits could not be refunded yet; the others are done. | `no field`: refund still held | none: `<cli> settle run --yes` again later | `<cli> settle list` |
| `daemon-gone` | `settle run` | The VPN service stopped during the refund. Nothing was lost. | `no field`: refund still held | none: `<cli> settle run --yes` again | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| <a id="code-withdraw-failed"></a>`withdraw-failed` | `settle withdraw` | The withdraw transaction failed. A zero balance is not this code: it prints "Nothing to withdraw" with exit 0. | `no field`: balance still held | none: `<cli> settle withdraw --yes` again | `<cli> settle list` |
| <a id="code-no-device-key"></a>`no-device-key` | `device setup` (rc.6) | `device setup` ran before `daemon init`. On rc5 this was the same sentence with `code: null`. | `no field`: nothing signed | none: the message says `devnet-dvpn daemon init`, then `device setup` again | `<cli> agent status` |
| <a id="code-wallet-is-device"></a>`wallet-is-device` | `device setup` | The wallet and the device key are the same key. | `no field`: nothing signed | none: use a separate wallet key | `<cli> device show --json` |
| <a id="code-device-setup-failed"></a>`device-setup-failed` | `device setup` | The setup transaction failed. | `no field`: nothing set up (a SOL top-up may have landed) | none: run `device setup --yes` again | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| `device-permission`, `device-sol` | `device switch` | The switch could not finish (read, stage or service step), or the wallet lacks SOL for it. This computer stays set up for the other wallet. | `no field`: nothing paid | the app's button as a command, or none | send SOL, then `<cli> device switch --yes` |
| <a id="code-switch-failed"></a>`switch-failed` | `device switch` | The switch failed with no code. | `no field`: nothing paid | none | `<cli> daemon doctor` |
| <a id="code-revoke-failed"></a>`revoke-failed` | `device revoke [--device D]` | The revoke transaction failed. | `no field`: nothing changed | none: run it again | `<cli> device show --json` |
| <a id="code-bad-device"></a><a id="code-own-device"></a>`bad-device`, `own-device` | `device revoke --device D` | `D` is not a device address, or it is this computer's own device. | `no field`: nothing ran | none: `device revoke` without `--device` for this computer | `<cli> device show --json` |
| <a id="code-device-key-unreadable"></a>`device-key-unreadable` | `device register` | The service's key folder is admin-only. | `no field`: nothing ran | the `device register <address>` form (no administrator needed) | none |
| <a id="code-invalid-address"></a><a id="code-invalid-amount"></a><a id="code-send-failed"></a>`invalid-address`, `invalid-amount`, `send-failed` | `wallet send` | Bad recipient, bad amount, or a failed transfer. | `no field`: nothing sent (`send-failed`: check the wallet) | none | `<cli> agent status` (balances) |

`settle run --device <this computer's device>`, the daemon commands, and (rc5 only) `device setup` with no
device key yet fail with `code: null` and a plain sentence that names the fix.

## Other commands: rc.7 codes (every failure has one)

rc.7 (R2) gives every failure outside `agent` that used to be a bare `code: null` a code and an `action`
(`cliErr` in `src/cli/cli-fail.ts`). None of them pays, so the class is `none` (money-note.ts) and the exit is 1.
Only `test` failures print a `money` field; the others carry none.

| Code | From | Meaning | Exit | Money moved? | Next (`action`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-device-home-gone"></a>`device-home-gone` | `device setup` | The VPN service's home folder (its device key and settings) is gone. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> daemon install --yes` |
| <a id="code-no-plan"></a>`no-plan` | `plans roster <plan>` | No plan with that id on devnet. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> plans list` |
| <a id="code-driver-repair-failed"></a>`driver-repair-failed` | `daemon repair-drivers` | The driver repair did not finish; `error` holds its log. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> daemon doctor --json` |
| <a id="code-migrate-failed"></a>`migrate-failed` | `daemon migrate` | The upgrade of the VPN service home stopped at the step named in `error`. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> daemon doctor --json` |
| <a id="code-device-not-ready"></a>`device-not-ready` | `daemon install` | The device is not funded and permitted yet, so the service will not start. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> device setup --yes, then <cli> daemon install --yes` |
| <a id="code-install-failed"></a>`install-failed` | `daemon install` | The service install failed; `error` says where. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> daemon doctor --json` |
| <a id="code-daemon-settings-empty"></a>`daemon-settings-empty` | `daemon set` | The service's settings file is empty. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> daemon install --yes` |
| <a id="code-daemon-settings-unreadable"></a>`daemon-settings-unreadable` | `daemon set` | The service's settings file cannot be read (a missing file is `daemon-missing`). | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> daemon install --yes` |
| <a id="code-dns-no-answer"></a>`dns-no-answer` | `daemon dns-check` | The DNS check got no answer. Exit 1 on purpose, so a script can gate on it. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> daemon doctor --json` |
| <a id="code-uninstall-failed"></a>`uninstall-failed` | `daemon uninstall` | The service uninstall failed; `error` says where. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> daemon doctor --json` |
| <a id="code-checks-off"></a>`checks-off` | `quality` (ip, dns, …) | Third-party checks are turned off in settings. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> settings set thirdPartyChecks=true` |
| <a id="code-test-plan-failed"></a>`test-plan-failed` | `test run` | The test run could not be planned (`error` says why). Nothing was opened. | 1 | `none` | `<cli> test servers` |
| <a id="code-no-test-run"></a>`no-test-run` | `test show / export [<run>]` | No test run with that id, or none yet. | 1 | `none` | `<cli> test history` |
| <a id="code-keystore-unavailable"></a>`keystore-unavailable` | `wallet create / import` (Windows) | Windows cannot encrypt a wallet for this logon (no password session, e.g. an SSH key login), or the encryption failed. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `<cli> wallet create --keyfile <path> --yes` |
| <a id="code-keyfile-read-only"></a>`keyfile-read-only` | `wallet create / import / remove` | A `--keyfile` / `DVPN_KEYFILE` wallet is read-only: this CLI never writes or deletes it. | 1 | `no field`: nothing paid | `unset DVPN_KEYFILE, then run the command again` |

Also coded in rc.7 by `cliErr`, with rows above: `rpc-busy` (`wallet show`), `no-device` (`device switch`),
`no-device-key` (`device setup`, `daemon init`), `no-wallet` and `daemon-missing` (`daemon install` / `set`), `no-nodes` (`test run`),
`node-gone` (`nodes show / probe <node>`), `driver-missing` (`daemon drivers`).

## Path B (`direct/*.sh`): codes only the scripts print

The scripts use the app's code names where a twin exists (`docs/DIRECT.md`, the Path B → Path A table).
These are the codes that exist only on Path B. Their anchors carry `direct-` so they never clash with an app
code of the same name (`install-failed`, `no-device`). Every line has `money` and `moneyNote`
(`direct/lib.sh`) and matches `direct/schema/failure.json`.

| Code | Script | Meaning | Exit | Money moved? | Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="code-direct-download-failed"></a>`download-failed` | `install.sh` | `apt-get update` or the release download (`SHA256SUMS`, a binary) failed. | 6 | `none` | `sleep 60 && sudo sh direct/install.sh` |
| <a id="code-direct-install-failed"></a>`install-failed` | `install.sh` | A setup step failed: the packages, copying a binary, `sentinel-dvpnd init`, the kill-switch setting, the service, or adding you to the group. `error` names the step. | 1 | `none` | the step's own command, then `sudo sh direct/install.sh` |
| <a id="code-direct-build-failed"></a>`build-failed` | `install.sh` (`BUILD=1`) | `direct/build.sh` failed. A wrong checksum is `checksum-mismatch`, not this. | 1 | `none` | `sh direct/build.sh` (needs git, make and Go 1.27.3) |
| <a id="code-direct-no-device"></a>`no-device` | any script after install | The daemon has no device key: `install.sh` did not finish. | 1 | `none` | `sudo sh direct/install.sh` |
| <a id="code-direct-route-failed"></a>`route-failed` | `connect.sh` | The route that keeps the node's own IP outside the tunnel could not be added (no default route, or `ip route replace` failed). | 1 | `none` | `ip route show default`, or the exact `sudo ip route replace …` line |
| <a id="code-direct-session-dropped"></a>`session-dropped` | `selftest.sh` | The session dropped during the hold. | 1 | `refund` | `sh direct/disconnect.sh && sh direct/refund.sh` |
| <a id="code-direct-step-failed"></a>`step-failed` | `selftest.sh` | A script the selftest ran stopped with no JSON line. When the script did print one, the selftest passes on its code instead. | 1 | the step's, else `none` | `sh direct/<script>.sh` |
| <a id="code-direct-interrupted"></a>`interrupted` | any (lib.sh EXIT backstop) | The script was killed (exit 130 / 143) before it printed its line. | 1 | `MONEY_STATE`: how far it got (`none`, `unclear` before the session starts, `open` after) | the same command again (it is safe to repeat: `docs/DIRECT.md`, "Safe to run again?") |
| <a id="code-direct-unknown"></a>`unknown` | any (lib.sh EXIT backstop) | A `set -e` stop with no code of its own; `error` names the last command run. | 1 | `MONEY_STATE`, as above | `none`: the failure table in `docs/DIRECT.md`; otherwise `sh direct/refund.sh` |

## rc.6 and later: exit codes and changed answers

This applies when `devnet-dvpn version --json` says `0.3.0-rc.6` or newer (released; rc7 = `8f458d71`). Every row
above still holds, apart from the changes listed here.

**Exit codes by class** (`src/cli/exit-codes.ts`). The `code` field stays the precise reason.

| Exit | Class | Codes |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | ok | none |
| 1 | error | any code not listed below, and `code: null`. Includes `rpc-timeout`, `rpc-network`, `rpc-quota` and `timeout`: network codes whose money class is `open` (a deposit may be open) |
| 2 | needs `--yes` | no code (`needsConfirm: true`) |
| 3 | wrong usage | no code |
| 4 | needs you or your operator | `not-funded`, `spending-limit`, `price-cap`, `no-wallet`, and since rc7 `keyfile-missing` and `keyfile-mode` (rc.6: exit 1) |
| 5 | refused for safety | `kill-switch-held` (money `none`), `kill-switch-failed` (money `open`: read `money`), and `kill-switch` |
| 6 | network or RPC, no deposit possibly open: retry later | `rpc-busy`, `rpc-unavailable` (money `unclear`), and `rpc-ws` |

Exit 6 is given only to a network code whose money class is not `open` (`exitCodeFor`: `moneyOf(code) !== 'open'`).
A network failure after which a deposit may be open exits 1. Exit 5 can still follow an open deposit
(`kill-switch-failed`). On any non-zero exit, read `money` before you retry.

**Changed answers:**
- `spending-limit` on `agent up --yes`: with the limit below the deposit and no `--raise-limit`, the
  answer is a refusal with nothing paid. `action` = `<cli> agent up --node <node> --basis <b> --units <n> --raise-limit --yes`.
  rc5 raised the limit inside `--yes` and said so in `limitRaised`.
- `node-refused` and `connect-failed`: "Something went wrong" no longer reaches the agent. With a deposit
  open: "The node did not start the session after your deposit was paid … The deposit is safe". Without
  one: "Connect failed for a reason this app does not name … Nothing was paid", pointing to `<cli> logs --lines 80`.
- New code `price-cap` (see its row under "agent up: refused by agent-cmd itself"): a default deposit cap
  when `--max-price` is not given; rc.6 = the Settings limit / 10, rc7 = market-sized (`defaults.priceCap`).
- rc7: every failure carries `next` (the same as `action`) and `docUrl` (this page, `#code-<code>`).
- `dns-revert-failed` on `agent down`: see its row.
- `daemon-gone`: money class `refund`.
- `agent status` with the service down and no device yet (E-84): `next` is the service install
  (`daemon-missing`), not `agent up --yes`.
- Amounts gain base-unit siblings: `solLamports`, `tdvpnBase`, `heldBase`, `spentBase` (status);
  `spentBase`, `refundableBase` (down); `deposit.tdvpnBase` (up).
- `version --json` adds `programId` and `mint` (E-81).

# file: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md

# Troubleshooting: symptom → cause → command

For `devnet-dvpn` v0.3.0-rc7, macOS v0.3.0-rc4 ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md); older releases: [`OLDER-RELEASES.md`](OLDER-RELEASES.md)). Every `code` here is a real one; its full row
(meaning, whether money moved, next, the other way out) is in [`CODES.md`](CODES.md). Terms:
[`GLOSSARY.md`](../GLOSSARY.md).

First, always:

```sh
devnet-dvpn agent status --json      # read "next" (and "alsoNext"); run it as printed
```

A failure line `{"ok":false,…}` carries `action` (rc7: `next`, the same line): run it. `money` says whether money moved; `docUrl` links the code's row. Use this page when
`action` is null, or when the symptom has no code.

| Symptom | Cause | Command |
|---|---|---|
| `agent up` connected but `exitIp` is `null` | The address check did not finish within 8 s. The tunnel may be fine. | `devnet-dvpn quality ip --json`: `direct.ip` (whole-device protocols) or `viaSocks.ip` (V2Ray / Xray on Linux) must differ from your own address. |
| `exitIp` (or `quality ip`) shows your **own** address while `connected` is true | The node stopped serving; for a few seconds `agent status` can still say `connected`. Then it answers `"code":"server-stopped"`. The deposit is safe. | `devnet-dvpn agent up --yes` (another node; the dead one is skipped 10 min), or `devnet-dvpn agent down --yes` (closes the deposit). With `"blocked": true` as well: `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network` first (`next`), then one of those two (`alsoNext`). |
| `quality ip` shows **no** address after `agent down`, or `agent status` says `"blocked": true` | The kill switch still holds the block (the session had dropped before you disconnected). | `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network` (now), then `devnet-dvpn daemon set --kill-switch off --yes` (so it does not come back). Or `devnet-dvpn agent up --yes` to reconnect with protection. rc7: with no session, `next` is that `agent up --yes` and `alsoNext` is `daemon restore-network`. |
| `agent status` says `"reconnecting": true` (rc7) | The live session dropped and is reconnecting; the kill switch blocks the internet meanwhile (`connected` false, `blocked` true). The deposit stays open. | Wait a minute and run `agent status --json` again, or run `next` (`devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network`) to go direct now; `alsoNext` names reconnect / close. |
| `agent status` `next` is `devnet-dvpn agent up` with no `--yes` (rc7) | The device has no spending permission left, or the wallet holds under 1 tDVPN (with `held`). | Run it as printed: the preview pays nothing and names what is missing (funding or a limit), then follow its `next`. |
| `"code":"kill-switch-held"` on `agent up` | The block lets through only the last node, so this connect cannot lift it. Nothing was paid. | `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network, then devnet-dvpn agent up --yes` |
| SSH session lost after a connect or after turning the kill switch on | The kill switch blocks everything that is not the tunnel; over a LAN, `--allow-lan` was off. | From a second way in (cloud console, serial console, a person at the machine): `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network`, then `devnet-dvpn daemon set --kill-switch off --yes`. Before next time: `devnet-dvpn daemon set --allow-lan true --yes` (LAN), and never the kill switch over internet SSH without another way in ([`agent-safety.md`](agent-safety.md)). |
| `"code":"spending-limit"` (exit `4`) | This computer's spending limit is below this deposit, and `--raise-limit` was not given. Nothing was paid. | Run the `action`: your line pinned to the node it picked, with `--raise-limit --yes` (your `--protocol` and `--max-price` kept). Or set your own limit: `devnet-dvpn device setup --allowance N --yes` (N in tDVPN, above the deposit). Or a smaller deposit: fewer `--units`. |
| `"code":"price-cap"` (exit `4`) | No `--max-price` was given and the deposit is above the default cap (`defaults.priceCap`: the larger of the spending limit / 10 and the market p75 price × units). Nothing was paid. | Run the `action` (it names the node's price with `--max-price`), or ask for less: fewer `--units`, or `--max-price 0.01` for a cheaper node. |
| `agent up` answered `limitRaised` / `limitNote` and you did not want it | You ran it with `--raise-limit`, so it raised the limit for this deposit. A cap, not a charge. | Lower it: the command in `limitNote` (`devnet-dvpn device setup --allowance <N> --yes`). |
| `"code":"not-funded"` | Less SOL than the step needs (about 0.06 before this computer is set up, fees only after) or less tDVPN than the deposit; `error` names the exact shortfall and a recommended amount that also covers a reconnect. Nothing was paid. | Fund the address in `action`, then `devnet-dvpn agent up --yes`. Or `devnet-dvpn agent up --units <fewer> --yes`. |
| `"code":"not-enough-tdvpn"` | The node `agent up` picked costs more than you hold. Nothing was paid. | `devnet-dvpn agent up --max-price 0.01 --basis per_gb --yes`, or fund more tDVPN. |
| Funding: the operator sees a faucet limit message | Each faucet allows **2 requests every 8 hours**, shared by everyone on the network; the Sentinel faucet also has a daily total. | tDVPN: anyone holding some runs `devnet-dvpn wallet send --to <ADDRESS> --tdvpn 100 --yes`, or wait the time the faucet names. SOL: `solana airdrop 1 <ADDRESS> --url devnet`, or wait; about 0.06 SOL is enough. Done when `agent status --json` shows `sol` above 0.06 and `tdvpn` at least the deposit ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) section 3). |
| A deposit stays in `deposits` with `status` `closing` | A per-GB deposit takes about 2 hours to close (stage 1 of 2). Normal. | After `readyAt` (Unix seconds): `devnet-dvpn settle run --yes`, then `devnet-dvpn settle withdraw --yes`. `next` of `agent status` names the time. |
| A deposit stays `open` with no session | It was never closed (a failed connect after paying, `node-refused`, or a dropped session). | `devnet-dvpn agent down --yes`. Never `agent up` first: it would open a second deposit. |
| `agent down` answers `notClosed` / `warning` | The deposit was opened by another device of this wallet (a replaced computer); this computer cannot close it. | `devnet-dvpn device revoke --device <device> --yes` (if not revoked yet), then `devnet-dvpn settle run --device <device> --yes` |
| `agent down` answers `"code":"busy"`, `settle-failed` or `daemon-gone` | The disconnect is done; the refund run did not finish. Nothing was lost. | `devnet-dvpn settle list`, then `devnet-dvpn settle run --yes` |
| `settle withdraw` answers `withdraw-failed` | The withdraw transaction failed; the balance (`held`) is still there. | `devnet-dvpn settle withdraw --yes` again. "Nothing to withdraw" (exit 0) is not a failure. |
| `agent status` says `"service": false`, or `"code":"daemon-unavailable"` / `service-down` | The VPN service is not running or not answering. | `devnet-dvpn daemon doctor --json` (no check may say `"level": "fail"`); if it is not installed: `devnet-dvpn daemon install --yes` (administrator / root). |
| `"code":"service-not-ready"` | The service is starting or stopping. | The same command again in a moment. |
| `"code":"daemon-missing"` | The VPN service is not installed. Nothing was paid. | Linux / macOS: `devnet-dvpn daemon install --yes` as root or with passwordless `sudo`. Windows: see the next row. |
| Windows: a UAC prompt appears and nothing happens, or `"code":"daemon-relogin"` | The shell is not elevated (an agent cannot answer UAC), or the service pipe does not accept this account yet. | Run `devnet-dvpn daemon install --yes` once from an **elevated** PowerShell or an administrator SSH login. After `"relogin": true`, a non-elevated shell needs a new sign-in or SSH session. |
| macOS over SSH: "The login Keychain is locked in this session" | Without a key file the wallet is kept in the login Keychain, which stays locked in an SSH session. | Use a key file: `export DVPN_KEYFILE="$PWD/agent-key.json"` (or `--keyfile <path>`); a key-file wallet never touches the Keychain. Or unlock it: `security unlock-keychain` (needs the password). |
| `"code":"keyfile-missing"` (exit `4`) | The file `DVPN_KEYFILE` / `--keyfile` names is gone. The funds stay with that key. | Restore the file from your backup and run the command again. Never `wallet create`: a new wallet holds none of the funds. |
| `"code":"no-wallet"` but you had a wallet | `DVPN_KEYFILE` is not set in this shell (it lives only in the shell that set it). | `export DVPN_KEYFILE=<full path>` (PowerShell: `$env:DVPN_KEYFILE = '<full path>'`), or `devnet-dvpn wallet import <file>`. Never `wallet create`. |
| `"code":"wallet-switch-needed"` | This computer is set up for another wallet. Nothing was paid. | Load that wallet's key file, or `devnet-dvpn device switch --yes`. |
| `"code":"clock-skew"` | This computer's clock is off (the error says by how much). Nothing was paid. | Set the clock right, then `devnet-dvpn agent up --yes`. |
| `"code":"node-refused"` | The node refused after the deposit opened. It is skipped next time. | `devnet-dvpn agent down --yes` (closes that deposit), not `agent up`. |
| `"code":"unknown"` on `agent up` (rc6, rc7) | The connect failed with no known cause, before anything was paid ("Nothing was paid"). | `devnet-dvpn logs --lines 80`, then `devnet-dvpn agent up --yes` once more. |
| `"code":"connect-failed"` | The connect failed with no code; it is not known whether a deposit was opened. | `devnet-dvpn agent status --json`: a deposit in `deposits` with no session → `devnet-dvpn agent down --yes`; none → read `error`, then `agent up --yes` once more. |
| `"code":"no-nodes"` | No online node matches the filters. No transaction ran. | `devnet-dvpn nodes list --online --json`, then widen `--protocol` / `--country` / `--max-price` (and check `--basis`). Under `--max-price`, `error` names the cheapest matching price and `action` is a runnable line with it: run it if you accept that price. |
| `"code":"no-device"` | The device key for this computer could not be made. Nothing was paid. | `devnet-dvpn daemon doctor --json`; fix the check that says `"level": "fail"`. |
| `"code":"no-subscription"` (with `--plan`) | The wallet has no subscription to that plan. Nothing was paid. | `devnet-dvpn plans list`, then `devnet-dvpn plans subscribe <plan> --yes`, or drop `--plan`. |
| `"code":"keyfile-mode"` (exit `4`) | The key file can be read by other users of this computer. Nothing was paid. | `chmod 600 <the key file named in error>`, then `devnet-dvpn agent up --yes`. |
| `"code":"rpc-unavailable"`, `rpc-ws`, `rpc-network`, `rpc-quota` | The Solana connection (RPC) the VPN service uses does not answer. `money` says whether a deposit may be open. | Run `next`: `devnet-dvpn daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes` (any Solana devnet RPC, e.g. `https://api.devnet.solana.com`), then `devnet-dvpn agent up --yes`. With money not `none`: `devnet-dvpn agent status --json` first. |
| Anything else | | `devnet-dvpn daemon doctor --json`, `devnet-dvpn logs --lines 80`, and the row for the `code` in [`CODES.md`](CODES.md). |

# file: docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md

# Security model

What holds your money, what can spend it, what a node sees, and what we run. For `devnet-dvpn` v0.3.0-rc7.
Devnet only: SOL and tDVPN here have no value. Terms: [`GLOSSARY.md`](../GLOSSARY.md).

## What we host: nothing

No account, no API key, no server of ours sits between you and a node. You download a release from
GitHub (checked against its `SHA256SUMS`), your computer talks to Solana devnet RPC and to the node you pay.
This repository holds documents, the installers and an MCP server that runs on your own computer.

## Two keys

| Key | Where it lives | What it can sign |
|---|---|---|
| **Wallet key** (the key file) | The file `DVPN_KEYFILE` / `--keyfile` names. Or, without a key file, the OS key store (Windows: DPAPI; macOS: the login Keychain). | Everything the wallet can do: send tDVPN and SOL anywhere (`wallet send`), set up and revoke devices, set the spending limit, withdraw. |
| **Device key** | This computer, made by `daemon init`; used by the VPN service. | Only what the wallet granted it in `device setup`: open, fund, start closing and close deposits with nodes, and open plan subscriptions. It spends tDVPN from your wallet only up to the **spending limit**. It pays its own fees from the **device SOL** (about 0.05 SOL). |

- **Spending limit:** a cap, not a charge. A new install may spend up to 150 tDVPN (an existing limit is kept). `agent up` never raises it by
  itself: with a deposit above it, it refuses (`spending-limit`, nothing paid) until you add `--raise-limit`. Without
  `--max-price` it also refuses a deposit above the default cap (`price-cap`): the larger of the limit / 10 and the
  p75 price of the matching online nodes times `--units`, never above the limit; `defaults` in the `agent up` answer
  says which (`source` `market` or `fixed`). (rc5 raised the limit by itself and said so:
  [`OLDER-RELEASES.md`](OLDER-RELEASES.md).) See it:
  `devnet-dvpn device show --json` (`grant.allowance`, base units). Set it: `devnet-dvpn device setup --allowance N --yes`.
- **Take a device's rights away:** `devnet-dvpn device revoke --device <device> --yes`. Its open deposits stay
  refundable with the wallet key (`devnet-dvpn settle run --device <device> --yes`).
- **Deposits:** money you pay a node goes into a deposit on chain, not to the node. The node can claim only
  what you used (it signs, you check its count; the client refuses a count above its own). The rest comes back
  to your wallet after `agent down` (per GB: after about 2 hours).

## The key file

- `wallet create --keyfile <path>` never writes over an existing file. On Linux and macOS it makes the file
  readable only by you (`0600`) in a folder only you can open (`0700`). On Windows, keep it in your own profile
  folder.
- Whoever has the file owns the wallet. **Never print it, never paste it into a chat or a log, never commit it.**
  Keep one copy somewhere safe: there is no recovery phrase and no reset.
- Use a full path. `DVPN_KEYFILE` lives only in the shell that set it.
- Lost the file: the funds stay with that key. Never `wallet create` in its place (`keyfile-missing`).

## What a node can see

- **Your IP address** (it is the other end of the tunnel) and **the traffic you send through it**: where it goes,
  how much, and when. Anything not encrypted end to end (plain HTTP, plain DNS sent through it) it can read.
  Use HTTPS.
- **Your wallet address and device key** (they pay it), and the deposit.
- It does **not** see your key file, other wallets on the computer, or traffic you route around the tunnel.
