- The internet sees the node's address (`exitIp`), not yours.

## Kill switch, DNS, LAN

- **Kill switch** (`daemon set --kill-switch on --yes`): blocks the internet whenever the tunnel is not up, so
  a dropped session does not fall back to your own address. `on` and `persist` are the same setting here.
  It can also block your SSH session: from the internet, never turn it on without another way in.
  `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network` lifts the block; `--kill-switch off` stops it coming back.
- **DNS:** with the kill switch **off**, WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenVPN and Hysteria2 can send DNS lookups
  outside the tunnel (a known gap). If DNS privacy matters, keep the kill switch on. V2Ray and Xray resolve
  through the proxy.
- **LAN:** `--allow-lan true` keeps hosts on your local network reachable (and a LAN SSH session alive) while
  the kill switch is on. Off means LAN traffic is blocked too.
- **What goes through the node:** WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenVPN and Hysteria2 carry the whole computer. V2Ray
  and Xray carry only what uses the local SOCKS proxy (`socks`) on Linux, the whole computer by default on a
  new Windows or macOS install (`wholeDevice`). Split tunnelling sends chosen addresses or apps around it.

Per OS details and the evidence: [`agent-safety.md`](agent-safety.md). What is proven: [`PROOF.md`](PROOF.md).

## What an agent must not do

- Run a command that spends without reading its preview first: without `--yes` nothing is signed (exit `2`).
- Run `agent up` without `--max-price`.
- Make a new wallet when one existed.
- Print, log or commit the key file.

# file: docs/agent-safety.md

# Agent safety — kill switch, split tunnelling, DNS, proxy (per OS)

For an AI agent driving `devnet-dvpn`. Every value below comes from the app's own CLI reference
([Windows](https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-windows/blob/main/docs/CLI.md),
[Linux](https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-linux/blob/main/docs/CLI.md),
[macOS](https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-macos/blob/main/docs/CLI.md),
[Android](https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-android/blob/main/docs/CLI.md))
and network-safety docs; every "proven" line is a test run of the app on that OS, named by
release and date. Proof overview: [`PROOF.md`](PROOF.md).

## The one rule: never cut your own line

Every one of these settings is applied by **`daemon set … --yes`**, which needs administrator /
root and **restarts the VPN service**. Change settings while disconnected.

1. **Your control channel is traffic too.** With the kill switch `on` or `persist`, the machine
   drops everything that is not the tunnel, the Solana RPC and the node — including the SSH or
   API connection you are being driven through (seen on Linux and on macOS: with LAN off the
   kill switch drops SSH, by design). If you are remote, keep the kill switch `off`, or `on`
   only with `--allow-lan true` **and** a control channel that comes from the LAN.
2. **In this app the kill switch `on` and `persist` are the same setting.** When a session
   drops, it keeps the internet blocked, including across restarts. It has already locked a
   test machine out for good. Unattended with no one to run rule 3, keep it `off`.
3. **Lost the network → `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network`.** It ends any session and releases
   the kill switch and the proxy (every OS, every released version). It removes only the app's
   own tunnels, rules and DNS — never a firewall flush or a tunnel of your own. Proven on
   v0.3.0-rc2, every OS (2026-11-13): after a reboot with the kill switch on, "Internet blocked
   by the kill switch", then Restore → direct. It lifts the block for now; it can come back at
   the next dropped session or service restart. `devnet-dvpn daemon set --kill-switch off --yes`
   stops it coming back.
4. **After every `disconnect` / `agent down`, check `devnet-dvpn quality ip`.** If it shows no
   address, the kill switch is still blocking — this happens when the session had already
   dropped before you disconnected. Run rule 3. Also check `devnet-dvpn status --json` shows no
   session. On Android, disconnect releases the block.
5. **`status` can say "Not connected" while the kill switch still blocks.** About a minute after
   a tunnel is lost, `status` changes from "Reconnecting — internet blocked to protect you" to
   "Not connected", with no hint that the block is still on (seen on Windows, v0.3.0-rc2). Never
   take "Not connected" to mean you are back on your own connection: `quality ip` is the test.

## Changing server with the kill switch on

Use `connect <other node> --switch --yes`. Do **not** `disconnect` first: with the kill switch
`on`, `disconnect` releases the block, so the gap between the two sessions goes out on your real IP.

Earlier switch failures all **failed closed — nothing leaked**:
- VPN service 6.13 and older, every OS: the new connect was refused ("not admitted") and the
  internet stayed blocked until Disconnect / Restore network. Fixed in service 6.14.
- macOS, service 6.15: the switch could fail with "Solana endpoint didn't answer"; the block held
  and nothing was paid. Fixed in service 6.16.

Proven on the v0.3.0-rc2 builds (2026-11-13 to 11-15):

| OS (VPN service) | switch under the kill switch |
|---|---|
| Windows (6.14) | PASS, 0 leaks; a watcher saw the direct IP 0 times in 226 samples |
| Android (6.14) | PASS under `persist`: WireGuard→WireGuard in 11 s, WireGuard→V2Ray in 14 s |
| Linux (October 0.1.9 build) | V2Ray→WireGuard, V2Ray→Xray, Xray→V2Ray connect and are direct after; no leak sampling during the switch |
| macOS (6.16) | WireGuard→WireGuard PASS, 68 probes, 0 leaks |

**Known issue (Windows, open):** re-picking the **same** server can fail late and release the
block. Switch only to a **different** server. If a switch fails, the block holds: try another
node, or `daemon restore-network`.

## Values each OS accepts (released packages)

`daemon set` has the same flags on every OS, but each OS accepts only its own DNS backend, and the
released packages differ (the `daemon set` row of each release's CLI reference:
[Windows v0.2.1](https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-windows/blob/v0.2.1/docs/CLI.md),
[Linux v0.1.21](https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-linux/blob/v0.1.21/docs/CLI.md),
[macOS v0.1.3](https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-macos/blob/v0.1.3/docs/CLI.md)).

**Install v0.3.0-rc2 or newer** (see [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md)). The stable releases cannot
make a key file: their `wallet create` has no `--keyfile`. Columns below = the stable releases'
`daemon set` row.

| flag | Windows v0.2.1 | Linux v0.1.21 | macOS v0.1.3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kill-switch` | `off` `on` `persist` | `off` `on` `persist` | `off` `on` `persist` |
| `--allow-lan` | `true` `false` | `true` `false` | `true` `false` |
| `--dns` | `handshake` `cloudflare` or `ip,ip` | same | same |
| `--dns-mode` | `netsh` `none` | `resolvectl` `resolvconf` `none` | `networksetup` `none` |
| `--whole-device` | `true` `false` | **not offered** on Linux | `true` `false` |
| `--split-mode` | `off` `include` `exclude` | same | same |
| `--split-apps` | `"C:\path\app.exe;…"` or `none` | listed, but **refused** ("Choosing apps does not work on Linux…", also in v0.3.0-rc2) | `"PATH;…"` or `none` |
| `--split-routes` | `IP-or-CIDR,…` or `none` | same | `CIDR,…` or `none` |

Read back with `devnet-dvpn daemon settings`; what split does right now with `devnet-dvpn split status`.

**To undo split tunnelling, clear the list too:**
`devnet-dvpn daemon set --split-mode off --split-routes none --split-apps none --yes`.
`--split-mode off` on its own KEEPS the saved route and app lists, and `--split-routes ""`
answers ok but keeps them too: only `none` clears a list. Then check `daemon settings`
shows no split routes or apps (finding M11, v0.3.0-rc2). On Linux leave out `--split-apps`,
which Linux refuses.

## Windows

| what | do this | proven |
|---|---|---|
| Kill switch `on` | `daemon set --kill-switch on --yes` | all six protocols (October 2026 builds); holds when the protocol process dies and when the VPN service dies |
| Kill switch `persist` | avoid (rule 2) | all six across restart / reboot |
| `--allow-lan` | `--allow-lan true` to keep LAN hosts reachable | all six |
| DNS | keep the kill switch **on** if DNS privacy matters | with the kill switch **off**, WireGuard / AmneziaWG / OpenVPN / Hysteria2 **leak DNS** (known gap); with it on, no leak and the first lookup takes under 3 s. V2Ray / Xray resolve through the proxy |
| Split per app | `split apps` → `daemon set --split-mode exclude --split-apps "C:\…\app.exe" --yes` | all six |
| Split per address | `daemon set --split-mode exclude --split-routes 10.0.0.0/8 --yes` | all six |
| Split + kill switch | possible, proven only on two protocols | WireGuard and Xray; AmneziaWG / OpenVPN / Hysteria2 / V2Ray **not yet run** |
| Whole device (V2Ray / Xray) | `--whole-device true` | all six |
| Proxy (V2Ray / Xray only) | `proxy status` → `proxy on --yes` / `proxy off`; `proxy browser` = one window through the VPN | the system proxy is saved and restored exactly |

Later Windows runs (2026-10-25) passed split by app and by address and the kill switch on /
persist / service killed / reboot / allow-LAN on every protocol; the reboot cases also pass on
v0.3.0-rc2-era code (2026-11-13).

## Linux

| what | do this | proven |
|---|---|---|
| Kill switch `on` | `daemon set --kill-switch on --yes` (nftables, all six; no protocol refused) | 167 checks, 0 failed (October 2026); path lost, protocol killed, service killed → no leak |
| Kill switch `persist` | avoid (rule 2) | 197 checks, 0 failed |
| `--allow-lan` | `--allow-lan true` | LAN in and out with the kill switch on; link-local and the gateway stay on the network card during a full tunnel |
| DNS | `--dns-mode` is chosen by setup (`resolvectl`, or `resolvconf` without systemd-resolved, e.g. EL9) | 49 checks, 0 failed: kill switch off → no lookup leaves on the network card; on → VPN DNS on the tunnel. **Limit:** a name that does not exist is retried with the machine's search domains and goes to the LAN DNS |
| Split per app | **not on Linux**: `--split-apps` is refused. V2Ray / Xray are per-app by nature: only what you send to the SOCKS proxy uses the node | October 0.1.9 build; same refusal in the v0.3.0-rc2 source |
| Split per address | `daemon set --split-mode include\|exclude --split-routes <CIDR,…> --yes`, kill switch **off** | WireGuard / AmneziaWG / OpenVPN / Hysteria2, October 0.1.9 build (not yet run on v0.3.0-rc2): include → the chosen range exits at the node, the rest direct; exclude → the reverse; direct again after disconnect. V2Ray with split set: the proxy still exits at the node |
| Split + kill switch | with the kill switch on, a split setting is not applied: the full tunnel is kept and `split status` says why | 61 checks, 0 failed |
| Whole device (V2Ray / Xray) | **not offered**: they are a proxy only on Linux | — |
| Proxy (V2Ray / Xray only) | `proxy status` → `proxy on --yes` (GNOME / KDE) / `proxy off`; `proxy browser` | GNOME and KDE, settings restored byte for byte |

**Best split on Linux:** by address on WireGuard / AmneziaWG / OpenVPN / Hysteria2 (kill switch
off), or a V2Ray / Xray node with only the traffic you want protected sent to the SOCKS
endpoint from `proxy status`.

## macOS

| what | do this | proven |
|---|---|---|
| Kill switch `on` | `daemon set --kill-switch on --yes` (pf anchor, both directions; no protocol refused) | the block holds when the path to the node is lost (never the direct IP); v0.3.0-rc2 (service 6.16): 3 reboots with the kill switch on, 0 leaks in 30 checks |
| Kill switch `persist` | avoid (rule 2) | holds; uninstalling while it is armed leaves the internet direct, reinstalling arms nothing |
| `--allow-lan` | `--allow-lan true` (LAN passes both ways only when true) | PASS (2026-10-27): with LAN off a new SSH from the LAN fails, with LAN on it works. Older test machines failed this check; the current one passes |
| DNS | `--dns-mode networksetup` (VPN DNS on every network service) or `none` | 61 checks, 0 failed |
| Split per address | `daemon set --split-mode include\|exclude --split-routes <CIDR,…> --yes` | all six protocols, include and exclude, nothing left behind after |
| Split per app | `split apps` → `daemon set --split-apps "<path>;…" --yes` | the setting is applied; per-app traffic not yet measured separately |
| Whole device (V2Ray / Xray) | `--whole-device true` | 55 checks, 0 failed |
| Proxy (V2Ray / Xray only) | `proxy status` → `proxy on --yes` (every enabled network service) / `proxy off`; `proxy browser` | saved and restored exactly, also after the service and the protocol are killed |

## Android

The Android app has the same commands inside it, plus Android-only `split show`, `split set` and
`split routes`. A released Android build cannot be driven from outside the app, so an agent does
not run on Android and it is not covered here.

# file: docs/OPERATOR.md

# For the person whose agent is asking for help

Your AI agent wants a private internet connection. It uses Sentinel dVPN: instead of signing up
with a VPN company, it pays a VPN server (a "node") directly, from a small wallet of its own, on
Solana **devnet**. Devnet is the test network: its tokens are free and have no value.

The agent does almost everything itself. It needs a person for two things only: **getting its
wallet funded** (the faucets are web pages for people) and, on some machines, **one
administrator prompt** during setup.

The guide your agent follows: <https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet/blob/main/AGENTS.md>.

## 1. "Please fund my wallet"

The agent sends you a message with its wallet address. It looks like a long string of letters
and numbers. You need a GitHub account. It takes about two minutes and costs nothing.

**tDVPN, to pay the VPN.** Open <https://faucet.sentinel.co>.

1. Click **Connect GitHub** first (in the "Connect your GitHub." box) and approve. Do this before
   pasting anything: the page reloads on sign-in and an address typed earlier is lost. The big
   button that says "Connect GitHub to request" stays greyed out until you have done this.
2. Back on the page (it shows "GitHub connected"), paste the address into
   **Solana wallet address**.
3. Click **Request 100 tDVPN**. Done when you see **"100 tDVPN received"**.

**SOL, for network fees.** On the same page, the "Claim Devnet Sol" card has **Open official
faucet** (it opens <https://faucet.solana.com>).

1. Check the network says **devnet**, paste the same address into **Wallet Address**.
2. Click **Amount**, choose **0.5** (the choices are 0.5, 1, 2.5 and 5), then **Confirm Airdrop**.
3. A **Cloudflare Verification** box asks you to complete a captcha. Do it. Done when a
   **"Success!"** message appears.

No sign-in is needed on this page. Its "Connect your GitHub" box only raises the limit.

Then tell the agent you have seen "100 tDVPN received" and "Success!". It checks the balance
itself.

**If it does not work:**

- Each faucet allows **2 requests every 8 hours**. Once signed in, the Sentinel faucet shows
  "N / 2 remaining" and, after a request, "Next request available …". When none are left, its
  button reads "Claim limit reached". People on the same network share one allowance. (Its
  subtitle says "Claim 100 tDVPN every 8 hours"; the real limit is 2.)
- The Sentinel faucet also has a daily total for everyone. If it says the limit is reached and
  your 8 hours have passed, waiting will not help that day. Anyone with a funded Devnet dVPN
  wallet can send tDVPN instead: `devnet-dvpn wallet send --to <ADDRESS> --tdvpn 100 --yes`.
- The Solana faucet is often busy. Try again later. If the agent's machine has the Solana command
  line, the agent may get the SOL itself.
- Taking funds back from an agent's wallet later: sending all of its SOL is refused ("This would
  leave an account below Solana's minimum balance … Send a little less"). Leave about 0.001 SOL.

## 2. The one administrator moment

Setting up the VPN on the machine needs administrator / root rights once: when the app is
installed and when the agent installs its VPN service. Afterwards the agent runs as a normal
user. Whether you are needed depends on the machine.

| OS | No prompt when… | Otherwise | Can the agent answer it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux | the agent's user has passwordless `sudo`, or it runs as root | the system asks for a password | No, not over SSH: run the step as root or allow passwordless `sudo` |
| Windows | the agent's shell already runs as administrator (an elevated terminal, or SSH as an administrator) | one UAC "allow changes?" prompt | No. With no desktop session the step fails |
| macOS | the agent's user has passwordless `sudo` | a password dialog on the screen | No: only a person at the screen can type it |

If the agent says it is stuck at this step, it is waiting for you: either answer the prompt at
the machine, or give its account the rights above. In a sandbox where nobody can become
administrator, the VPN service cannot be installed, and the agent will tell you so.

On Windows the agent may also say the account can use the service only after its next sign-in.
That is normal once, after the first install.

## 3. What it costs

Nothing real. Everything is on devnet with free test tokens: 100 tDVPN and 0.5 SOL last a long
time. The agent puts a small deposit on each connection and gets back what it does not use.

## 4. The key file

The agent's wallet is one file, usually named `agent-key.json`. Whoever has the file has the
wallet. **Never send it to anyone, never paste it into a chat or a website, never commit it to
git.** Nobody (no faucet, no support person, no agent) ever needs it from you. You only ever share
the address, which is safe to share.

## 5. Stopping the VPN and getting the deposit back

The agent normally does this itself. To do it yourself, open a terminal on the agent's machine
with the same key file set (`DVPN_KEYFILE`) and run:

```sh
devnet-dvpn disconnect              # stops the VPN: the machine uses its own connection again
devnet-dvpn settle run --yes        # starts closing the deposit
```

The deposit can be refunded about two hours later (`devnet-dvpn settle list` shows when). Then:

```sh
devnet-dvpn settle run --yes        # finishes closing
devnet-dvpn settle withdraw --yes   # moves the refund back to the wallet
```

Nobody has to stay online for the two hours.

If the internet on that machine stays blocked after the VPN is stopped (`devnet-dvpn quality ip`
shows no address), the kill switch is still blocking; this happens when the VPN session had
already dropped. `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network` lifts the block for now; it can come back.
`devnet-dvpn daemon set --kill-switch off --yes` stops it coming back.

## 6. Not supported yet

- **Android:** the app works on a phone, but an agent cannot drive the released Android app from
  outside it.
- **Windows on ARM:** no build of the release the agent needs (v0.3.0-rc6) yet.
- **Apple silicon Macs:** the build exists but has not been tested; Intel Macs are tested.
- **Machines where nobody can be administrator** (most sandboxes): the VPN service cannot be
  installed.

What has been tested on each system, step by step: [`PROOF.md`](PROOF.md).

# file: mcp/README.md

# MCP server: Devnet dVPN for an AI agent

A stdio MCP server with no dependencies, in one file: [`server.js`](server.js). It runs the
**installed** `devnet-dvpn` CLI (from the Devnet dVPN package for your OS) and returns the CLI's
JSON and exit code unchanged. Solana devnet only: the tokens have no value.

**Status (2026-11-15, Linux, Node 22):** the unit tests (`node --test mcp/server.test.js`) pass.
A live check (`node mcp/live-check.mjs`, real server, real CLI, real devnet; it spends nothing)
passed against the installed v0.3.0-rc2: `initialize`, `tools/list` (9 tools), `vpn_status`,
`vpn_wallet`, `vpn_nodes` (about 7 s), and on rc2 `vpn_agent_status` / `vpn_up` answer the
"use `vpn_nodes` + `vpn_connect`" fallback. Against a development build that has the `agent`
commands, `vpn_agent_status` answered with `next`, and `vpn_up` on a wallet that had already
been emptied answered `code: "not-funded"` with the amount and address in `action`, as the CLI
does. `vpn_connect` and `vpn_settle` were not called by the check (they spend); the commands
they run are proven on their own.

## 1. Set the machine up with the CLI first

MCP cannot set the machine up: installing the service needs administrator / root once. Do sections
1–4 of [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) with the CLI: install **v0.3.0-rc6** by name (macOS: v0.3.0-rc4),
`wallet create --keyfile <path> --yes`, get the address funded (a person sends devnet SOL and
tDVPN), then `daemon init` → `device setup --yes` → `daemon install --yes`. After that,
everything below runs as the normal user over MCP.

## 2. Needs

- **Node.js 20 or newer** to run `server.js`.
- **The CLI.** The server looks for it in this order:
  1. `DEVNET_DVPN_BIN`, if set (a full path);
  2. `devnet-dvpn` on the `PATH` the MCP client gives the server;
  3. macOS only: `/usr/local/bin/devnet-dvpn` (made by `daemon install`), then
     `/Applications/Devnet dVPN.app/Contents/Resources/bin/devnet-dvpn`, then the same under
     `~/Applications`. This covers clients started as GUI apps, which get a short `PATH`.
     Windows only: the installer's default folder,
     `C:\Program Files\Devnet dVPN\bin\devnet-dvpn.cmd`. This covers a client started before the
     install, whose `PATH` is still the old one.

  | OS | where the CLI is |
  |---|---|
  | Linux | `/usr/bin/devnet-dvpn` |
  | Windows | `<install folder>\bin\devnet-dvpn.cmd`, on `PATH` for programs started **after** the install. In the default folder nothing more is needed; in another folder, restart the MCP client once or set `DEVNET_DVPN_BIN` |
  | macOS | `/Applications/Devnet dVPN.app/Contents/Resources/bin/devnet-dvpn`; also `/usr/local/bin/devnet-dvpn` after `daemon install` |

- **A key file**, named by `DVPN_KEYFILE`, as an **absolute** path (the client's working directory
  is unknown). The key travels only through this env variable, never as an argument.
  On macOS, use a key file: without one the CLI uses the login Keychain, which can show an access
  prompt that nobody may be there to answer.

## 3. Config

Get the server: `git clone https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet`
(it is `mcp/server.js` in that folder).

Any MCP client that starts a stdio server. The generic form:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agentic-privacy": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/mcp/server.js"],
      "env": { "DVPN_KEYFILE": "/absolute/path/to/agent-key.json" }
    }
  }
}
```

On Windows, escape the backslashes in JSON:
`"args": ["C:\\agent\\agentic-privacy-solana-devnet\\mcp\\server.js"]`, `"DVPN_KEYFILE": "C:\\agent\\agent-key.json"`.
Add `"DEVNET_DVPN_BIN"` to `env` only if the CLI is not found (macOS paths need no extra quoting
inside a JSON string, even with the space).

For a command-line client that takes the server as a command, the same thing is
`DVPN_KEYFILE=/absolute/path/to/agent-key.json node /absolute/path/to/mcp/server.js`.

The server speaks MCP protocol versions `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` and `2024-11-05`. Its
`initialize` answer carries short instructions for the model (the tool order and the `yes` rule).

## 4. Tools

### Six CLI tools (every release from v0.3.0-rc2 on)

| tool | runs | gives back (`result`) |
|---|---|---|
| `vpn_status` | `devnet-dvpn status --json` | wallet, device, service and session state |
| `vpn_wallet` | `devnet-dvpn wallet show --json` | `owner` (the address to fund), `ownerLamports` (SOL × 10⁹, a number), `ownerTdvpn` (tDVPN × 10⁶, a string), `ready` (true only after `device setup`), … |
| `vpn_nodes {country?, protocol?, sort?}` | `devnet-dvpn nodes list --online [--country CC] [--protocol P] [--sort price] --json` | an array of online nodes |
| `vpn_connect {node, basis?, units?, plan?, yes?}` | `devnet-dvpn connect <node> [--basis per_gb\|per_hour] [--units 1-1000] [--plan S] [--yes] --json` | the session: `id`, `node`, `status` (`active`), `service` (protocol), `channel`, `spent`, `proxyEndpoint` (V2Ray/Xray SOCKS, else empty), `error`, `warning` |
| `vpn_disconnect` | `devnet-dvpn disconnect --json` | `{"ok": true}` |
| `vpn_settle {channel?, yes?}` | `devnet-dvpn settle run [--channel C] [--yes] --json` | `signatures`: the transactions sent; without `yes`, a preview with `pending` (the deposits it would settle) |

`protocol` is one of `wireguard`, `amneziawg`, `openvpn`, `v2ray`, `xray`, `hysteria2`; `country`
is a two-letter code; `sort` is `price`. A typical run: `vpn_wallet` (check funds) → `vpn_nodes
{"protocol": "wireguard", "sort": "price"}` → `vpn_connect {"node": "<address from the list>", "yes": true}` → work
→ `vpn_disconnect` → `vpn_settle {"yes": true}`. A per-GB deposit becomes refundable about two hours after
`vpn_settle` starts the close; run `vpn_settle` once more then (the rest of the refund is a CLI
step: `settle withdraw --yes`).

`vpn_connect` and `vpn_settle` spend or sign, so, like `vpn_up` and `vpn_down`, they pass `--yes` only with `"yes": true`; without it the CLI answers a preview (exit `2`) and nothing is spent.

### Three agent tools (v0.3.0-rc4 and newer)

The output contract is [`docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md`](../docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md) (a copy of the
app source's file, kept equal by a test); the fields below follow it.
Amounts are decimal strings in tDVPN or SOL (e.g. `"0.002"`), `baseUnits` is the same amount in
base units, and times (`readyAt`) are Unix seconds.

**`vpn_agent_status`** runs `devnet-dvpn agent status --json`. It is read-only and never needs `yes`.

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `address` | wallet address; `null` = no wallet on this computer |
| `sol`, `tdvpn` | balances; `null` when there is no wallet or they could not be read |
| `held` | the wallet's balance held in the program, which `settle withdraw` moves to the wallet; **not** the `refundable` of `vpn_down` (v0.3.0-rc4 named it `refundable`) (on devnet a closed deposit's refund went straight to the wallet, so this stayed `"0"`) |
| `device` | this computer's device key; `null` = not set up |
| `service`, `connected` | booleans: the VPN service answers / a session is live |
| `blocked` | `true` only when no session is live and the internet does not answer (the kill switch holds the block, or the network is down) |
| `session`, `node`, `protocol`, `spent`, `exitIp`, `socks`, `wholeDevice` | only when connected (`exitIp` `null` if the check took over 8 s; `socks` `null` when the protocol gives none, and on Android) |
| `deposits` | only when the wallet has open or closing deposits: `{channel, node, status, refundable, readyAt}` each |
| `code`, `message`, `nodeStopped`, `alsoNext` | only when the node stopped serving: `code` = `server-stopped`, `connected` is false, the deposit is safe; `next` = `agent up --yes` (another node), `alsoNext` = `agent down --yes` (closes the deposit) |
| `next` | the next step: create a wallet, fund it, `agent down --yes` (connected), or `agent up --yes` |

**`vpn_up {protocol?, country?, node?, basis?, units?, plan?, max_price?, yes?}`** runs
`devnet-dvpn agent up […] [--yes] --json`. It picks the best matching online node, pays the
deposit (or uses the plan) and connects.

- `protocol`: `any` or one of the six. `country`: two letters. `node`: one exact node.
  `plan`: a subscription you hold. `units`: 1–1000, default from settings.
- `basis` defaults to the **saved setting**, not always `per_gb`. `max_price` is tDVPN per unit
  of the basis, so the server refuses `max_price` without `basis`.
- On its own it reads the session, nodes, wallet and plans, and creates the device key if
  there is none (local, no transaction). The deposit, the spending limit, the connect and a
  switch need `yes: true`.

| answer | fields |
|---|---|
| connected (exit 0) | `session`, `node`, `protocol` (the one really used), `country`, `exitIp`, `directIp`, `socks` (`socks5h://host:port` or `null`), `wholeDevice`, `channel`, `deposit`, `next` (always `agent down --yes`), `note` (what the session means, in one sentence); `blockedBefore: true` when the kill switch held the internet before it; `replaced` / `replacedNote` when the live session was not tunnelled and it switched; `skipped` / `skippedNote` when it left out a node that recently stopped or refused |
| `deposit` | `{basis, units, tdvpn, baseUnits}` (`tdvpn` = the most it can hold; the unused part is refunded); `{plan, tdvpn: "0"}` with a plan; `null` when `reused` |
| already connected to a match | the same, with `reused: true`; nothing paid, no `yes` needed. A match: `node` is the live node, or, with no `node`, `protocol` and `country` (each only if given) equal the live ones. `basis`, `units`, `plan` and `max_price` are not compared while a session is live |
| connected elsewhere | it switches: leaves the live node and connects to the new one (with the kill switch on, the block stays up in between); never picks the live server |
| preview (exit 2, no `yes`) | `needsConfirm: true`, `what` (the sentence it would do), `node`, `deposit`, `switchFrom` (`null` = not connected) |

**`vpn_down {yes?}`** runs `devnet-dvpn agent down [--yes] --json`. With `yes: true` it
disconnects (with the kill switch on, the block usually lifts at the disconnect; check as described below), then one
`settle run`: per-hour deposits close at once (they bill until closed), per-GB deposits start
their two-hour close.

In this app the kill switch `on` and `persist` are the same setting. After `disconnect` / `agent
down`, check `devnet-dvpn quality ip`. If it shows no address, the kill switch is still blocking —
this happens when the session had already dropped before you disconnected. `devnet-dvpn daemon
restore-network` lifts the block for now; it can come back at the next dropped session or service
restart. `devnet-dvpn daemon set --kill-switch off --yes` stops it coming back. (These are CLI
commands; the MCP server has no tool for them.)

| answer | fields |
|---|---|
| done (exit 0) | `disconnected` (disconnect's own answer or `null`), `spent` (`null` = no session), `refundable` (the sum over `pending`, a lower bound; **not** the wallet balance of `vpn_agent_status`), `readyAt`, `signatures`, `pending` (deposits left: `{channel, node, mode, status, readyAt, refundable, …}`), `next` |
| `next` | after `readyAt`: `settle run --yes`, then `settle withdraw --yes`; or `settle list`; or `agent up --yes` to connect again |
| preview (exit 2, no `yes`) | `needsConfirm: true`, `what`, `session`, `perHour`, `perGb` (deposits it would close / start closing, the live session's own deposit included) |

These two ask for consent explicitly, because `vpn_up` picks the node and the deposit for you:
`yes` must be the boolean `true` (the string `"true"` is refused). Without it the CLI exits `2`
and shows what it would do; the tool returns that as a **preview** (`structuredContent.preview:
true`, `isError: false`). Call again with `"yes": true` to do it.

On macOS, until `daemon install` has run, a `next` may start with the quoted app path instead of
`devnet-dvpn`.

A `next` or `action` that runs `… agent up`, `… agent down` or `… agent status` maps to `vpn_up`,
`vpn_down` or `vpn_agent_status` (`--yes` in it = `yes: true`). Any other command in it
(`daemon install`, `device setup`, `settle run`, …) is a CLI step: see "Not covered".

**On a release without the `agent` commands** (v0.3.0-rc2 or older: [`docs/OLDER-RELEASES.md`](../docs/OLDER-RELEASES.md)), the three tools return `isError: true` with
`structuredContent.error = "no agent command in this CLI"` and a `fix` that says to use
`vpn_nodes` + `vpn_connect`. Nothing is run.

## 5. Results and errors

Every result has `structuredContent = { exitCode, command, result, isError }`:

- The CLI's own fields are also copied to the top, unchanged and only when the CLI sent them. On a
  failure that is `error`, `code`, `action`, `money`, `next`, `alsoNext` and `docUrl`. On a success
  or a preview it is `next`, `defaults` and `alsoNext`. The server never re-words them.
- `command`: the exact CLI line that ran (no key in it).
- `result`: the CLI's JSON (`null` if it printed none). The text content is the same JSON line.
- `exitCode`: `0` ok, `1` error, `2` needs `--yes`, `3` usage. Non-zero sets `isError`, except
  the exit-2 preview of `vpn_up` / `vpn_down`.
- A CLI error is `{"ok": false, "error": "…", "code": "…", "action": "…"}`: `action` is the next
  thing to do. On a non-zero exit the CLI's stderr is added as a second text item.

### Failure codes of the agent tools

On a failure (exit 1) `result` is `{"ok": false, "error", "code", "action"}`. Do what `action`
says; when it is `null`, read `error`. "→ status" means the action is `agent status`: read
`error`, and pick another server or filter if the code names the server.

| code | where | action / meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `no-wallet` | up | `wallet create --keyfile <path> --yes`, then have the address funded |
| `no-wallet` | down | `vpn_disconnect` to leave the VPN now; then `wallet import <file>` (the wallet that paid) and `vpn_down {"yes": true}` to close the deposits: with no wallet the CLI cannot read or close them; nothing ran |
| `no-device` | up | `daemon doctor`: the device key could not be made |
| `no-subscription` | up with `plan` | `plans list`, then `plans subscribe <plan> --yes`, or drop `plan` |
| `no-nodes` | up | `nodes list --online --json`, then widen protocol / country / max_price (check basis); nothing paid |
| `not-funded` | up | send the SOL / tDVPN it names to the address, then `agent up --yes`; nothing paid |
| `connect-failed` | up | → status (connect failed with no code) |
| `settle-failed` | down | `settle list`: the disconnect is done; the deposits are listed there |
| `busy` | down | `settle run --yes` (`vpn_settle {"yes": true}`): the disconnect is done, but another refund run held the lock, so nothing was closed; a per-hour deposit bills until it is |
| the disconnect's own code (e.g. `daemon-unavailable`), else `stop-failed` | down | `daemon doctor`, then `vpn_down {"yes": true}` again: the disconnect failed, so no deposit was closed, and a per-hour deposit keeps billing while the session is up |
| `daemon-missing` | up | `daemon install --yes` once (administrator / root; Windows: from an elevated shell or an administrator SSH login), then `agent up --yes` |
| `daemon-relogin` | up | Windows: the service does not accept this account yet: `daemon install --yes` once from an elevated shell, or a new sign-in; elsewhere as `daemon-missing` |
| `protocol-missing` | up | another protocol this computer has, or `daemon repair-drivers --yes`; the deposit comes back with `agent down --yes` |
| `device-permission` | up | `device setup --yes`, then `agent up --yes` |
| `daemon-unavailable`, `daemon-restarting` | up | `daemon doctor` |
| `test-running` | up | `test stop`, then `agent up --yes` |
| `rpc-busy` | up | `agent up --yes` again in a minute |
| `rpc-ws` | up | rc7: the RPC websocket address does not answer; it is not known whether a deposit opened (`vpn_status` lists it). Set another RPC (`daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes`), then `vpn_up` again |
| `price-changed`, `deposit-unusable`, `deposits-unread` | up | `agent up --yes` again: nothing was paid, and it reads the price fresh (`max_price` still caps it). The server's price rose above the deposit shown / your open deposit with it started closing / your open deposits could not be read |
| `not-confirmed`, `plan-limit`, `busy`, `unsupported`, `network-mismatch` | up | → status: refused before anything started |
| `session-active`, `node-gone`, `node-stale`, `node-offline`, `protocol-blocked`, `driver-missing`, `basis-unavailable`, `not-enough-tdvpn`, `spending-limit`, `device-sol`, `preflight`, `kill-switch-held`, `switch-reconnecting`, `switch-offline` | up | → status: the check before paying failed; nothing paid |
| `price-cap` | up | rc6: no `max_price` and the deposit is above the default cap (the spending limit / 10: 5 tDVPN by default); nothing was paid. Call `vpn_up` again with `max_price` (the `action` names the node's price) or fewer `units` |
| `keyfile-mode` | up | rc7: the key file can be read by other users of this computer; nothing was paid. `chmod 600 <the key file named in error>`, then `vpn_up` again |
| `cancelled` | up | → status: stopped |
| `waiting-for-network`, `ticket-other-owner`, `approval-revoked`, `service-stopped-connecting`, `node-identity`, `node-ledger`, `node-price`, `node-error`, `kill-switch-failed`, `tunnel-failed`, `tunnel-dead`, `tunnel-mtu`, `tunnel-closing`, `port-in-use`, `dns-apply`, `deposit-pending`, `rpc-network`, `rpc-timeout`, `rpc-quota`, `timeout`, `chain-encoding` | up | → status: failed after the start; a deposit already paid stays open until `agent down --yes` |
| `credit_exhausted`, `peer_limit_reached`, `lease_insufficient`, `subscription_invalid`, `ticket_request_stale`, `provider_unreachable`, `ticket_invalid`, `unauthorized`, `cannot cover the prepay`, `voucher_exceeds_escrow`, `channel_node_reopened`, `terms_rejected`, `rate_limited`, `voucher_signature_invalid`, `mode_not_voucher`, `mode_not_stream` | up | → status: the server refused; pick another with `node` or other filters |
| `stop-failed`, `dns-revert-failed`, `tunnel-left` | up | → status: leaving the old session failed |
| `unknown` | up | → status |
| `service-down` | any | the VPN service is not running: the start hint, or `null` |
| `service-not-ready` | any | `null`: try again in a moment |
| `approval-revoked` | any | `device setup --yes` (also above) |
| `not-enough-tdvpn` | any | `null`: fund the wallet or use fewer `units` (also above) |
| `session-active` | any | `disconnect` (also above) |
| `rpc-unavailable` | any | every RPC endpoint failed: check the network, or set another RPC |
| `keyfile-missing` | up | restore the key file named in the error from your backup (it is the only key to this wallet), then `agent up --yes`; never `wallet create` (a new wallet cannot see the old refunds) |
| `wallet-switch-needed` | up, down, status | load the key file of the wallet named in the error, or `device switch --yes` (sets this computer up for the loaded wallet; the other wallet's deposits stay refundable). Nothing was paid |
| `clock-skew` | up | set this computer's clock to the right time (the error says by about how much), then `agent up --yes` |

Usage errors (exit 3) print nothing on stdout, only one line on stderr: a bad flag value, an
unknown flag or subcommand. The tool's schema check stops nearly all of them before the CLI runs.

The server's own errors have `exitCode: null`, `isError: true`, `error` and `fix`: CLI not found
(the fix names the download for each OS), or bad input (the schema is checked before anything
runs; nothing passes through a shell).

Time limits: `vpn_connect` and `vpn_up` 300 s, `vpn_settle` and `vpn_down` 180 s, `vpn_nodes`
120 s, the rest 60 s. On a timeout the CLI is stopped and the result says so: call `vpn_status`
before retrying, because a connect may have finished anyway. A timed-out `vpn_connect` or `vpn_up` can leave a deposit already paid: `vpn_agent_status` (or `vpn_status`) shows it, and `vpn_disconnect` then `vpn_settle {"yes": true}` (or `vpn_down {"yes": true}`) gets it back.

On Windows the server runs the two programs inside the installer's `bin\devnet-dvpn.cmd` shim
directly, so no argument ever reaches `cmd.exe`.

**macOS:** if the service has not granted this account access yet, a call can run one
administrator step. Without passwordless `sudo`, that is a password dialog on the screen, and the
call waits for it until the time limit. A call that seems to hang may be waiting for that dialog.

**Windows:** if the service has not accepted this account yet, a call can run one administrator
step. From a client that is not elevated, that is a UAC prompt on the screen, and the call waits
for it until the time limit. With no desktop (a client run as a service, or over SSH as a
non-administrator) it fails with `code: "daemon-relogin"`: run `devnet-dvpn daemon install --yes`
once from an elevated shell, then retry.

## 6. Not covered by this server

First-run setup (`wallet create`, `daemon init`, `device setup`, `daemon install`), split
tunnelling and the kill switch (`daemon set …`), and `settle withdraw` are CLI-only: they need an
administrator step or are rare. Run them with the CLI, as `AGENTS.md` describes.

## 7. Checking it

- Unit tests, from the repo root: `node --test mcp/server.test.js` (Node 20+; a bare `mcp/`
  argument fails on Node 22). No CLI or network needed.
- Live check, spends nothing: `DVPN_KEYFILE=<key> node mcp/live-check.mjs --out <dir>` starts the
  server, speaks real JSON-RPC to it, and calls only the read-only tools plus `vpn_up` without
  `yes`. It needs `devnet-dvpn` findable as in section 2. `--bundle <devnet-dvpn.cjs>` adds a pass
  against a CLI built from source (the `out/cli/devnet-dvpn.cjs` of a build; the copy inside an
  installed app is packed in `app.asar` and plain Node cannot read it).
- Live check with one paid session (v0.3.0-rc4 or newer, after sections 1 to 4 of `AGENTS.md`):
  `DVPN_KEYFILE=<key> node mcp/live-check.mjs --out <dir> --paid --yes` adds `vpn_up`
  (`yes: true`, WireGuard, per GB, 1 unit), `vpn_agent_status` (connected), `vpn_down`
  (`yes: true`) and `vpn_agent_status` (not connected). It spends one deposit (about 0.002 tDVPN
  per GB on devnet; the unused part comes back after the two-hour close). Without both `--paid`
  and `--yes` it spends nothing. `--protocol <name>` and `--basis per_hour` change the session.

# file: install.sh

#!/bin/sh
# ─── install.sh: install devnet-dvpn (Sentinel dVPN on Solana devnet) on Linux or macOS ───
#
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet/main/install.sh | sh
#
# or, to read it first:
#
#   curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet/main/install.sh
#   sh install.sh
#
# What it does: finds your OS, CPU and package type (deb / rpm / pacman; macOS dmg), takes the
# newest release (pre-releases included) that has that file and is v0.3 or newer (the guide pins v0.3.0-rc6), downloads
# the file and the release's SHA256SUMS, checks the file, installs it with no questions, and runs
# `devnet-dvpn version --json`. Needs root or passwordless sudo (`sudo -n true` must work).
#
# Options, as environment variables:
#   DVPN_VERSION=v0.3.0-rc6   use this release tag instead of the newest (AGENTS.md pins it)
#
# Output: progress and errors on stderr; on success one JSON line on stdout:
#   {"ok":true,"tag":…,"file":…,"version":{…},"path":"export PATH=…"|null,"next":…}
# and on failure {"ok":false,"error":"<the sentence>"}.
# Exit codes: 0 installed · 1 failed (the reason is printed as one sentence).
# Nothing runs until the whole script has been read (everything is inside main, called last).

set -eu

LINUX_REPO='Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-linux'
MAC_REPO='Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-macos'
GUIDE='https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet/blob/main/AGENTS.md'
MAC_BIN='/Applications/Devnet dVPN.app/Contents/Resources/bin'

say() { printf 'install.sh: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
# Messages never contain a double quote, so they go into the JSON line as they are.
# Inside main, fd 3 is the real stdout and fd 1 points at stderr (see the exec there).
fail() { printf 'install.sh: %s\n' "$*" >&2; printf '{"ok":false,"error":"%s"}\n' "$*" >&3; exit 1; }

# ─── a tag is usable when it is v0.3 or newer (older releases cannot make a key file) ───
tag_ok() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed 's/^v//' | awk -F'[.-]' '{ exit !(($1 + 0) > 0 || ($2 + 0) >= 3) }'
}

# ─── pick the file name matching $2 (an extended regex) out of a SHA256SUMS file $1 ───
file_from_sums() {
  awk '{ f = $2; sub(/^\*/, "", f); print f }' "$1" | grep -E "$2" | head -n 1
}

main() {
  # The one JSON line goes to fd 3 (the real stdout). Everything else any command prints, the
  # package managers included, goes to stderr, so stdout is exactly one line.
  exec 3>&1 1>&2
  command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'curl is not installed; install curl and run this again.'

  # ─── root or passwordless sudo ───
  if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
    SUDO=''
  elif command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
    SUDO='sudo -n'
  else
    fail 'installing needs root or passwordless sudo (sudo -n true failed); run this as root, or ask your operator to install the app.'
  fi

  # ─── OS, CPU, package type → repo and file pattern ───
  os=$(uname -s)
  cpu=$(uname -m)
  case "$os" in
    Linux)
      REPO=$LINUX_REPO
      case "$cpu" in
        x86_64|amd64) deb=amd64; rpm=x86_64; pac=x64 ;;
        aarch64|arm64) deb=arm64; rpm=aarch64; pac=aarch64 ;;
        *) fail "this CPU ($cpu) has no Linux package; only x86_64 and aarch64 are built." ;;
      esac
      if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        KIND=deb; PAT="^devnet-dvpn_.*_${deb}\\.deb\$"
      elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        KIND=rpm; PAT="^devnet-dvpn-.*\\.${rpm}\\.rpm\$"
      elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        KIND=pacman; PAT="^devnet-dvpn-.*-${pac}\\.pkg\\.tar\\.zst\$"
      else
        fail 'no apt-get, dnf, yum or pacman found; download the AppImage from the releases page instead.'
      fi
      SUM='sha256sum -c -'
      ;;
    Darwin)
      REPO=$MAC_REPO
      KIND=dmg
      # Under Rosetta uname -m says x86_64 on Apple silicon; ask the hardware.
      if [ "$(sysctl -n hw.optional.arm64 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" = 1 ]; then a=arm64; else a=x64; fi
      PAT="^Devnet-dVPN-.*-${a}\\.dmg\$"
      SUM='shasum -a 256 -c -'
      ;;
    *) fail "this OS ($os) is not covered by install.sh; on Windows use install.ps1." ;;
  esac

  tmp=$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t dvpn)
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
  trap 'exit 1' INT TERM

  # ─── which release ───
  if [ -n "${DVPN_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    TAG=$DVPN_VERSION
    case "$TAG" in v*) ;; *) TAG="v$TAG" ;; esac
    tag_ok "$TAG" || fail "release $TAG is older than v0.3 and cannot make a key file; use DVPN_VERSION=v0.3.0-rc6."
    BASE="https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$TAG"
    curl -fsSL -o "$tmp/SHA256SUMS" "$BASE/SHA256SUMS" || fail "release $TAG has no SHA256SUMS (is the tag right? tags look like v0.3.0-rc6)."
    FILE=$(file_from_sums "$tmp/SHA256SUMS" "$PAT") || true
    [ -n "$FILE" ] || fail "release $TAG has no $KIND package for this CPU."
  else
    curl -fsSL -o "$tmp/releases.json" "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases?per_page=30" \
      || fail 'could not read the release list from GitHub (rate limit or no network); set DVPN_VERSION=<tag> and run again.'
    # The API lists releases newest-CREATED first, and the first usable one wins: a release made
    # later on an older line would be picked over a newer version. Pin DVPN_VERSION to rule that out.
    urls=$(grep -o '"browser_download_url": *"[^"]*"' "$tmp/releases.json" | sed 's/.*"\(https[^"]*\)"$/\1/') || true
    pick=$(printf '%s\n' "$urls" | while IFS= read -r u; do
      f=${u##*/}
      t=${u%/*}; t=${t##*/}
      if printf '%s\n' "$f" | grep -qE "$PAT" && tag_ok "$t"; then printf '%s\n' "$u"; break; fi
    done)
    [ -n "$pick" ] || fail "no release v0.3 or newer has a $KIND package for this CPU."
    FILE=${pick##*/}
    BASE=${pick%/*}
    TAG=${BASE##*/}
    curl -fsSL -o "$tmp/SHA256SUMS" "$BASE/SHA256SUMS" || fail "release $TAG has no SHA256SUMS; not installing an unchecked file."
  fi

  say "release $TAG, file $FILE"
  curl -fsSL -o "$tmp/$FILE" "$BASE/$FILE" || fail "download of $FILE failed."

  # ─── check the file against SHA256SUMS ───
  line=$(awk -v f="$FILE" '{ g = $2; sub(/^\*/, "", g); if (g == f) { print $1 "  " f; exit } }' "$tmp/SHA256SUMS")
  [ -n "$line" ] || fail "SHA256SUMS of $TAG has no line for $FILE; not installing an unchecked file."
  (cd "$tmp" && printf '%s\n' "$line" | $SUM >/dev/null) || fail "$FILE does not match SHA256SUMS; not installing it."
  say 'checksum OK'

  # ─── install, no questions ───
  case "$KIND" in
    deb)
      # Without the update a fresh machine fails with "libsecret-tools … not installable".
      $SUDO apt-get update -qq || fail 'apt-get update failed.'
      $SUDO env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y "$tmp/$FILE" || fail "apt-get install of $FILE failed."
      ;;
    rpm)
      if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        $SUDO dnf install -y "$tmp/$FILE" || fail "dnf install of $FILE failed."
      else
        $SUDO yum install -y "$tmp/$FILE" || fail "yum install of $FILE failed."
      fi
      ;;
    pacman)
      $SUDO pacman -U --noconfirm "$tmp/$FILE" || fail "pacman -U of $FILE failed."
      ;;
    dmg)
      mnt=$(hdiutil attach -nobrowse -readonly "$tmp/$FILE" | tail -n 1 | cut -f3-) || fail "could not open $FILE."
      [ -d "$mnt/Devnet dVPN.app" ] || { hdiutil detach -quiet "$mnt" || true; fail "$FILE has no Devnet dVPN.app inside."; }
      if [ -d '/Applications/Devnet dVPN.app' ]; then
        say 'replacing the installed /Applications/Devnet dVPN.app'
        $SUDO rm -rf '/Applications/Devnet dVPN.app' || fail 'could not remove the old app.'
      fi
      $SUDO ditto "$mnt/Devnet dVPN.app" '/Applications/Devnet dVPN.app' || { hdiutil detach -quiet "$mnt" || true; fail 'copying the app to /Applications failed.'; }
      hdiutil detach -quiet "$mnt" || say 'could not detach the disk image (harmless).'
      PATH="$MAC_BIN:$PATH"
      ;;
  esac

  command -v devnet-dvpn >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'installed, but devnet-dvpn is not on PATH.'
  ver=$(devnet-dvpn version --json) || fail 'installed, but devnet-dvpn version failed.'
  printf '%s\n' "$ver" >&2
  # One line, whatever the CLI printed (JSON allows newlines between tokens, never inside strings).
  ver=$(printf '%s' "$ver" | tr -d '\n\r')
  case "$ver" in '{'*'}') ;; *) ver=null ;; esac

  # ─── what next: human lines on stderr, one JSON line on stdout ───
  pathline=null
  if [ "$KIND" = dmg ]; then
    say 'macOS: a script cannot change the PATH of the shell that started it. Run this in your shell first:'
    printf '  export PATH="%s:$PATH"\n' "$MAC_BIN" >&2
    pathline="\"export PATH=\\\"$MAC_BIN:\$PATH\\\"\""
  fi
  rc=0
  devnet-dvpn agent status --json >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 3 ]; then
    next="this release has no agent commands: follow section 2 of $GUIDE"
  else
    next='devnet-dvpn agent status --json'
  fi
  say "next: $next"
  printf '{"ok":true,"tag":"%s","file":"%s","version":%s,"path":%s,"next":"%s"}\n' \
    "$TAG" "$FILE" "$ver" "$pathline" "$next" >&3
}

main "$@"

# file: install.ps1

# --- install.ps1: install devnet-dvpn (Sentinel dVPN on Solana devnet) on Windows ---
#
# In an ELEVATED PowerShell (an elevated terminal, or SSH as an administrator):
#
#   irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet/main/install.ps1 | iex
#
# or, to read it first:
#
#   curl.exe -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet/main/install.ps1
#   Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass -Force; . .\install.ps1
#
# Both forms run in your own shell, so the PATH it sets stays set there.
#
# What it does: takes the newest release (pre-releases included) that has the x64 installer and
# is v0.3 or newer (the guide pins v0.3.0-rc6), downloads it and the release's SHA256SUMS, checks it, runs the silent
# install and waits for it, adds devnet-dvpn to this shell's PATH and runs `devnet-dvpn version --json`.
#
# Options: $env:DVPN_VERSION = 'v0.3.0-rc6'   use this release tag instead of the newest (AGENTS.md pins it)
#
# Output: progress on the host; one JSON line as output, on success
#   {"ok":true,"tag":...,"file":...,"version":{...},"path":"<bin folder added to PATH>","next":...}
# and on failure {"ok":false,"error":"<the sentence>"}, then it stops with an error (so a script
# calling it sees it failed); it never closes your shell. Windows PowerShell 5.1 and 7. ASCII only.

function Install-DevnetDvpn {
  $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
  $ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'   # 5.1 downloads are very slow with the progress bar
  [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol -bor [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12

  $repo = 'Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-windows'
  $guide = 'https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/agentic-privacy-solana-devnet/blob/main/AGENTS.md'
  $pattern = '^Devnet-dVPN-Setup-.*-x64\.exe$'

  function Stop-Install([string]$why) {
    Write-Output ([ordered]@{ ok = $false; error = $why } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)
    throw "install.ps1: $why"
  }
  function Test-Tag([string]$tag) {
    # v0.3 or newer: older releases cannot make a key file.
    $p = ($tag -replace '^v', '') -split '[.-]'
    if ($p.Count -lt 2) { return $false }
    $maj = 0; $min = 0
    if (-not [int]::TryParse($p[0], [ref]$maj) -or -not [int]::TryParse($p[1], [ref]$min)) { return $false }
    return ($maj -gt 0 -or $min -ge 3)
  }

  # --- elevated? ---
  $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
  if (-not (New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($id)).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)) {
    Stop-Install 'this shell is not elevated; open an elevated PowerShell (or SSH in as an administrator) and run this again.'
  }
  $arch = $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432
  if (-not $arch) { $arch = $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE }
  if ($arch -ne 'AMD64') { Stop-Install "this CPU ($arch) has no installer; only x64 is built (v0.3.0-rc6 included)." }

  $tmp = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ('dvpn-' + [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tmp | Out-Null
  try {
    # --- which release ---
    if ($env:DVPN_VERSION) {
      $tag = $env:DVPN_VERSION
      if ($tag -notmatch '^v') { $tag = "v$tag" }
      if (-not (Test-Tag $tag)) { Stop-Install "release $tag is older than v0.3 and cannot make a key file; use `$env:DVPN_VERSION = 'v0.3.0-rc6'." }
      $base = "https://github.com/$repo/releases/download/$tag"
      try { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "$base/SHA256SUMS" -OutFile "$tmp\SHA256SUMS" }
      catch { Stop-Install "release $tag has no SHA256SUMS (is the tag right? tags look like v0.3.0-rc6): $($_.Exception.Message)" }
      $file = Get-Content "$tmp\SHA256SUMS" | ForEach-Object { (($_ -split '\s+')[1]) -replace '^\*', '' } |
        Where-Object { $_ -match $pattern } | Select-Object -First 1
      if (-not $file) { Stop-Install "release $tag has no x64 installer." }
    } else {
      try { $releases = Invoke-RestMethod -UseBasicParsing -Uri "https://api.github.com/repos/$repo/releases?per_page=30" }
      catch { Stop-Install "could not read the release list from GitHub (rate limit or no network); set `$env:DVPN_VERSION = '<tag>' and run again: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
      # The API lists releases newest-CREATED first, and the first usable one wins: a release made
      # later on an older line would be picked over a newer version. Pin DVPN_VERSION to rule that out.
      $pick = $null
      foreach ($r in $releases) {
        if ($r.draft -or -not (Test-Tag $r.tag_name)) { continue }
        $a = $r.assets | Where-Object { $_.name -match $pattern } | Select-Object -First 1
        if ($a) { $pick = @{ tag = $r.tag_name; file = $a.name }; break }
      }
      if (-not $pick) { Stop-Install 'no release v0.3 or newer has an x64 installer.' }
      $tag = $pick.tag; $file = $pick.file
      $base = "https://github.com/$repo/releases/download/$tag"
      try { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "$base/SHA256SUMS" -OutFile "$tmp\SHA256SUMS" }
      catch { Stop-Install "release $tag has no SHA256SUMS; not installing an unchecked file." }
    }

    Write-Host "install.ps1: release $tag, file $file"
    try { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "$base/$file" -OutFile "$tmp\$file" }
    catch { Stop-Install "download of $file failed: $($_.Exception.Message)" }

    # --- check the file against SHA256SUMS ---
    $want = $null
    foreach ($line in Get-Content "$tmp\SHA256SUMS") {
      $f = $line -split '\s+'
      if ($f.Count -ge 2 -and (($f[1] -replace '^\*', '') -eq $file)) { $want = $f[0].ToLower(); break }
    }
    if (-not $want) { Stop-Install "SHA256SUMS of $tag has no line for $file; not installing an unchecked file." }
    $got = (Get-FileHash "$tmp\$file" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower()
    if ($got -ne $want) { Stop-Install "$file does not match SHA256SUMS; not installing it." }
    Write-Host 'install.ps1: checksum OK'

    # --- silent install; -Wait, or it returns before it has finished ---
    $p = Start-Process -FilePath "$tmp\$file" -ArgumentList '/S' -Wait -PassThru
    if ($p.ExitCode -eq 3) { Stop-Install 'the installer says this CPU is the wrong one (exit code 3).' }
    if ($p.ExitCode -ne 0) { Stop-Install "the installer failed (exit code $($p.ExitCode))." }
  } finally {
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $tmp -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  }

  # --- PATH for this shell (new shells get it from the installer) ---
  $bin = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'Devnet dVPN\bin'
  if (-not (($env:Path -split ';') -contains $bin)) { $env:Path += ";$bin" }
  if (-not (Get-Command devnet-dvpn -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Stop-Install "installed, but devnet-dvpn is not in $bin." }
  $ver = devnet-dvpn version --json
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Stop-Install 'installed, but devnet-dvpn version failed.' }
  Write-Host $ver
  $verObj = $null
  # A native command's lines arrive as an array; 5.1's ConvertFrom-Json needs them as one string.
  try { $verObj = ($ver -join "`n") | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { Write-Host "install.ps1: version output is not JSON ($($_.Exception.Message))" }

  # --- v0.3.0-rc2 only: daemon install fails on a machine not joined to a domain ---
  if ($tag -eq 'v0.3.0-rc2' -and $env:USERDOMAIN -eq 'WORKGROUP') {
    $env:USERDOMAIN = $env:COMPUTERNAME
    Write-Host 'install.ps1: v0.3.0-rc2 on a machine not in a domain: set $env:USERDOMAIN = $env:COMPUTERNAME in this shell, which daemon install needs. In a new shell, set it again before daemon install.'
  }

  devnet-dvpn agent status --json *> $null
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 3) {
    $next = "this release has no agent commands: follow section 2 of $guide"
  } else {
    $next = 'devnet-dvpn agent status --json'
  }
  Write-Host "install.ps1: next: $next"
  # The one line for a program to read (human lines above go to the host, not the output).
  Write-Output ([ordered]@{ ok = $true; tag = $tag; file = $file; version = $verObj; path = $bin; next = $next } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 5)
}

Install-DevnetDvpn

# file: CHANGELOG.md

# Changelog: the agent page and the `agent` answers

What changed for an agent between releases of `devnet-dvpn`, newest first. The page for the current
release is [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md); what an older release still needs is in
[`docs/OLDER-RELEASES.md`](docs/OLDER-RELEASES.md). Field by field: [`docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md`](docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md).
Terms: [`GLOSSARY.md`](GLOSSARY.md).

Check which release you have: `devnet-dvpn version --json`.

## v0.3.0-rc7

Breaking: read these before you run an rc6 script on rc7.

- **Market-sized default cap.** Without `--max-price`, the cap is the larger of the spending limit / 10 and
  the p75 price of the matching online nodes times `--units`, never above the spending limit (rc6: always
  the spending limit / 10). With fewer than 3 priced nodes the fixed cap applies.
- **Spending limit 50 → 150 tDVPN** on a new install. An existing install keeps its stored limit; `defaults.spendingLimitRecommended` shows the market's suggestion; `settings set allowanceTdvpn=<n>` takes effect at the next raise (`--raise-limit`, or `device setup --allowance <n> --yes`).
- **`not-funded` text** names the exact shortfall plus "(X recommended: it also covers a reconnect)".
- **Exit `4` for `keyfile-missing` and `keyfile-mode`** (rc6: exit `1`).
- **`no-nodes` under `--max-price`** names the cheapest matching price, and its `action` is a runnable
  `agent up … --max-price <that price> --yes` line (rc6: "widen the filters").

Added, not breaking:

- `defaults` on every `agent up` preview and answer: `priceCap`, `priceCapBase`, `spendingLimit`,
  `spendingLimitRecommended`, `units`, `source` (`market` or `fixed`), `reason`, `market` (`p50`, `p75`,
  `nodes`, `outliers`).
- The `--raise-limit` action is your line pinned to the node `agent up` picked, keeping your
  `--protocol` and `--max-price` (E-88).
- A session reconnecting under the kill switch reads `connected: false`, `reconnecting` and `blocked: true`,
  and `next` is `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network` (E-87).
- Every failure carries `next` (the same as `action`, which stays).
- `rpc-unavailable`, `rpc-ws`, `rpc-network`, `rpc-quota`: `next` is the `daemon set --rpc <https url> --yes` line.
- `agent status` with the internet blocked and no session: `next` = `agent up --yes`, `alsoNext` = `daemon restore-network`.
- `agent status` names the preview (`agent up`, no `--yes`) when the device has no spending permission or under
  1 tDVPN is held in all.
- `agent down` adds `deposited` and `depositedBase`.
- A runnable `next` on success for the step commands (`wallet`, `device`, `settle`, `disconnect`, `daemon install`);
  `settle run` adds `nextAfter` (Unix seconds). A failed `wallet` / `device` / `settle` says "Nothing was sent or
  signed." when nothing was, not the deposit words.

## v0.3.0-rc6 (Windows, Linux; macOS stays v0.3.0-rc4)

Breaking: read these before you run an rc5 script on rc6.

- **Exit codes 4, 5, 6.** A failure no longer always exits `1`: `4` = needs you or your operator
  (`not-funded`, `spending-limit`, `price-cap`, `no-wallet`; nothing was paid), `5` = refused for safety
  (`kill-switch`, `kill-switch-held`, `kill-switch-failed`), `6` = network or RPC with no deposit open
  (`rpc-busy`, `rpc-unavailable`, `rpc-ws`). Other failures still exit `1`. The JSON line is the same.
- **`--raise-limit`.** `agent up` no longer raises this computer's spending limit by itself. A deposit
  above it is refused with `spending-limit` (nothing paid); `action` is an `agent up … --raise-limit --yes`
  line (read its node and units first). `limitRaised` / `limitNote` appear only when you passed it.
- **Default price cap (`price-cap`).** Without `--max-price`, a deposit above the spending limit / 10
  (5 tDVPN by default) is refused (nothing paid); `action` names the node's price with `--max-price`.
- **Version fields.** `version --json` adds `programId` and `mint`. On devnet they must read
  `J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs` and `Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa`; any
  other value is the wrong build: pay nothing.

Added, not breaking:

- Base-unit twins of every amount, as strings: `solLamports`, `tdvpnBase`, `heldBase`, `spentBase`,
  `refundableBase`, `deposit.tdvpnBase` (`deposit.baseUnits` stays, the older name).
- A connect that fails with no known cause names it: `node-refused` (a deposit was paid; `agent down --yes`
  closes it) or `unknown` ("Nothing was paid"). rc5 could say only "Something went wrong. Retry." (E-71).
- With the node stopped and the kill switch holding the block, `next` is one runnable command,
  `devnet-dvpn daemon restore-network`, and `alsoNext` names the reconnect or the close (E-86).

## v0.3.0-rc5

Breaking from rc4:

- **`refundable` → `held`** in `agent status`: the tDVPN held for your wallet in the program (what
  `settle withdraw` moves). `refundable` now appears only in `agent down`, where it means the tDVPN still
  to come back from closing deposits.
- **`serverStopped` → `nodeStopped`** in `agent status` (code `server-stopped` is unchanged).

Added:

- `agent up --yes` says when it raised the spending limit: `limitRaised` (`from`, `to`) and `limitNote`
  (the command that lowers it). rc4 could raise it silently (E-73).
- With the VPN service down and a deposit open, `agent status` names the service fix first (E-75).
- `agent down` reports deposits another device of this wallet opened: `notClosed` and `warning` (E-72).
- With the node stopped and the kill switch holding the block, `next` names
  `daemon restore-network` first (E-82).

## v0.3.0-rc4

The first release with `agent status`, `agent up` and `agent down`. Earlier releases (rc2) have only the
single commands: [`docs/OLDER-RELEASES.md`](docs/OLDER-RELEASES.md), "Step by step".

# file: docs/PROVENANCE.md

# Provenance: where every file an agent runs comes from

Every program and script this repository asks an agent to run, with how to check it. You always have a
choice: **download and verify** the published file, or (Path B only) **build it from source** and get
the same bytes. Terms: [`GLOSSARY.md`](../GLOSSARY.md).

How to verify a download: fetch the release's `SHA256SUMS` from the same release page, then
`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing` (Linux), `shasum -a 256 <file>` (macOS) or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` (Windows) and compare. The installers (`install.sh`,
`install.ps1`, `direct/install.sh`) do this for you and stop on a mismatch.

## Path A: the Devnet dVPN app (download only)

**The app's source code is not public.** You can check that the file you have is the one released (the
hashes below come from each release's `SHA256SUMS`), but you cannot rebuild it. What you can check after
install is which chain program and token it pays: see "Program and mint" below.

| File | SHA-256 | Release | Source @ commit | Build command | Toolchain | Reproducible? | Last verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Devnet-dVPN-Setup-0.3.0-rc.7-x64.exe` (Windows x64) | `7b5c875eac381b19f5e7a1f5d964c46cfab99f601b28c38ace8178e59517237c` | [v0.3.0-rc7](https://github.com/Sentinel-Bluebuilder/sentinel-solana-dvpn-windows/releases/tag/v0.3.0-rc7) | not public | not public | Electron (not published) | no | 2026-11-20: hash matches `SHA256SUMS` (rc7) |
